It introduces MARCH (Memory-Anchor Routing across Context History), maintaining structured memory states with selective retrieval to support memory routing and state evolution over long-horizon tasks.

entry.title: Knowledge Distillation During Mid-Training Favors Reasoning over Factual Recall

author.name: Jacqueline He, Howard Yen, Shuyue Stella Li, Margaret Li, Hanqing Zeng, Yinglong Xia, Benyu Zhang, Zhuokai Zhao, Qiang Zhang, Pang Wei Koh, Luke Zettlemoyer, Wen-tau Yih

entry.summary: Controlled experiments from a strong team including Zettlemoyer, Yih, and Koh show forward-KL distillation with post-trained teachers helps both reasoning and factual recall during pretraining but slows factual recall acquisition during mid-training while preserving reasoning gains, tracing the stage-dependent effect.

entry.title: Polished but Unresolved: Identifying Late-Stage Pressure States in Long-Horizon Tool-Use Agents

author.name: Haoyang Chen, Yi Liu, Jianzhi Shao, Xiaozhou Xu, Zhe Sun, Wei Hu

entry.summary: This paper identifies late-stage pressure states in long-horizon tool-use agents, where agents submit polished but incomplete answers while key constraints remain unresolved. A linear probe detects the pressure state from hidden states, and activation interventions causally shift whether agents continue tool use or finalize early. Constraint clarity and action mapping mitigate the pressure, informing a mitigation method.

entry.title: Faster Than Flash: Exploiting Attention Sparsity for Efficient Long-Context Decoding

author.name: Zhigeng Liu, Zhiyuan Ning, Ruixiao Li, Xiaoran Liu, Yuerong Song, Min Zhang, Ziwei He, Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: Faster Flash Decoding (FFD) is a hardware-algorithm co-design framework that fuses sparse attention selection and computation into a single kernel, using low-bit content-aware scanning instead of external metadata indices. Its top-delta strategy dynamically filters attention blocks to break the memory bandwidth wall in long-context decoding. This is a substantive efficiency contribution for serving long-context LLMs.

entry.title: SMELT: Scaling Laws for Compute-Matched MoE Looped Transformers

author.name: Shaowen Wang, Ge Zhang, Kairong Luo, Yuhao Wu, Shaofan Liu, Jiaheng Liu, Wenhao Huang, Shen Yan, Jian Li

entry.summary: SMELT studies looped transformers on Mixture-of-Experts architectures under compute-matched budgets (per-token FLOPs, parameters, KV cache), finding that looping the middle half of layers twice yields loss curves that drop faster with compute, saving 6.8-18.0% of training compute. Scaling laws are fit across four sizes up to 54B non-embedding parameters.

entry.title: AgentProv: Auditing Agentic LLM API Providers via Tool-use Policy Probes

author.name: Xun Wang, Bihe Zhao, Michael Backes, Franziska Boenisch, Adam Dziedzic

entry.summary: Presents AgentProv, a method for auditing commercial LLM API providers to detect silent backbone substitution, quantization, or wrapping. It observes that text-output-channel audits are structurally fragile for agentic APIs because serving stacks discard text on tool calls, and proposes tool-use policy probes as a new audit channel exploiting internalized tool-use behaviors. This addresses accountability for major providers like OpenAI, Anthropic, and Google.

entry.title: A Unified Mechanistic Analysis of Knowledge- and Safety-Based Refusals

author.name: Yuri Son, Seunghee Kim, Hyuhng Joon Kim, Taeuk Kim

entry.summary: Provides the first unified mechanistic study of knowledge-based and safety-based refusals using a new dataset of 213 contrastive quadruples. It finds overlapping but asymmetric mechanisms sharing a refusal direction, with safety signals transferring to knowledge refusal more than the reverse, and type specialization in upper layers.

entry.title: Context-Grounding Gains Are Mediated by Pre-existing Machinery: Auditing GRPO, SFT, and DPO

author.name: Prakhar Gupta, Vaibhav Gupta

entry.summary: Audits nine post-training arms across GRPO, SFT, and DPO to test whether gains in following conflicting prompt evidence require new machinery or strengthen pre-existing machinery estimated from the starting checkpoint. It finds GRPO grounding gains are small and bounded below the conflict-SFT gain, while DPO drives larger changes.

entry.title: MemoryWalker: Stop Training Agents on Contexts They Never Saw

author.name: Zinco J, Xunjie Zhu, Shen Huang, Zhenyi Wang, Pengjun Xie, Jieping Ye

entry.summary: MemoryWalker tackles the conditioning problem that arises when training agents under production-style context compression: every eviction branches the effective history into a tree, so naive linearizations cause time-travel leakage or train-inference mismatch. It introduces two exact, gradient-equivalent corrections (LogitTree segmented K-forward traversal and a packed 4D attention mask) plus a single-backward-pass self-distillation approximation (SDCC).

entry.title: Subliminal Learning as Trait-Direction Drift: A Mechanism and Targeted Control under SFT Distillation

author.name: Zhixuan Liu, Zhichen Dong, Yuyu Fan, Xiangtian Li, Chao Yang

entry.summary: Proposes and validates trait-direction drift as a mechanism for subliminal learning in distillation: biased teacher generation creates measurable preference gaps in training data, and student-recognizable gaps induce trait-aligned updates during SFT. The mechanism enables targeted control and mitigation of hidden trait transfer through distillation.

entry.title: ZimaBlue: Evolving Generalizable World Action Models through Scalable Video Pre-training

author.name: Xionghao Wu, Yijun Yang, Shiyang Zhou, Haoze Sun, Jianhui Liu, Songsong Yu, Jiyao Zhang, Wenbo Li, Bo Wang, Guoqing Ma, Lin Song, Renjie Liao, Shenghe Zheng, Wei Tang, Xiaojuan Qi, Yanwei Li, Yuan Zhang, Zhuotao Tian, Haoyang Huang, Nan Duan

entry.summary: ZimaBlue learns generalizable World Action Models from large-scale egocentric video via a three-stage curriculum: causal embodied video pretraining, then conversion of action-free video experience into robot control, addressing the action-label bottleneck in manipulation.

entry.title: Commit-first LLM judging inherits the judge's own errors

author.name: Idil Gozel

entry.summary: This audit examines commit-first LLM judging, where a judge solves a task before scoring candidates, finding that none of 24 configurations across eight widely used evaluation frameworks implement it. Nine frameworks use an ineffective variant, traceable to a shared ancestor prompt copied via a typographical error. It highlights a systemic flaw in how LLM-as-judge pipelines are built and how errors propagate through prompt genealogy.

entry.title: Scaling Near-Optimal SFT-RL Annotation Budget Allocation from Small to Large LLMs

author.name: Jingtan Wang, Arun Verma, Xiaoqiang Lin, Zhengyuan Liu, Nancy F. Chen, Daniela Rus, Bryan Kian Hsiang Low

entry.summary: Studies how to split a fixed annotation budget between supervised fine-tuning and reinforcement learning during LLM post-training, introducing a near-optimality framework that characterizes the set of allocations within tolerance of peak performance. The key empirical finding is that the near-optimal region is wide, widens with scale, and transfers from small proxy models to large target models.

entry.title: SCoNE: Selective Context-aware Neuron Editing for Robust Retrieval-Augmented Generation

author.name: Chaewon Kim, Seo Yeon Park

entry.summary: SCoNE is a training-free model editing method that strengthens context-aware FFN neurons, identified via attribution and cross-input variability, to make RAG systems robust to noisy retrieved documents. It requires few mining samples and no inference overhead while outperforming baselines on knowledge-intensive QA.

entry.title: LLMPEDIA: Browsing, Verifying, and Comparing the Parametric Encyclopedic Knowledge of LLMs

author.name: Muhammed Saeed, Simon Razniewski

entry.summary: LLMPEDIA recursively materializes roughly 1.3M articles from the parametric memory of GPT-5-mini, DeepSeek-V3.2, and Llama-3.3-70B without retrieval, then audits sampled atomic claims, finding a 68.4 percent true rate, over 21 points below MMLU scores, with 30.5 percent of claims insufficient to verify.

entry.title: Uncovering Understanding-Generation Synergy in Native Unified Multimodal Models: From Representation, Task to System

author.name: Penghao Wu, Haiwen Diao, Weichen Fan, Lewei Lu, Dahua Lin, Ziwei Liu

entry.summary: Investigates understanding-generation synergy in natively unified multimodal models at representation, task, and system levels in a controlled setting without pretrained vision priors, finding mutual benefit at representation level but competition when objectives share a computation path, informing unified model architecture design.

entry.title: WHALE: A Simple Recipe for Joint Harness-Weight Optimization

author.name: Haechan Kim, Yoonho Lee, Gisang Lee, Chelsea Finn, Kangwook Lee

entry.summary: WHALE proposes alternating optimization of model weights and the executable harness code that manages agent context and control flow, instantiated via online rejection-sampling fine-tuning and harness search. The key insight is that optimizing either component in isolation bottlenecks the other. With Chelsea Finn among the authors, this is a credible step toward co-trained agent systems.

entry.title: SoK: When Safe Agents Fail Together: The Security of Multi Agent LLM Systems

author.name: Rui Yang, Junjie Xu, Zhengyu Liu, Neil Fendley, Yang Hong, Ziyang Li, Yinzhi Cao

entry.summary: This SoK systematizes multi-agent LLM security through an execution-centered analysis of 197 works, organizing attacks by adversary position, interaction interface, and system-level risk via an A-I-R framework, covering six interfaces and eight recurring attack paths. It warns that multi-agent settings can masquerade as security effects without an execution-level view. A much-needed systematization in a fast-moving area.

entry.title: Group Adaptive Clipping Policy Optimization

author.name: Sheng Jia, Xiao Wang, Shiva Prasad Kasiviswanathan, Rein Houthooft

entry.summary: Identifies that GRPO-style RLVR uses a fixed importance-ratio clipping boundary that disproportionately suppresses rare correct rollouts on hard problems, which carry the strongest exploration signal. GAPO adapts the clipping boundary per rollout group as a plug-in modification, improving learning on harder tasks.

entry.title: Post-Training Science for Supervised Fine-Tuning

author.name: Charles O'Neill, Mudith Jayasekara, Harry Partridge

entry.summary: A systematic one-lever-at-a-time sweep of SFT decisions (learning rate, batch size, LoRA versus full fine-tuning, epochs, optimizer, data) across dense and MoE models in Qwen3 and Llama families on four real-world customer SFT datasets with built-in evaluations. It turns per-run folk knowledge about SFT hyperparameters into measured, transferable guidance.

entry.title: Validity-Aware Jailbreak Evaluation for Large Language Models

author.name: Qilong Wu, Sahil Wadhwa, Pranab Mohanty, Giri Iyengar, Varun Chandrasekaran

entry.summary: This work cleanly isolates long-horizon state tracking in LLMs by requiring a model to compute an MD5 hash through a deep sequence of dependent tool calls, removing confounds from instruction interpretation. It shows that excellent per-step accuracy decays catastrophically end-to-end and that existing agentic benchmarks cannot attribute failures. A sharp diagnostic for a core agentic limitation.

entry.title: Probabilistic Model Checking of Autoregressive Neural Sequence Models

author.name: Helge Spieker, Dennis Gross, Arnaud Gotlieb

entry.summary: Introduces a pipeline that extracts a discrete-time Markov chain from an autoregressive neural sequence model's generation process and verifies PCTL specifications with PRISM, yielding certified intervals on constraint-violation probability and input coverage. This brings formal probabilistic verification to neural sequence models where test-set accuracy is silent.

entry.title: H3-World: Turning Language Understanding into World Control

author.name: Danze Chen, Zeqing Wang, Ziyue Lin, Xingyi Yang, Yeying Jin

entry.summary: H3-World converts the existing 33B MiniMax-H3 video generator into an interactive world model, using structured character and camera language instructions aligned to temporal video latents for precise, temporally grounded control without dedicated action modules. It demonstrates that language is emerging as a natural control interface for large video generators, relevant to simulation and embodied AI research.

entry.title: Patterning in Practice: Debiasing Reward Models with Susceptibilities

author.name: George Wang, Elizabeth Donoway, Daniel Murfet

entry.summary: Uses patterning, reweighting preference pairs by their measured susceptibility to benchmark losses, to debias a Gemma 2 9B reward model trained on Skywork-Reward-Preference. It gains +14.2 points on RM-Bench Hard where style cues conflict with correctness while preserving overall accuracy, matching or beating the strongest comparable published method, with interpretable reweightings.

entry.title: Can Large Language Models Forecast What Researchers Study Next?

author.name: Fenghai Li, Zihan Tang, Haofei Yu, Yining Zhao, Jiaxuan You

entry.summary: Introduces IdeaForecastBench, a benchmark testing whether LLM-generated research ideas anticipate actual future papers, using 624 rolling episodes across 52 topics with a retrieve-then-judge protocol. It compares history-compression strategies across several model families and proposes a Mode-Decomposition Forecaster.

entry.title: A Lagrangian View of Flow Matching

author.name: Peyman Milanfar

entry.summary: Peyman Milanfar (Google) presents a Lagrangian, particle-centric derivation of flow matching and rectified flow, deriving a conservation-of-target-identity invariance condition for optimal single-step generation and a governing quasi-linear advection PDE.

entry.title: CMRVision: A Foundation Model for Cardiac MR Image Analysis

author.name: Athira J. Jacob, Puneet Sharma, Daniel Rueckert

entry.summary: CMRVision is a cardiac MR foundation model pretrained with DINOv3-style self-supervised learning on 36 million multi-center, multi-sequence CMR images, systematically ablated on multi-task segmentation and view classification, showing domain-specific pretraining benefits.

entry.title: Beyond the Clock: Measuring the Value of Adaptive Revision

author.name: Ayushi Chadha

entry.summary: This paper studies meta-level control in hierarchical latent reasoners: when should a manager revise or preserve a commitment governing lower-level computation? Across three seeds, learned revision timing yields qualitatively different policies, yet none beats the best fixed timing policy, separating state dependence from decision value. The finding is a caution about adaptive revision mechanisms in compound agentic systems.

entry.title: Membership Inference in Fine-tuned Diffusion Language Models via Token-level Memorization Asymmetry

author.name: Shengfang Zhai, Leo Marchyok, Yuling Shi, Huanran Chen, Yinpeng Dong, Jiaheng Zhang, Sanghyun Hong

entry.summary: Identifies token-level memorization asymmetry in diffusion language models through theoretical analysis of diffusion training dynamics, and proposes Q-Skew, a quantile-weighted skewness indicator for membership inference on fine-tuned diffusion LMs that outperforms baselines.

entry.title: Towards Generalizable Visually Grounded Exploration of Household Devices

author.name: Linhao Zheng, Zeming Liu, Wangke Chen, Li Zeng, Wanxiang Che, Heyan Huang, Yuhang Guo

entry.summary: This paper targets generalizable visually grounded exploration, where embodied agents operate novel household devices without manuals or training trajectories by grounding world knowledge into visual affordances. It argues existing benchmarks fail to test this capability and proposes a new evaluation setting. The work addresses a key bottleneck for autonomous embodied agents.

entry.title: Verifiable Disaster Storylines and Causal Knowledge Graphs: A Citation-Grounded Pipeline from Heterogeneous Humanitarian Sources

author.name: Ivan Decostanzi, Michele Ronco, Sergio Consoli, Christina Corbane, Lorenzo Bertolini, Indaco Biazzo, Daria Mihaila, Manuel Garcia-Herranz, Felix Schwebel, Yelena Mejova, Kyriaki Kalimeri

entry.summary: The authors build a RAG pipeline combining EM-DAT disaster records with ReliefWeb and European Media Monitor documents to produce citation-grounded disaster storylines and causal knowledge graphs for humanitarian responders. Each extracted storyline field and causal edge is grounded in sources, covering 17 fields including child-sensitive impact indicators. It targets the critical early-hours information synthesis bottleneck in crisis response.

entry.title: Delegation Without Trust: An Empirical Gap Analysis of Identity, Authorization, and Runtime Governance in Multi-Agent LLM Systems

author.name: Panduranga Sai Varma Dantuluri, Jyotirmoy Sundi

entry.summary: The paper argues that multi-agent LLM security must be evaluated under an untrusted-model assumption: even a fully prompt-injected agent should not exceed explicitly delegated authority. It contributes a threat model with four adversaries, a gap analysis of identity, authorization, and runtime governance, and evaluations showing current stacks fall short. This is a foundational framing for agent authorization.

entry.title: Benchmarking Vision-Language Models for Automated Pathology Diagnosis and Report Generation

author.name: Yumi Lee, Harim Oh, Hyoryung Kim, Minji Kim, Eunsu Kim, Hyeseong Lee, Junya Fukuoka, Andrey Bychkov, Jijgee Munkhdelger, Rajiv Kumar Kaushal, Ayushi Sahay, Rajni Yadav, Bharathi Prabakaran, Sulen Sarioglu, Serdar Balc{\i}, Ilknur Turkmen, Yuri Tolkach, Christian Harder, Julian Westerdorf, Reinhard Buettner, Audun Ljone Henriksen, Sepp De Raedt, Byung Hyun Lee, Sungjin Lim, Joohoon Lee, Gwanghyun Kim, Se Young Chun, Suryakant Singh, Saarthak Kapse, Prateek Prasanna, Kyung A Kim, Yousun Kang, Sehwan Yoo, Sungman Hong, Shubham Innani, Michael Feldman, Spyridon Bakas, Ujjwal Baid, Prasad Dutande, Suhas Gajare, Bhakti Baheti, Serkan S\"okmen, Ece Tu\u{g}ba Cebeci, Ahmet Hal{\i}c{\i}, Musa Balc{\i}, Kardelen Pe\c{c}enek, Srividhya Sainath, Kyongseok Jang, Messi H. J. Lee, Noorul Wahab, Bodong Du, Jiaming Zhang, Qixiang Zhang, Jang-Hwan Choi, Sangjeong Ahn

entry.summary: Introduces a clinically curated Pan-Asia whole-slide-image to report dataset of roughly 10,500 pairs from five institutions and the REG 2025 benchmark from a MICCAI challenge, analyzing methods spanning VLMs, MIL frameworks, and retrieval-augmented generation for pathology report generation. It addresses the data scarcity bottleneck for WSI-based report generation.

entry.title: Lagged Coupling: Internal Representations Become Readable Before They Become Causal

author.name: Xining Xun

entry.summary: Across the full Pythia suite, shows that linear probes can read target variables from the residual stream very early while steering along the same direction remains null-equivalent in most model-checkpoint cells, a phenomenon called lagged coupling that does not shrink with scale. It decomposes into saturated internal readability, gradual behavioral readability, and near-absent causal efficacy.

entry.title: Context Window Failures in Relational Foundation Models

author.name: Denis Oliveira Correa, Francisco Galuppo Azevedo

entry.summary: Introduces Animus, a synthetic financial dataset where predicting customer income requires aggregating tens of thousands of transactions, exposing context-window truncation failures in relational foundation models. Three recent architectures achieve R2 of at most 0.18 on the raw representation, while a simple temporal pre-aggregation recovers up to 0.65.

entry.title: Text Capability Loss in Vision-Language Adaptation: An Attention-Sink Diagnosis

author.name: Minsik Choi, Geewook Kim, Young Geun Kim

entry.summary: Traces text capability loss when fine-tuning an LLM into a vision-language model to attention-sink corruption: VL fine-tuning perturbs the early sink position that anchors much of the attention probability mass. It introduces Sink Strength, a scalar computable in seconds on a single GPU, that predicts post-adaptation degradation of strict-grader capabilities.

entry.title: When Metropolis and Hastings Meet Bradley and Terry: Exact MCMC From Preference Voting

author.name: Ariel Smogorghevski, Nir Rosenfeld, Yaniv Romano

entry.summary: Pref-MH is an exact Metropolis-Hastings sampler for distributions conditioned on semantic properties, using only stochastic binary pairwise comparisons from humans or model judges. The key insight is that the MH unnormalized density ratio matches Bradley-Terry preference odds, enabling conditional sampling without pointwise density evaluations.

entry.title: From Base Rollouts to RL Reasoning: A Budgeted Search Perspective

author.name: Wenhe Sun, Cunxiang Wang, Zijun Yao, Yixin Cao

entry.summary: Uses a Unified Decoding Framework to study behaviorally whether RL with verifiable rewards creates new reasoning or shifts rollout distributions toward trajectories base models can already reach, comparing Base and RL checkpoints from SimpleRL-Zoo under shared decoding budgets.

entry.title: Qwen-Drive-1.0: An Initial Step towards a Vision-Language Foundation Model for Autonomous Driving

author.name: Xin Zhou, Zongchuang Zhao, Zhibo Yang, Mingsheng Li, Humen Zhong, Shuai Bai, Du Chu, Ruizhe Chen, Zhaohai Li, Jun Tang, Qiuyue Wang, Mingkun Yang, Jiazhao Zhang, Dayiheng Liu, Dingkang Liang, Xiang Bai

entry.summary: Qwen-Drive-1.0 from the Qwen team integrates 3D perception, VQA, and motion planning in a VLM for autonomous driving, using an external BEV perception head as an inspectable interface and a Planning Expert conditioned on shared VLM representations.

entry.title: Physically Plausible Video Generation via Visual-Semantic Chain-of-Events Conditioning

author.name: Zixuan Wang, Yixin Hu, Wen Li, Feng Chen, Yan Liu, Duo Peng, Yinjie Lei

entry.summary: Reframes physically plausible video generation as event-centric generation, decomposing physical phenomena into causally connected events represented via evolving scene graphs rather than holistic chain-of-thought prompts. Introduces a chain-of-events conditioning framework with physics-driven reasoning modules.

entry.title: On-the-Fly3R: Towards Robust Online 3D Reconstruction with Feed-Forward 3R Models for Large-Scale UAV Scenarios

author.name: Zhe Shen, Liyuan Lou, Yifei Yu, Guanbo Wang, Quanjian Ji, Xin Wang, Zongqian Zhan

entry.summary: RadMatch is an auditable radiology report evaluation metric that decomposes report comparison into finding-level matching with significance-aware scoring and error characterization across seven clinical attributes, replacing opaque single-score LLM metrics with an interpretable actionable-error count.

entry.title: EvoFlint: An Evolutionary Atlas of Multi-Turn LLM Vulnerabilities

author.name: Feitong Qiao, Liren Peng, Shiming Ren, Aishwarya Jadhav, Arghavan Bahadorinejad, Marinette Chen, Muhan Zhang, Abdulaziz Suria, Gennevi Lu, Anish Das Sarma

entry.summary: The paper traces safety alignment in diffusion language models across denoising steps and token positions, finding refusal signals concentrate in early steps and leading positions, and that early committed tokens strongly shape final safety outcomes. This is timely given the rise of dLLMs as an alternative generation paradigm. A first substantive look at dLLM-specific alignment structure.

entry.title: Why Multi-Layer Message Passing Works: Completeness Theory for Graph Neural Network Interatomic Potentials

author.name: Pingbing Ming, Han Wang

entry.summary: Proves that the Hypergraph Neural Network with 3-body message passing is a universal approximator for potential energy surfaces and establishes a multi-layer completeness theory: L layers on sparse cutoff graphs match full L-hop neighborhoods under genericity, overlap, and connectivity conditions. This gives the first rigorous justification for the truncated-cutoff multi-layer design used in essentially all practical ML interatomic potentials.

entry.title: HarnessDev: Can LLMs Create and Evolve Their Own Agent Harness?

author.name: Yuhao Wu, Jingyuan Zhang, Jiajun Shi, Xinping Lei, Qingshui Gu, Yuxuan Zhang, Zexuan Wang, Chen He, Chen Huang, Maojia Song, Zhiyuan Zeng, Shaowen Wang, Jinkai Liu, Yunfeng Shi, Jiaheng Liu, Shen Yan, Wenhao Huang, Ge Zhang, Wenxuan Zhang

entry.summary: HarnessDev shifts agent evaluation from task outputs to runnable infrastructure: agents must create a complete execution harness from a minimal seed and then evolve it, measuring a capability (harness development) that standard evaluations ignore.

entry.title: OpenAgentFlow: Enabling System-Wide Safety Boundaries for Heterogeneous AI Agent Fleets

author.name: Dongsheng Chen, Xiangyu Zhao, Xin Yao, Xuetao Wei

entry.summary: OpenAgentFlow proposes a control-plane/action-plane architecture that establishes the action-commit boundary as a shared enforcement interface for safety policies across heterogeneous agent fleets. It treats safety as a system-level action-governance problem spanning GUI, API, tool, and LLM-generated actions. Addresses a real gap as agents compose into multi-system deployments.

entry.title: Recursive Criticality of AI Self-Improvement

author.name: Mikhail Burtsev

entry.summary: Burtsev models the conditions under which AI used in AI R&D becomes self-amplifying, deriving a recursive reproduction number R_AI that compares feedback strength against rising research difficulty. When R_AI exceeds 1, improvements compound across development cycles, defining a criticality threshold for recursive self-improvement. Provides a simple formal lens on a key AI forecasting and governance question.

entry.title: AnalysisBank: An Expert Analysis Pattern Library for Financial Report Generation

author.name: Yajing Yang, Yunshan Ma, Kelvin J. L. Koa, Min-Yen Kan

entry.summary: AnalysisBank distills 550 expert financial reports into a reusable library of analytical moves pairing data signals with expert text spans, then composes reports by retrieving and applying these moves at inference time. It identifies 47-52 signal types across 13 move types and improves novelty of generated financial reports across four LLM backbones. This matters because it shifts financial report generation from section templates to data-grounded analytical composition.

entry.title: The Interlingua Hypothesis: LLMs Translate via a Latent Task-agnostic Feature Space

author.name: Jacob Brinton, Jannik Brinkmann, Mark Crovella, Aaron Mueller

entry.summary: The paper proposes the interlingua hypothesis, that LLMs translate by encoding source sentences into a latent task-agnostic feature space and decoding targets from it, supported by three evidence lines including predictability of BLEU variance across language pairs. It connects translation behavior to recent multilingual interpretability findings. A strong interpretability contribution.

entry.title: Beyond the Image Plane: World-Grounded Queries for Multi-Object Tracking

author.name: Orcun Cetintas, Guillem Bras\'o, Tim Meinhardt, Laura Leal-Taix\'e

entry.summary: Introduces PLANET, an end-to-end multi-object tracker that lifts 2D tracking datasets into 3D and embeds reconstructed world geometry into query formation and positional encodings, moving beyond image-plane ambiguity. An auxiliary 3D location prediction task encourages world-grounded queries.

entry.title: Autonomous discovery of new structure-plausibility laws for explainable and rapid crystal diagnosis and screening

author.name: Zhilong Song, Lixue Cheng

entry.summary: Uses tool-using agents to generate, test, and actively refute two million candidate structure-plausibility laws, yielding eight Plausibility Rules for Inorganic Structures that encode five physicochemical mechanisms. Experimental structures satisfy the rules at 82 to 99 percent, versus Pauling's rules at 2 to 5 in many cases.

entry.title: Foundation models for electricity price forecasting and battery arbitrage: Can they replace market-specific forecasting models?

author.name: Arkadiusz Lipiecki, Rafa{\l} Weron

entry.summary: Evaluates nine zero-shot foundation forecasting model variants from five families against specialized electricity price forecasting benchmarks in Germany, Poland, and Spain, including economic value in battery arbitrage. Only TabPFN variants consistently beat the benchmarks statistically, and even then the advantage does not directly translate into higher arbitrage profits.

entry.title: Scaled Idempotence in Transformer Attention: Paired OV Geometry and Shared-Value Algebras

author.name: Jiming Feng, Junliang Li

entry.summary: Identifies a recurrent algebraic regularity in transformer attention: a sparse subset of effective OV operators nearly closes under composition. Across nine MHA/GQA models spanning 2.8B-235B parameters, several percent of heads show strong squared-closure alignment, and an exact factorization plus orientation-scrambling experiments tie the effect to K-orientation geometry rather than singular values or norms.

entry.title: CopyShield: A Cross-Level Benchmark of Copyright Defenses in LLMs

author.name: Maryam Alshehyari, Dushyant Singh Chauhan, Samuele Poppi, Martin Takac, Salem Lahlou, Nils Lukas

entry.summary: CopyShield is a controlled benchmark comparing three copyright defenses for LLMs at distinct intervention levels (contrastive decoding at output, DPO at behavior, activation intervention at representation) on LLaMA-3.1-8B and Mistral-7B, measuring literal leakage, calibrated non-literal leakage, utility, and degeneracy. It finds intervention level is associated with distinct compliance-utility trade-offs.

entry.title: Pre-carved Niches: The Formation Dynamics of Modular Task Partitions in Early LLM Training

author.name: Guangqi Li, Yongxin Li

entry.summary: Tracks how modular task partitions form during LLM training by training Pythia-410M from scratch and running attribution patching at every step, alongside gradient-norm probes and loss decompositions across 14 tasks in four cognitive domains. A key finding is that the modular map is pre-carved: dominant task overlap exists before any learning at roughly 3.6x a task-independent baseline.

entry.title: Position: Privacy Is a Claim, Not a Property of Synthetic Data

author.name: Jiachen Zhao, Antonia Januszewicz, Taeho Jung

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that privacy claims about synthetic data have quietly shifted from explicit residual-risk claims under stated assumptions to appearance-based properties inferred from the generation process. Empirical analysis of recent publications across major ML venues shows synthetic data is frequently used in privacy-sensitive settings without articulated threat models or falsifiable privacy criteria.

entry.title: NashDreamer: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning for Zero-Sum Imperfect-Information Games

author.name: Tom\'a\v{s} Hole\v{c}ek, Viliam Lis\'y

entry.summary: Proposes NashDreamer, a model-based reinforcement learning framework for two-player zero-sum imperfect-information games, built on a centralized multi-agent recurrent state-space model that decouples environment dynamics from player strategies. The paper argues centralized model learning is a mathematical necessity in multi-agent settings due to identifiability barriers. This extends MBRL, which has largely succeeded in single-agent domains, into a challenging competitive setting.

entry.title: VerTox: Verifiable Reward-Guided Corpus Poisoning Against Neural Ranking Models

author.name: Zhiqi Huang, Vivek Datla, Zhichao Xu, Puxuan Yu, Vivek Srikumar, Alfy Samuel

entry.summary: VerTox is the first framework to formulate corpus poisoning of neural ranking models as a verifiable reward-guided RL problem, using LLMs to craft small numbers of malicious documents that distort RAG-relevant retrieval behavior.

entry.title: When Tokenization is Secretly Output Supervision

author.name: Tanja Baeumel, Josef van Genabith, Simon Ostermann

entry.summary: Argues tokenization in autoregressive models acts as output supervision: via controlled numeric-reasoning experiments decoupling input and output tokenization, output granularity drives task performance, training dynamics, and internals while input tokenization matters little.

entry.title: Teaching Vision-Language Models to Use the Scale They Are Given: Label-Free Equivariance Training for Metric Physical Reasoning

author.name: Kaizhen Tan, Yang Feng, Heqing Du, Siru Tao, Xin Xu, Hanzhe Hong

entry.summary: Shows across eight vision-language models that predictions only partially respond when all world-space quantities in a prompt are rescaled, despite models knowing the correct closed-form scaling laws when asked in scale-free form. Proposes label-free equivariance training to teach models to use supplied scale references for metric physical reasoning.

entry.title: Mind the Rift: Cross-Scale Coupling Mismatch for AI-Generated Video Detection

author.name: Siyu Li, Jin Yang, Weiheng Liang

entry.summary: Identifies cross-scale coupling mismatch as a forensic signal for detecting AI-generated video: natural videos exhibit coupled macro-level temporal dynamics and micro-level pixel residuals from unified imaging physics, which generators systematically violate. Proposes a method that extracts and quantifies information at both scales independently.

entry.title: Monocular Depth Estimation from a Single Image: Progress and Opportunities

author.name: Muxin Liu, Xiaoyang Lyu, Yang-Tian Sun, Yi-Hua Huang, Ziyi Yang, Peng Dai, Xiaojuan Qi

entry.summary: A comprehensive survey of monocular depth estimation tracing evolution from early learning methods to foundation models, distinguishing relative and metric depth, covering datasets, pre-foundation-model advances, and current opportunities.

entry.title: Seeing the World and the Self from Egocentric Video

author.name: Kai Guan, Minchao Jiang, Ruichen WangLi, Wentao Zhu, Lei Zhang

entry.summary: RESELF jointly reconstructs the surrounding scene and the wearer's full-body motion from egocentric video in a shared metric frame, combining deterministic geometric regression for the largely visible scene with generative motion inference for the severely occluded body.

entry.title: BenchMIRT: What are LLM benchmarks actually measuring?

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Ai2 introduces BenchMIRT, a method using multidimensional item response theory to audit LLM benchmarks question by question, revealing which capabilities each question actually measures. This enables building smaller, more focused, and more interpretable evaluation suites.

entry.title: When Features Become Instances: Inverted Contrastive Learning for Unsupervised Feature Selection

author.name: Utsab Ghosh, Roshni Chakraborty

entry.summary: UI-Venus-2 is a general-purpose foundation GUI agent operating across mobile, web, and desktop through a unified closed-loop reasoning-action framework. It scales environment coverage to 170+ multilingual mobile apps plus native desktop OS, with a deep-research pipeline for task construction and improved reward verification. Targets the gap between benchmark GUI agents and dependable real-world automation.

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning Enhanced LLM Agents for Complex Vehicle Routing Problems

author.name: Yi Chen, Zikang Yu, Jiahai Wang, Jinbiao Chen, Jianpeng Zhou, Zizhen Zhang

entry.summary: RLEA is a multi-agent framework that automates modeling of complex vehicle routing problems, using a neural Planner trained with Soft Q-learning to orchestrate LLM agents, plus evolutionary memory and retrieval-augmented components. It lowers the domain expertise barrier for using advanced optimization solvers. This makes combinatorial optimization more accessible to non-experts.

entry.title: Good Memory Has ECC: Evaluating the Memory of Vision-Language Models Beyond Accuracy

author.name: Shmuel Berman, Jia Deng

entry.summary: ECCBench proposes evaluating VLM memory along three axes beyond raw accuracy: efficiency in FLOPs, compression of compressible inputs, and calibration of abstention under uncertainty. The authors find that pretrained VLMs compress memory over text differently than expected, revealing gaps that accuracy-only benchmarks miss. This reframes memory evaluation in a way more aligned with long-horizon deployment needs.

entry.title: Lingua Franca or Probing Artifact? Rethinking Latent Language in Multilingual LLMs

author.name: Deniz Bayazit, Badr AlKhamissi, Antoine Bosselut

entry.summary: The study asks whether different probing methods for identifying latent language in multilingual LLMs measure the same phenomenon, testing across families, checkpoints, and up to 27 languages. It finds probes systematically disagree, suggesting claims about English-pivot routing may be artifacts of probe choice. This is a cautionary result for multilingual interpretability research.

entry.title: Instella-MoE Technical Report

author.name: Jiang Liu, Sudhanshu Ranjan, Prakamya Mishra, Yonatan Dukler, Gowtham Ramesh, Jialian Wu, Ximeng Sun, Wen Xie, Chaojun Hou, Vikram Appia, Zhenyu Gu, Zicheng Liu, Emad Barsoum

entry.summary: Instella-MoE is a fully open 16B-total-parameter Mixture-of-Experts language model with 2.8B active parameters, trained from scratch entirely on AMD Instinct MI300X and MI325X GPUs, featuring Gated Multi-head Latent Attention and FarSkip-Collective connectivity. It documents a full multi-stage pipeline including RL post-training. Valuable as open infrastructure and evidence of a non-NVIDIA training stack.

entry.title: Efficient SWE Agent Benchmarking via Trajectory-Aware Evaluation

author.name: Kefeng Duan, Dewu Zheng, Yanlin Wang, Xiwen Wang, Ensheng Shi, Xilin Liu, Yuchi Ma, Jiachi Chen, Mingwei Liu, Zibin Zheng

entry.summary: PTA-IRT introduces a trajectory-aware item response theory framework for efficient SWE-agent benchmarking, using historical execution trajectories (explored context, attempted edits, solving paths) as privileged information to calibrate small subsets that estimate full-benchmark performance. It fuses process and outcome signals rather than using pass/fail matrices alone.

entry.title: Elite-Weighted Supervised Fine-tuning for Goal-Directed Molecular Optimization

author.name: Shiyun Wa, Yifei Wang, Anna G. Green, Simone Sciabola, Ye Wang

entry.summary: Introduces Elite-Weighted Supervised Fine-tuning (EW-SFT) for goal-directed molecular optimization: reward is used only to select high-scoring elite molecules, and the model updates via its own pretraining loss on those, avoiding architecture-dependent policy-gradient machinery. This makes the optimizer reusable across generator architectures.

entry.title: Online Self-Weighted Fine-Tuning

author.name: Haiquan Wen, Yiwei He, Bei Peng, Guangliang Cheng

entry.summary: Online Self-Weighted Fine-Tuning (OSW-FT) augments SFT with online trajectory-level weighting: a few inference-only rollouts estimate the model's current success rate per query, and the SFT loss is rescaled accordingly. The update direction stays anchored to expert trajectories while magnitude adapts, offering an SFT/RL middle ground with better stability than RL and adaptivity that vanilla SFT lacks.

entry.title: The Multiple Timescales of Gradient Descent on the Edge of Stability: A Perturbative Derivation of the Central Flow

author.name: Rapha\"el Berthier

entry.summary: Provides a perturbative derivation of the central flow, the empirically accurate continuous-time model of gradient descent at the edge of stability, treating gradient descent as a singularly perturbed dynamical system. Three timescales emerge: fast oscillations along sharp directions and slower drifts, formalizing previously heuristic results.

entry.title: Births are difficult to predict even with rich survey and full-population register data

author.name: Elizaveta Sivak, Emily M. Cantrell, Thomas Emery, Javier Garcia-Bernardo, Flavio Hafner, Kasia Karpinska, Malte L\"uken, Adrienne Mendrik, Joris Mulder, Hanzhang Ren, Varun Satish, Mark Verhagen, Angelica M. Maineri, Paulina Pankowska, Jasmin Abdel Ghany, Bruno Arpino, Giovanni Cassani, Julia Hellstrand, Katya Ivanova, Sanni Kuikka, Ana Macanovic, Charles Rahal, Felix C. Tropf, Roland J. Veen, Nicole Walasek, Dani\"el van Wijk, Kelsey Q. Wright, Emilio Zagheni, Henry Abbink, Emanuele Aliverti, Matteo Amestoy, Tilbe Atav, Nicola Barban, Sunnee Billingsley, Goan J. Booij, Louis Boucherie, Yael Broos, Li Ya Chang, Jamie C. Chiu, Chiara Ludovica Comolli, Boris Cule, Qixiang Fang, Dennis M. Feehan, Rachel Ganly, Erwin Gielens, Rolando M. Gonzales Martinez, Andrea Gradassi, Rosember Guerra-Urzola, Mario Guerra-Urzola, St\'ephane Guerrier, Enamul Hassan, Vincent A. Haverhoek, Andrew T. Hendrickson, Amber Howard, Yuxuan Jin, Sayash Kapoor, Erik-Jan van Kesteren, Iris ten Klooster, Marie Labussiere, Lydia T. Liu, Tiffany Liu, Adam Maghout, Simone Meneghello, Lasse Mohr, Clara H. Mulder, Saul J. Newman, Jessica Nis\'en, Janis Norden, Mikkel Odgaard, Riccardo Omenti, Ozancan Ozdemir, Christina Pao, Paige Park, Gaia Penta, Juan C. Perdomo, Tanzir Pial, Alessio Piraccini, Federica Querin, Ziwei Rao, Christian Rellama, Adrien Remund, Frederieke Richert, Arnout van de Rijt, Mojtaba Rostami Kandroodi, Stijn J. Rotman, Lucas Sage, Germans Savcisens, Katrin Schwanitz, Steven Skiena, Alessandro Spata, Yannick Stadtfeld, Benedikt Stroebl, Gaetano Tedesco, Mathilde Theelen, Gianluca Tori, Abigail Tun-Mendicuti, Rishabh Tyagi, Keyon Vafa, Luiz Felipe Vecchietti, Linda Vecgaile, Willem R. J. Vermeulen, Maria-Pia Victoria Feser, Lionel A. Voirol, Thom B. Volker, Xinran Wang, Jiani Yan, Xinyi Zhao, Flora Zhou, Zuzana Zilincikova, Malvina Nissim, Matthew J. Salganik, Gert Stulp

entry.summary: A large collaborative data challenge in which 147 researchers predicted births among Dutch residents using survey data and full-population registers, spanning methods from logistic regression to LLMs and transformers. Predictions were only moderately accurate, advanced models did not beat classical ones, registers did not beat surveys, and simulated stochastic biology established a predictive ceiling suggesting chance, not method, is the binding constraint.

entry.title: OUTLETS: Output-Length Prediction from Speculative Decoding Backbones

author.name: Weihuang Wen, Yingying Liu, Yichuan Liu, Wenqi Zeng, Li Zhou, Chumin Sun, Jie Sun, Tianshu Yu

entry.summary: OUTLETS discovers that draft-decoder representations in speculative decoding frameworks like EAGLE-3 predict output generation length, enabling efficient output-length prediction for LLM serving and cluster scheduling without external proxy models.

entry.title: ClinTraceBench: Source-Verifiable Longitudinal Clinical Reasoning over EHR-Derived Dialogues

author.name: Huimin Wang, Zhengyi Zhao, Yutian Zhao

entry.summary: ClinTraceBench introduces 385 MIMIC-IV-derived dialogues with event-ID provenance and a nine-task taxonomy to evaluate how eight history representation strategies (retrieval, timelines, summaries, agentic memory) support longitudinal clinical reasoning across four backbones.

entry.title: You Cannot Photograph the Same Street Twice: Reliability Limits in Vision-Language Measurement of Urban Change

author.name: Kaizhen Tan

entry.summary: Tests longitudinal reliability of vision-language models measuring urban change from repeated Street View imagery across 4,648 image pairs in five US cities. Finds re-photographing an unchanged street shifts perception scores by an amount equal to 66.5% of the between-street difference, with image re-encoding and prompt-order effects each contributing roughly a fifth of variation.

entry.title: RingMoClaw: An Experience-Inspired Multi-Agent Framework for Self-Evolving Research in Remote Sensing

author.name: Kaiyue Kang, Qixuan He, Peijin Wang, Yingchao Feng, Chao Ren, Kangxin Wang, Wenhui Diao, Yixiao Wang, Liangjin Zhao, Kaiwen Wei, Nayu Liu, Xian Sun

entry.summary: RingMoClaw is an experience-inspired self-evolving multi-agent framework for remote sensing visual interpretation research, with research and quality-control branches and a dual-stream experience bus enabling autonomous iteration on model design and data processing.

entry.title: Compressing AI Traffic: Standardized Neural Network Coding of Visual-Token Representations in Split Vision-Language Inference

author.name: Reza Heidari, Hamed R. Tavakoli, Juho Kannala

entry.summary: Formalizes intermediate visual-token embeddings as AI traffic in split VLM inference and applies the ISO/IEC 15938-17 Neural Network Coding standard to compress the complete visual interface of a Qwen3-VL-8B video QA pipeline with a training-free codec, sweeping quantization across a wide rate range.

entry.title: Towards reliable multimodal disaster severity assessment through preference optimization and explainable vision-language reasoning

author.name: Yuanjun Zhang, Fuzel Ahamed Shaik, Suvojit Acharjee, Fahad Khalid, Mourad Oussalah

entry.summary: A two-stage SFT plus DPO training framework for multimodal disaster severity assessment is proposed, deriving a ReasoningSet and PreferenceSet from a single human-in-the-loop annotation workflow. It evaluates both classification accuracy and explanation quality, addressing scarce annotated data and poor reasoning evaluation. This improves transparency of disaster damage assessment models.

entry.title: Distributed Implicit Harm: A Compositional Safety Blind Spot in MLLM-Based Video Moderation

author.name: Ruotong Wang, Zihao Zhu, Siwei Lyu, Xin Tao, Baoyuan Wu

entry.summary: The paper identifies Distributed Implicit Harm in video moderation: videos whose benign components combine into harmful meaning, either temporally (DIH-T) or across audio-visual modalities (DIH-M). The authors construct data and methods to study this compositional safety blind spot in MLLM-based moderation. It surfaces a real failure mode that current moderation systems likely miss.

entry.title: Confess What You Know: Forget-Set Misalignment with Model Knowledge in LLM Unlearning

author.name: Miso Kim, Georu Lee, Seungwon Jeong, Woojin Lee

entry.summary: The paper identifies forget-set misalignment in LLM unlearning: when the forget set omits memorized information, leakage persists, and when it targets unknown content, utility degrades. Gradient-level analysis shows these stem from misaligned targets, and the proposed CONFS framework uses model confessions to construct aligned forget sets data-blind. A thoughtful fix to a practical unlearning flaw.

entry.title: Does Fault Localization Beat a Fresh Attempt? A Placebo-Controlled Study of Test-Guided Code Repair

author.name: Anik Jha

entry.summary: A placebo-controlled study disentangling whether fault localization helps test-guided code repair or whether targeted edits succeed merely because they are small or because resampling succeeds anyway. Across three model sizes and 488 failing candidates it finds localization is rarely applicable, a sobering audit of a common agentic repair strategy.

entry.title: The zbMATH Open Knowledge Graph: Tracing Centuries of Mathematical Research

author.name: Yuni Susanti, Moritz Schubotz

entry.summary: Presents the zbMATH Open Knowledge Graph covering more than 250 years of mathematics with 34 million entities and 168 million RDF triples, integrating expert-curated reviews, classifications, and disambiguated authorship beyond bibliographic metadata. It enables fine-grained longitudinal analysis of mathematical research.

entry.title: Right Frame, Wrong Rule: Cultural Cues Expose the Financial Knowledge Gap They Were Meant to Close

author.name: Rania Elbadry, Ahmed Heakl, Saeed Almheiri, Fan Zhang, Muhra AlMahri, Xueqing Peng, Mohsinul Kabir, Shuyao Wang, Yi Han, Saadeldine Eletter, Duzhen Zhang, Preslav Nakov, Yuxia Wang, Fajri Koto, Zhuohan Xie

entry.summary: Introduces normative pluralism as a setting where models must select among valid normative frameworks, studied via Islamic finance with a taxonomy separating framework selection from within-framework correctness. Across twelve models and fifty demographic signals, cultural cues steer framework selection and expose accuracy gaps, including a stereotype trap where models pick the cued framework but answer incorrectly.

entry.title: Topological Steering

author.name: Beno\^it Gu\'erand, Tan Minh Nguyen

entry.summary: Topological Steering introduces steering of LLM behavior through topological representations of activation spaces using persistence diagrams from topological data analysis. The global, rather than local, structure is intended to make behavioral control more robust to outliers and distribution shift, and results show consistent improvements over baseline steering.

entry.title: Compile, Don't Memorize: A Context Compilation Architecture (CCA) for In-Context Learning

author.name: Jinhu Qi, Minda Hu, Wentao Zhang, Weiqiang Jin, Yanyu Chen, Junli Wang, Irwin King

entry.summary: Identifies structural brittleness in in-context learning with long novel contexts, where open-weight models pass only 12-16% of detail-graded tasks, and proposes an explicit Context Compilation Architecture that compiles context before answering. It benchmarks against gist retrieval and multi-agent strategies.

entry.title: Explore Before Committing: Hypothesis-Guided Search for Deep Research Agents

author.name: Ruochen Zhou, Zhengyu Chen, Luan Zhang, Siyang Gao, Yee Whye Teh, Shiqi Chen

entry.summary: Analyzes trajectory-level failure modes of deep research agents that commit early to a single search direction, and proposes hypothesis-guided search that grounds exploration in concrete candidates and shifts direction when evidence is weak.

entry.title: A multicenter benchmark and clinically structured metric for coronary CTA report generation

author.name: Zhiyu Ye, Yue Sun, Limiao Zou, Cheng Xu, Keting Xu, Tong Hu, Yue Yu, Hairong Zheng, Yining Wang, Tong Zhang

entry.summary: Establishes a four-centre benchmark of 3,021 coronary CTA series with a clinically structured metric (CSM-CCTA) evaluating open-source 3D vision-language models on report generation at patient, vessel, and segment levels with expert-weighted components.

entry.title: ASSERT: Adaptive Stochastic Sampling for Robust Diffusion Models on Analog Compute-in-Memory Hardware

author.name: Yuannuo Feng, Yizhe Chen, Wenshuai Yao, Yuxin Xie, Ngai Wong, Wenyong Zhou, Wang Kang

entry.summary: ASSERT studies diffusion model inference on analog compute-in-memory hardware with a noise model calibrated against multiple physical CIM chips, finding the early high-noise denoising stage most vulnerable and proposing adaptive stochastic sampling based on first-order trajectory analysis.

entry.title: Fi-ImageNet-1k: An OOD Benchmark From the Inside of the ImageNet-1k Validation Set

author.name: Ruslan Rozumnyi, Mat\v{e}j Such\'anek, Tom\'a\v{s} Voj\'i\v{r}, Kl\'ara Janou\v{s}kov\'a, Ji\v{r}\'i Matas

entry.summary: Fi-ImageNet-1k builds an OOD benchmark from ImageNet-1k validation images that the ReImageNet reannotation effort assigned to no ImageNet-1k class, with expert human annotation supported by MLLM, VLM, and reverse-image-search evidence, exploiting annotation errors as a natural OOD source.

entry.title: Dyn-3D: Unveiling and Resolving Ego-Motion Ambiguity in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jiayu Ding, Zhuodong Liu, Lei Zhang, Manyu Xiong, Hongbo Jin, Haoran Tang, Hongbo Zhang, Changen Zhu, Wenbo Xing

entry.summary: Identifies Kinematic Collapse in vision-language models doing dynamic 3D spatial reasoning: models overfit smooth trajectory priors and degrade severely under large displacements. Introduces the Dyn-3D benchmark with counterfactual 3D rendering to decouple visual changes from kinematics, plus the TempoVista framework with Kinematic-GSPO training.

entry.title: Diffusion Based Unpaired Data Learning for Inverse Problems

author.name: Chenglong Bao, Yiming Dang, Chenguang Duan, Yuling Jiao, Defeng Sun

entry.summary: LUD-DIF proposes a diffusion-based approach for solving inverse problems with unpaired data, decoupling the ELBO of the joint distribution into two independent diffusion processes under a weak-coupling assumption, with theoretical error bounds and a theorem-motivated hyperparameter heuristic.

entry.title: Data-Driven Persona-Conditioned Agents for A/B Test Simulation

author.name: Ziyad Benomar, Weronika {\L}ajewska, Leonardo Perelli, Saab Mansour

entry.summary: The authors show that denoising diffusion models implicitly compute attention-like operations, arguing attention emerges as a universal principle from general training objectives. They also draw functional parallels between autoencoders and attention-based models, and sketch how the equivalence can be exploited to shorten diffusion training. This is a theoretical unification claim across generative paradigms.

entry.title: The Safeguard Worked. Is the LLM System Safer?

author.name: Pingyu Wu, Weiming Zhang, Nenghai Yu

entry.summary: The paper develops a deployment-level criterion for evaluating LLM safeguards, asking how much harmful help a persistently adapting attacker can still obtain, and shows evidence requirements are strongly asymmetric: one successful attack suffices to show residual harm. It enables comparison across safeguard families under one standard. A useful conceptual sharpening for safety evaluation.

entry.title: PCoMoE: Shifting MoE Inference from Monolithic Expert Selection to Fine-Grained Path Composition

author.name: Ziyan Gan, Fangxin Liu, Chenyang Guan, Junjie Wang, Ning Yang, Haomin Li, Xiang Li, Siran Yang, Jiamang Wang, Lin Qu, Zongwu Wang, Li Jiang, Haibing Guan

entry.summary: PCoMoE shifts MoE inference from atomic whole-expert selection to fine-grained path composition, with compatibility-aware layer-wise pruning to suppress intra-expert computational redundancy that existing frameworks ignore.

entry.title: StudentSim: Training LLM-based Student Simulators

author.name: Ke Yang, Chenglong Wang, Michel Galley, Chandan Singh, Jeevana Priya Inala, ChengXiang Zhai, Jianfeng Gao

entry.summary: StudentSim trains LLM-based student simulators via pooled training followed by per-student specialization, turning sparse per-student tutoring data into individualized simulators that both mirror competence and respond to guidance, enabling adaptive AI tutors.

entry.title: LLM-Driven Autonomous Vehicles Inherit Human Driver Biases in Pedestrian Yielding: Results and Implications From A New Benchmark

author.name: Irem Yoldas, Martim Brand\~ao, Jie Zhang, Odinaldo Rodrigues

entry.summary: This paper introduces two bias-testing methodologies — All Else Being Equal and Self-Consistency tests — showing that LLM- and VLM-driven autonomous vehicles inherit human driver biases, including lower pedestrian-yielding rates toward Black pedestrians. It argues fairness analysis must be part of AV evaluation when using general-purpose commonsense models. Timely safety and fairness concern for LLM-based driving.

entry.title: FractalNet-Based Heterogeneous Federated Learning for Orbital Edge Intelligence in Satellite Mega-Constellations: A Wildfire Case Study

author.name: Sai Puppala, Koushik Sinha

entry.summary: The paper proposes heterogeneous federated learning based on FractalNet for orbital edge intelligence in satellite mega-constellations, with depth assigned per satellite according to SWAP-C constraints and predicted inter-satellite contact windows. A wildfire case study demonstrates the approach. It adapts learning architectures to the physical realities of space deployment.

entry.title: CompanionSim: Synthetic Data for Evaluating Anthropomorphism in Human-AI Relationships

author.name: Jacy Reese Anthis, Mark D\'iaz, Renee Shelby

entry.summary: CompanionSim releases a simulation framework with 2,240 simulated multi-turn human-chatbot conversations spanning 16 chatbot behaviors and seven use cases, with human annotations validating fidelity. It aims to accelerate research on AI companionship effects, such as validation and attachment, where real interaction data is scarce. Includes authors from Google with HCI and AI backgrounds.

entry.title: From Terminology to Diagrams: Visual-Instruction Generation for Scientific Diagram Understanding

author.name: Raul Ortega, Jos\'e Manuel G\'omez-P\'erez

entry.summary: Introduces a framework for generating diagram-grounded visual instruction data from scientific curricula, producing SciGram with over 194K diagrams and 1.4M instruction examples targeting scientific diagram understanding. It targets the persistent weakness of VLMs on functional-relational diagrams versus natural images.

entry.title: From Truncation to Commitment: Persistent Context in Uniform Discrete Diffusion

author.name: Satoshi Hayakawa

entry.summary: Proposes committed reveal sampling, a training-free sampler for uniform-state discrete diffusion that stores selected argmax tokens as persistent context for later predictions, with analysis showing Bayes error of clean-token selection cannot increase as noise decreases. It provides a rationale for late selection and keeping selected tokens visible.

entry.title: Text-guided flow matching enables sample-efficient crystal structure generation

author.name: Wentao Li

entry.summary: Introduces TFMat, a text-conditioned flow-matching framework for crystal structure generation using structured materials language as a semantic prior, reaching a 92.04 percent match rate on MP-20 with twenty candidates and improving over CrystalFlow on standard benchmarks. It gives materials scientists a natural-language control interface to generative structure models.

entry.title: Who Judges the Judges? A Chinese Safety QA Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Responses and Safety Judges

author.name: Rui Yang, Shuang Huang, Junhua Liu, Ziqi Zhao, Qingzhong Yan, Yuhang Sun, Cong Liu, Guoping Hu, Rui Mei, Jing Shao

entry.summary: Introduces C-SafeQA, a policy-grounded benchmark for response-level Chinese safety evaluation with 538 base and 8,877 adversarial queries, 37,660 labeled query-response records, and agreement-aware multi-model adjudication with expert blind audits. It shifts evaluation focus from query risk to whether responses violate policy and tests safety judges themselves.

entry.title: Learning Task-Specific Antibody Representations via Function-Aware Masking

author.name: Ayan Goel, Thomas A. Walton, Amirali Aghazadeh

entry.summary: Introduces function-aware masking for antibody language model pretraining, aligning mask placement with functional priors such as IMGT annotations or structure predictions rather than defaulting to CDR-focused masking. Specialist masking strategies yield task-specialist representations useful for binding-related and property prediction tasks.

entry.title: SFAD: Speculative Factuality-Aware Decoding

author.name: Guanqiao Chen, Di Wang, Lijie Hu

entry.summary: SFAD is a speculative decoding framework that improves contextual faithfulness without inference slowdown, using a new preference dataset (ConFide) to avoid the double forward pass of contrastive decoding or costly RLHF alignment.

entry.title: Can Scene Text Recognition Read Rare Compositions?

author.name: Genpei Zhang

entry.summary: Stratifies scene text recognition accuracy by word rarity and character n-gram novelty, showing accuracy at the rare-word and rare-trigram corner drops 10-18 points below common cases across languages, and that this is not a capacity bottleneck since backbone scale-ups do not close the gap. Challenges the assumption that scene text recognition is a solved problem.

entry.title: HyperWorld: Hypergraph-Structured State Serialization Improves Learned Textual World Models

author.name: Yun-Jian Zhang, Chen-Wei Liang, Tian-Yi Zhang, Jian Ding, Yi-Lun Wu, Ao-Bo Li, Wei-Cong Su, Saifullah, Hong-Yu An, Mu-Jiang-Shan Wang

entry.summary: HyperWorld is a controlled study of how state serialization format affects learned textual world models, comparing raw observations, independent sentences, pairwise triples, and entity-centered hyperedge units under a shared training objective. It finds that grouping related facts around entities improves the model's ability to predict symbolic action effects. This matters for building LLM agents that can plan in text environments.

entry.title: CacheBridge: Efficient Cross-Model KV Cache Transfer

author.name: Xingyu Qu, Siyuan Lu, Zhiyu Chen, Sheng Wang, Tao Lin

entry.summary: FLaG is a plug-in token aggregation module that re-expresses encoder outputs in the Fourier domain before pooling, using latent queries and channel gating on the rFFT spectrum. It is evaluated across protein, image, and other classification tasks. The work broadens the design space for pooling beyond the original token space.

entry.title: Are We There Yet? Assessing Computer-Use Agents for Blind Users' Accessible Interaction with Desktop Applications

author.name: Satwik Ram Kodandaram, Monalika Padma Reddy, Xiaojun Bi, Jiawei Zhou, I. V. Ramakrishnan, Vikas Ashok

entry.summary: This three-week diary study of eight blind users operating a screen-reader-accessible computer-use agent prototype, OLLA, collected 1,258 commands across 12 applications, finding the best model, the released GPT-5, achieved only 52.5 percent success. Trace analysis reveals grounding, planning, constraint-tracking, and termination failures. It documents both accessibility promise and real gaps of CUAs for blind users.

entry.title: Replacing Training with Memory: Listwise Selection for Text-to-SQL

author.name: Yeonseok Jeong, Soyoung Yoon, Seongjun Lee, Seung-won Hwang

entry.summary: Proposes MaP-SQL, a fine-tuning-free listwise selector for Text-to-SQL pipelines that replaces two learned objectives with inference-time retrieval of reusable structured memories encoding schema mappings and positional-bias mitigation. It matters because it removes the costly fine-tuning step commonly needed for candidate selection in generate-execute-select systems.

entry.title: Calibration is the Bottleneck: An Action-Class Diagnostic of Multi-Turn Tool-Calling

author.name: Kangjia Zhao, Jiajun Li, Haozhan Shen, Wei Chow, Linfeng Li, Hang Song, Lingdong Kong, Chen Zhi, Tiancheng Zhao, Songhua Liu, Jianwei Yin

entry.summary: Proposes an action-class diagnostic framework decomposing multi-turn tool-calling failures into action-class miscalibration and execution failure, with a self-revealing upper bound based on gold action recall. It shows aggregate benchmark accuracy obscures imbalanced progress across multi-turn situations.

entry.title: SinkPruner: Sink-Free Visual Token Pruning for Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Shiyu Li, Zi-Yuan Hu, Shijia Huang, Yanyang Li, Yiwu Zhong, Liwei Wang

entry.summary: Proposes SinkPruner, a training-free visual token pruning method for multimodal LLMs that identifies high-norm outlier tokens as redundant and prunes them, correcting mistakes made by vision-centric and text-guided pruning strategies. It reduces inference cost while preserving multimodal understanding.

entry.title: On Synthesis of Metric Interval Temporal Logics

author.name: Hsi-Ming Ho, Shankaranarayanan Krishna, Khushraj Madnani

entry.summary: Presents the first framework for precise passive learning of Metric Interval Temporal Logic without templates or restricted fragments, reducing timed learning to a scalable untimed problem by injecting inferred timing constraints as Boolean atomic propositions. It targets automated mining of formal specifications for real-time system verification.

entry.title: EDRAC: Benchmarking Arabic Dialect Reading Comprehension

author.name: Noor Abo Mokh, Kirill Chirkunov, Teresa Lynn, Nizar Habash, Reham Marzouk, Malik H. Altakrori, Younes Samih, Muhammed Abu Odeh, Nour Rabih, Rahaf Alshahrani, Hamad Alshehhi, Hamdan Al-Ali, Muhra Almahri, Besher Hassan, Mohamed Anwar, Abed Alhakim Freihat, Preslav Nakov, Alham Fikri Aji

entry.summary: Introduces EDRAC, the first large-scale benchmark for dialectal Arabic machine reading comprehension and generative QA covering five major dialects, with 499 passages from naturally occurring spoken interactions and 4,977 QA pairs built via a human-LLM collaborative pipeline. It fills a gap left by benchmarks focused on formal Modern Standard Arabic.

entry.title: CordisBench: Can Language Models Reason About Component Lifecycles in Dynamic Agent Harnesses?

author.name: Damien Sileo, Dimitri Kachler

entry.summary: CordisBench is a 1,200-question benchmark testing whether LLMs can reason about component lifecycles in dynamic agent harnesses, where models modify the software that shapes their own execution. Tasks include identifying affected components and predicting state under teardown orders; three efficiency-oriented models are evaluated.

entry.title: Deterministic LLM Inference Across GPU Kernels: Power-of-Two INT8 Quantization Scales and the Limits of Tolerance-Based Conformance

author.name: Teng-Ruei Chen

entry.summary: Injects nine faults into a reference INT8 quantized GEMM pipeline over thousands of layer-fault-regime cells of Qwen3-1.7B and measures what tolerance-based conformance suites can detect. It finds that a class of epilogue faults moves output by at most a single bfloat16 spacing, making tolerance checks structurally blind to them, motivating deterministic inference requirements.

entry.title: How Do Language Models Choose Between Context and Memory?

author.name: Benjamin Shih, John Winnicki, Arianna Cao

entry.summary: Investigates how language models choose between contextual information and parametric memory when they conflict, using counterfactual experiments that interchange coordinates along authority directions between matched prompts. It distinguishes whether steering directions are causal and reusable across tasks, beyond mere correlation.

entry.title: Gradient-Update Mismatch: Rethinking Conflict-Free Training of Physics-Informed Neural Networks

author.name: Jing Xiao, Xinhai Chen, Qinglin Wang, Menghan Jia, Zhiquan Lai, Dongsheng Li, Jie Liu, Tiejun Li

entry.summary: Identifies a gradient-update mismatch in physics-informed neural network training: even when gradient surgery produces a conflict-free direction, modern optimizers with historical state and adaptive scaling can destroy that property after transformation. The paper characterizes when this occurs and proposes fixes for conflict-free training of PINNs. This improves understanding of multi-objective loss interactions in physics-ML.

entry.title: Measuring Optimal Transport in Transformer Depth

author.name: Alexandre Quemy

entry.summary: Measures whether token-state clouds in transformers (Pythia-160M/410M) move across depth according to optimal transport, using exact assignment and calibrated cost decomposition. Both models approximate the OT map at the final layer, with the larger model matching optimal cost.

entry.title: Reliability Challenges in Diffusion Vision-Language Models

author.name: Md. Atabuzzaman, Chris Thomas

entry.summary: First systematic reliability evaluation of hallucination and bias in diffusion vision-language models, benchmarking six dLVLMs against AR baselines and finding reversed yes-bias, competitive hallucination but degraded linguistic quality, and near-zero accuracy on underrepresented racial groups.

entry.title: Beyond Language Priors: Diagnosing and Fixing Visual-Origin Hallucinations in Multimodal LLM

author.name: Peiyang Xu, Xiaopei Zhu, Jun Zhu, Xiaolin Hu

entry.summary: Challenges the language-prior account of object hallucination in MLLMs, providing quantitative evidence for visual-origin hallucination: hallucinated samples show lower image-text similarity and inverted attention patterns, motivating fixes targeting visual feature extraction and alignment.

entry.title: Forbid Your Attention: Fooling Multimodal Large Language Models by Selectively Removing Intrinsic Focus in Spectral Domain

author.name: Daizong Liu, Junhao Dong, Zhiyuan Ma, Xiaoye Qu, Xiang Fang, Runwei Guan, Keke Tang, Jianfeng Dong, Yew-Soon Ong

entry.summary: Investigates the intrinsic focus of multimodal LLMs in the frequency domain and finds predictions are especially sensitive to phase information; exploits this to build adversarial attacks that selectively remove intrinsic focus in the spectral domain.

entry.title: HELIOS: From midnight to noon, continuous outdoor urban scene relighting

author.name: Hala Djeghim, Nathan Piasco, Luis Rold\~ao, Moussab Bennehar, Dzmitry Tsishkou, C\'eline Loscos, D\'esir\'e Sidib\'e

entry.summary: HELIOS performs continuous outdoor urban scene relighting from midnight to noon using unlabeled real-world driving data without paired multi-illumination supervision, integrating albedo-based conditioning into a cycle-consistent diffusion pipeline with robust albedo distillation for nighttime conditions.

entry.title: MeRoPE: Metric Rotary Position Embedding for Camera-Controlled Video Generation

author.name: Zhijian Qiao, Xinjiang Wang, Jiajie Chen, Haoming Huang, Meng Li, Chih-Chung Chou, Jing Wang, Shaojie Shen

entry.summary: MeRoPE introduces a norm-preserving metric rotary position embedding for camera-controlled video generation, encoding relative orientations between calibrated viewing rays and multi-frequency metric displacements to fix unbounded attention-logit growth on real metric trajectories.

entry.title: MegaStyle++: Scaling Image Style Space through Hierarchical Style Definition

author.name: Junyao Gao, Sibo Liu, Jiaxing Li, Yanan Sun, Weidong Zhang, Jun Zhang, Cairong Zhao

entry.summary: MegaStyle++ proposes a hierarchical definition of image style from overall style identity to fine-grained attributes and releases MegaStyle++-8M, a dataset with 150K style identities, 1M style prompts, and 8M stylized images for training style-aware models.

entry.title: TPR-Attention for Combinatorial Generalization

author.name: Melisa Civeleko\u{g}lu, Isabeau Pr\'emont-Schwarz

entry.summary: Introduces TPR-attention, an attention mechanism over tensor-product representations that embeds structured inductive bias into deep networks to enable combinatorial generalization. Controlled experiments on compositional tasks show it outperforms existing architectural components on recombining known factors of variation.

entry.title: Provably Efficient Federated Reinforcement Learning with Linear Function Approximation and Logarithmic Communication Cost

author.name: Zihang Liang, Haochen Zhang, Lingzhou Xue

entry.summary: Fed-LSVI is the first provably efficient federated online RL algorithm with linear function approximation, using determinant-based event-triggered synchronization to achieve logarithmic communication cost without sharing raw trajectories. This addresses both the communication bottleneck and privacy constraints of federated RL. The theoretical guarantees are the core contribution.

entry.title: Don't Let the Model Write the YAML: Deterministic, Minimal-Diff GitOps Remediation from LLM-Proposed Field Changes

author.name: Pruthvi Davineni

entry.summary: This paper evaluates having LLMs write GitOps remediation files directly and finds no text-generation strategy is safe for unattended automation: unified diffs silently misapply roughly one in seven times under tolerant patching, and full-file rewrites are non-deterministic and capability-dependent. It proposes deterministic, minimal-diff remediation from LLM-proposed field changes instead. A practical, deployment-grounded safety result.

entry.title: Heard but Not Heeded: Paralinguistic Information Encoding and Loss in Audio-Language Models

author.name: Bhuvan Koduru, Dareen Safar B Alharthi, Rita Singh, Bhiksha Raj

entry.summary: The paper mechanistically analyzes paralinguistic information, how something is said, in four open audio-language models including Whisper-large-v2 and Qwen2-Audio-7B Instruct, using CKA, probing, and a content-prosody leakage metric. All models encode speaking style strongly in late encoder layers but the information is lost downstream. This documents a systematic capability gap in audio-language models.

entry.title: From Rollouts to Recipes: Self-Contained Post-Training for LLMs

author.name: Yifei Li, Lingling Zhang, Muye Huang, Zihan Ma, Jiashuai Liu, Jun Liu

entry.summary: Self-Routing is a behavior-conditioned post-training framework that uses rollout correctness and confidence to route each sample to GRPO, on-policy self-distillation, regularization, or skipping, improving over uniform recipes on math reasoning with Qwen3 and Qwen3.5 backbones.

entry.title: IntroConformal: Conformal Factuality Guarantees for Large Vision-Language Models via Introspective Signals

author.name: Md. Atabuzzaman, Christian Alexander, Chris Thomas

entry.summary: IntroConformal is a training-free conformal risk control framework providing finite-sample factuality guarantees for LVLMs using introspective signals like layer-wise semantic stability rather than external verifiers.

entry.title: Feed-Forward Multi-view Multi-person Reconstruction with Contrastive Human-Aware 3D Representation

author.name: Yuanwang Yang, Buzhen Huang, Zongxuan Ren, Jing Huang, Kun Li

entry.summary: Presents a top-down paradigm for feed-forward multi-view multi-person reconstruction that maintains a unified instance-centric human-aware 3D space, jointly handling camera calibration, cross-view association, and reconstruction via cross-modal contrastive learning without explicit matching.

entry.title: I-CARE: Analysis of interference-related phenomena in a controllable, diverse and representative unlearning setting for text-to-image models

author.name: Leonardo Santiago Benitez Pereira, Marcos Escudero Vi\~nolo, Luis Herranz Arribas

entry.summary: I-CARE formalizes interference — unintended degradation of semantically related concepts during machine unlearning in text-to-image models — as a first-class object of study. It provides definitions of tasks, metrics, and reporting templates rather than a new benchmark or algorithm. This enables reproducible comparison of unlearning methods' side effects.

entry.title: Deploying and Evaluating a Smart-Agriculture Agentic Engine for Full-Season Soybean Farm Operations

author.name: Ao Qu, Panagiotis Michelakis, Linyuan Han, Yiannis Hadjiyianni, Kun Ouyang, Konstantinos Siskos, Feng Li, Ran Meng, Jingchi Jiang, Dimitrios Stamoulis, Jie Liu

entry.summary: FAIRY is a full-stack smart-agriculture agent system deployed at an operating soybean research farm, executing full-season workflows from ridge preparation through planting, irrigation, treatment, and harvest. It integrates machinery APIs, soil and canopy sensors, drones, satellite products, weather data, and crop-process models. A rare end-to-end agentic deployment in a physical, long-horizon domain.

entry.title: IMPACT: Attention Is the Interaction Map for Scalable Interaction-Aware World Model Training

author.name: Rongze Tang, Jianjie Fang, Zhaolu Wang, Ziyou Wang, Xvyuan Liu, Haisheng Su, Xin Zhang, Wei Wu, Chen Gao, Yong Li, Zhibo Chen

entry.summary: IMPACT identifies a supervision-allocation mismatch in world model training: globally averaged MSE lets static content dominate optimization while sparse dynamic-object regions critical to interactions are underweighted. It repurposes attention maps as interaction maps to reallocate supervision without auxiliary estimators or manual annotation. Improves physically plausible interaction modeling at scale.

entry.title: QTEA: Ternary LLMs with Sparse Residual Salient Weight and By-Column Optimization

author.name: Yipin Guo, Arun M George, Jie Fu, Tareq Mahmoud, Sixue Xing, Siddharth Joshi

entry.summary: QTEA is a sub-2-bit post-training quantization framework that quantizes LLM weights to ternary values while using salient weights as residual error compensators under semi-structured 1:4 sparsity for GPU efficiency. It also adds column-wise rescale refinement to GPTQ-style quantization. This targets the hard regime below 2 bits where most PTQ methods collapse.

entry.title: CoLT-Drive: Counterfactual Long-Tail Benchmarking and Knowledge-Preserving Adaptation for Driving Affordance Prediction

author.name: Zhengxu Tang, Guofeng Cui, Ziyu Gong, Xiaozhou Zhang, Ruifeng Deng, Chengzhi Qi, Ke Chen, Sachin Patil, Tianjun Xiao, Langechuan Liu, Pichao Wang

entry.summary: CoLT-Drive reframes long-tail driving failures as decision-level affordance prediction, asking whether a model infers how rare objects change feasible ego-vehicle actions rather than merely recognizing them. The 3,536-sample counterfactual benchmark inserts rare objects into fixed scenes to measure this. Industry-affiliated authors provide a focused new evaluation target for driving systems.

entry.title: FoldingAgent: Inferring Parametric Origami Procedures from Demonstration Videos

author.name: Maya Moriya, Sigal Raab, Yael Vinker, Tali Dekel

entry.summary: FoldingAgent is an agentic framework that infers explicit parametric folding programs from origami demonstration videos using a VLM equipped with tools for geometric simulation, physical plausibility checks, and self-verification. Unlike static crease-pattern prediction, it operates sequentially and can replan. Creative multimodal reasoning demonstration, likely from a strong vision group.

entry.title: Capability-Gated Language Models: Security Composes, Utility Does Not

author.name: Patrikas Vanagas, Augustas Ma\v{c}ijauskas, Laurynas Lopata

entry.summary: The paper formalizes capability-gated deployment: per-principal access control inside one set of LLM weights, with configurations forming a lattice of meets and joins. Instantiated via sparse rank gating over nested factorization, it proves security composes while utility does not. A novel angle on deployment-time safety customization.

entry.title: HBQ: Hierarchical Scaling Block Quantization with Hardware-Efficiency-Aware Design for Accurate LLM Inference

author.name: Chun-Ting Chen, Dongmin Han, Hangyeol Mun, Jake Hyun, Arnab Raha, Amit Agarwal, Mark Anders, Mohamed Abdelfattah, Jae-sun Seo

entry.summary: HBQ explores the design space of block quantization for LLM inference with hardware-efficiency-aware design, finding that larger blocks amortize dequantization costs but hurt accuracy. It proposes hierarchical scaling blocks to navigate this trade-off with measured hardware and benchmark results. Valuable for low-precision inference deployment.

entry.title: EM^2Mem: Event-Centric Multimodal Memory for Large Language Models

author.name: Yijun Chen, Yaqi Zheng, Yanya Li, Boyi Xiao, Buqiang Xu, Shuofei Qiao, Jizhan Fang, Xinle Deng, Yunzhi Yao, Xuehai Wang, Liuxin Zhang, Hui Li, Huajun Chen, Shumin Deng

entry.summary: EM2Mem proposes event-centric multimodal memory for long-video question answering, binding heterogeneous evidence to event anchors so that memory cells are generation-ready with aligned multimodal records, temporal context, and provenance. It addresses the problem that isolated retrieved fragments force models to reconstruct alignment at inference time. A solid memory-architecture contribution.

entry.title: DualStake: Dual-Path Confidence Calibration in Deep Research Agents

author.name: Yinuo Xu, Yuwei Liang, Jianjie Cheng, Meng Wang, Yongcan Yu, Shuo Lu, Jian Liang
