entry.summary: Proposes DualStake, a dual-path confidence calibration method for Deep Research agents that elicits evidence confidence after retrieval and answer confidence after generation, finding the former is the stronger uncertainty signal. It targets the severe overconfidence that undermines user trust and abstention decisions.

entry.title: Embedded Conditional Independence Tests for Large Language Model Generated Text with an Application to German Parliament Speeches

author.name: Marco Simnacher, Georg Keilbar, Benjamin K\"onig, Christoph Lippert, Sonja Greven

entry.summary: Proposes embedded conditional independence tests for LLM-generated text, testing whether an output carries information about an attribute beyond its source text, with an application to German parliament speeches. It extends CIT applicability to high-dimensional multimodal data via embeddings with sufficiency conditions.

entry.title: Disclosure-Gated User Simulation for Companion-Agent Evaluation

author.name: Yao Liu, Yu He

entry.summary: Addresses the over-cooperative simulated user problem in LLM-based agent evaluation with a disclosure gate that conditions information release on companion agent behavior, using a five-gate ladder merged into three observable depth layers. The user simulator is trained against the specification so gating behavior need not be test-time prompted.

entry.title: Causal Evidentiary Governance for High-Risk Machine Learning Systems

author.name: Samah Kareem, Bar{\i}\c{s} \c{C}elikta\c{s}

entry.summary: Introduces Causal Evidentiary Governance, a framework where regulated institutions commit to versioned DAGs partitioning causal pathways into allowable and disallowed groups, with a Causal Harm Rate metric and signed decision attestations. It targets gaps in fairness governance under the EU AI Act and GDPR regarding causal attribution and evidentiary verification.

entry.title: REFACTOR-VLA: Unsupervised Library Learning of Typed Motor Programs

author.name: Riyaaz Shaik, Chandru Venkataraman

entry.summary: Introduces REFACTOR-VLA, a wake/sleep system that learns reusable robot skills by clustering motor-program fragments under a behavioral-equivalence kernel computed from rollouts of a learned latent world model. It addresses the monolithic design of VLA models like OpenVLA and RT-2 that lack reusable behavior abstractions.

entry.title: Position Matters: Feature Inversion Attacks in ViT Split Inference with Token Reduction and Shuffling

author.name: Stefano Leggio, Giulio Rossolini, Alessandro Biondi

entry.summary: Introduces ViTAMINS, integrating synthetic hard negatives into self-supervised vision transformer pretraining, yielding emergent classifier-like representations with gains up to 11.3 percent and a ViT-B surpassing V-JEPA with ViT-L. It benchmarks broadly across ImageNet, retrieval, copy detection, and segmentation.

entry.title: Designing Proactive Thought Partners for Writing

author.name: Chao Zhang, Abe Davis, Chih-Wei Chen, Chin-Chia Hsu

entry.summary: A design-space study of proactive thought partners for writing: configurable AI agents that offer higher-level cognitive support (beyond autocomplete) at appropriate moments. A one-week deployment with 16 participants yields qualitative insights into roles and proactivity configurations.

entry.title: Adaptive Critical Token-Aware Retrieval for Repository-Level Code Generation

author.name: Kefeng Duan, Dewu Zheng, Yanlin Wang, Terry Yue Zhuo, Mingwei Liu, Jianxing Yu, Jiachi Chen, Ensheng Shi, Xilin Liu, Yuchi Ma, Zibin Zheng

entry.summary: Proposes adaptive retrieval for repository-level code generation that identifies critical tokens during autoregressive generation and injects fine-grained repository context targeted at those tokens, rather than providing generic task-level context. Motivated by the observation that generation errors concentrate at a few decisive positions.

entry.title: Can LLMs Use Relational Transformer Embeddings?

author.name: Francisco Galuppo Azevedo, Clarissa Lima Loures

entry.summary: Tests whether frozen Relational Transformer embeddings injected as soft tokens into Qwen3.5-4B (with MLP projection, LoRA, SFT then GSPO) enable LLMs to reason over multi-table relational data across 10 RelBench tasks under four supervision regimes. The study clarifies when this fusion strategy helps versus fails.

entry.title: Post-hoc Alignment of LLM-judges to Human Judgment Distribution

author.name: Sebastian Steindl, Nikos Voskarides, Alberto Gasparin, Diego Marcheggiani

entry.summary: Systematically studies whether LLM-as-a-judge can predict human judgment distributions rather than only aggregated hard labels, finding near-human hard-label performance but poor soft-label prediction across five datasets.

entry.title: Behaviorally Effective LoRA Writes Are Sparse and Structured

author.name: Haruto Sato, Yuki Tanaka, Ren Nakamura, Aoi Kobayashi, Mei Ito

entry.summary: Shows behaviorally effective LoRA writes are sparse and structured using a Learned-Basis LoRA recipe that warms up an unconstrained adapter, converts to an orthonormal basis, and continues training, with held-out accuracy preserved across 14 exact switches.

entry.title: Aligned but Flattened: Analyzing the Trade-off between Cultural Alignment and Diversity in LLMs

author.name: Jingshen Zhang, Shaoyang Xu, Wenxuan Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a framework jointly formalizing cultural alignment and diversity, benchmarking six LLMs on the World Values Survey and uncovering a trade-off: optimizing cultural alignment flattens cultural diversity, suggesting models memorize dominant values rather than perceive nuance.

entry.title: What Does an Agentic Software Engineering Benchmark Measure? Profiling Task Demands and Agent Behaviour Beyond What Category Labels Reveal

author.name: Radin Shayanfar, Keheliya Gallaba, Ahmed E. Hassan

entry.summary: Introduces the Spread-Novelty-Centrality profile characterizing demands of repository-level coding tasks, applied to five benchmarks and 14,922 agent trajectories, showing category labels are unreliable proxies for what benchmarks actually demand.

entry.title: StreamScout: Learning When to Look Deeper for Streaming Video Understanding

author.name: Ce Zhang, Jing Bi, Jinxi He, Jianshu Zhang, Jingyang Lin, Yunzhong Xiao, Minghao Fu, Yaqi Xie, Zhentao Xie, Weicong Chen, Katia Sycara, Ming Zhou

entry.summary: StreamScout adapts inference depth to query difficulty in streaming video understanding, maintaining a lightweight textual timeline and progressively adding up to three increasingly informative visual views at query time.

entry.title: Advanced Pixel Diffusion Model with Guided Sparse Global Refinement

author.name: Weiyi You, Jinhua Zhang, Xingyu Zhou, Wei Long, Junyu Lou, Shuhang Gu

entry.summary: PixSGR introduces sparse global refinement for pixel-space diffusion, overcoming the trade-off between large-patch tokenization detail loss and intra-patch refinement that breaks structural continuity across patch boundaries.

entry.title: CERF: Communication-Efficient and Retraining-Free Collaborative Perception

author.name: Jiuwu Hao, Ziyi Ni, Liguo Sun, Yuting Wan, Yueyang Wu, Ti Xiang, Haolin Song, Pin Lv

entry.summary: CERF introduces a virtual modality generated from other agents' perception outputs to augment BEV features for open heterogeneous collaborative perception, achieving communication efficiency and retraining-free deployment without dense feature map exchange.

entry.title: Pix2Rep-v2: Data-Efficient Representation Learning for Dense Medical Imaging Applications

author.name: S. Sifaoui, E. Angelini, S. Toupin, T. Pezel, L. Le Folgoc

entry.summary: Pix2Rep-v2 provides dense self-supervised learning of pixel- and voxel-level representations with redundancy reduction and equivariance principles, scaling efficiently to 3D and wide field-of-view medical imaging and evaluated across four datasets, multiple modalities, and data regimes.

entry.title: Benchmarking spiking neural networks across sensing modalities on edge devices

author.name: Xin Du, Di Yu, Changze Lv, Yuqi Zhang, Zhuo Chen, Wentao Tong, Helin Zheng, Weisong Zhang, Xiaofan Zhao, Linshan Jiang, Shijie Ji, Hui Fang, Xiaoqing Zheng, Gang Pan, Shuiguang Deng

entry.summary: A systematic benchmark of spiking neural networks across five sensing modalities and multiple edge devices, evaluating spike encoding, neuron models, and topologies under consistent training and deployment protocols. Key finding: SNN advantages are strongly modality-dependent, with wireless sensing emerging as a standout use case versus broadly comparable ANN performance elsewhere.

entry.title: Predicting Program Exit Code with LLMs and Programming Language Semantics

author.name: Lara Marinov, Aditya Thimmaiah, Jayanth Srinivasa, Junyi Jessy Li, Milos Gligoric

entry.summary: The paper introduces Program Executability Prediction, a task asking LLMs to predict whether a program is semantically valid given syntax and operational semantics, to determine whether models apply given semantics or lean on pretraining priors. A custom dataset with valid and invalid programs enables controlled study. A valuable probe of LLM code understanding.

entry.title: TUTTI: Toward generalizable audio-to-score transcription via fully synthesized data

author.name: Jianhuai Hu, Yashan Wang, Shangda Wu, Zhancheng Guo, Shijie Liang, Wuna Meng, Chuanqi Yang, Xiaobing Li, Feng Yu, Maosong Sun

entry.summary: TUTTI is a pretraining paradigm for generalizable audio-to-score transcription built entirely on synthetic multi-instrumentation data generated by a symbolic music model with audio rendering. It removes dependence on scarce human-annotated paired data and improves cross-domain generalization. Notable also as work from a Tsinghua-affiliated music AI group.

entry.title: HarnessEvolve: Learning from Reference Trajectories for Reliable Agent Self-Evolution

author.name: Wen Jiang, Mingmin Chu, Yimeng Tian, Qianxin Zhang, Haofei Yang, Rui Yang, Yang Liu, Tao Lv, Fangming Li

entry.summary: HarnessEvolve is a self-evolving agent framework that learns from reference trajectories to address credit assignment failure, shortcut learning, and catastrophic forgetting when optimizing an agent harness. It decouples the execution agent from trajectory-derived guidance. A competent contribution to the fast-growing agent self-improvement area.

entry.title: Does task decomposition improve automatic NLG evaluation?

author.name: Sebastian Steindl, Nikos Voskarides, Alberto Gasparin, Diego Marcheggiani

entry.summary: Systematically compares LLM-as-a-judge methods with and without task decomposition for NLG evaluation, finding no evidence decomposition itself helps; previously reported gains stem from using human labels as training data, not from decomposition.

entry.title: AI Morbidity and Mortality: A Framework for Clinical AI Failure Review

author.name: Paulius Mui, Dean F. Sittig, Steve Labkoff, Sanjay Basu

entry.summary: AI M&M proposes a structured, blameless framework for case-based review of clinical AI failures, analogous to morbidity and mortality conferences in medicine. It combines standardized case intake, evidence preservation, investigator-level reconstruction, and tool-in-loop attribution to explain how risk emerges across AI systems, clinicians, and workflows. Addresses a real institutional gap as clinical AI deploys at scale.

entry.title: Autoresearch for Marketplace Catalogs: From Legacy Forms to AI-Native Matching

author.name: Kartik Ravisankar, Hojat Abdolanezhad, Daniel Capo, Sang Su Lee, Shishir Dash, Vijay Anand Raghavan

entry.summary: EULER is a multi-agent system for mathematical discovery that treats cross-domain bridges — transferring a problem between mathematical communities' tools and objects — as the unit of search. It runs direct, adjacent, and distant-domain routes in competition with evidence-checked returns and contamination-screened frozen conjectures. Evaluated on 120 recent conjectures.

entry.title: Retrieval, Scoring, and Decoding Shape Performance and Stability in LLM-based Conversational Recommendation

author.name: Ante Kapetanovic, Tomislav Duricic, Andro Mercep, Emanuel Lacic

entry.summary: This paper dissects how retrieval, scoring, and decoding choices affect LLM-based conversational recommendation on the ReDial benchmark. It shows that reported gains from LLM rerankers are highly protocol-dependent, with strict candidate-aware scoring dramatically outperforming zero-shot generation. The work matters because it exposes measurement fragility in a popular applied setting.

entry.title: Do General NLP Embeddings Capture Ontological Reasoning?

author.name: Hamed Babaei Giglou, Jennifer D'Souza, S\"oren Auer

entry.summary: AVA is a framework of 171,007 contrastive triplets from 163 ontologies for testing whether general-purpose embeddings capture logic-sensitive relational semantics, using hard negatives with contradictory relational meaning. Evaluations of 25+ embedding models show substantial weaknesses, with the best model achieving only modest accuracy. The benchmark exposes a real gap between linguistic fluency and ontological reasoning.

entry.title: Independent Reinforcement Learning in Discounted Markov Games

author.name: Asrin Efe Yorulmaz, Ugur Aydin, Tamer Basar

entry.summary: This theory paper proves that for discounted general-sum Markov games there is no polynomial-time algorithm, under PPAD hardness assumptions, for computing accurate coarse correlated equilibria with independent decentralized learners. It also gives the first radically uncoupled algorithm with sub-exponential convergence guarantees. A meaningful advance in multi-agent learning theory.

entry.title: Differentially Private Paired Table-Image Multimodal Synthesis

author.name: Kai Chen, Josephine Lamp, Somesh Jha, Tianhao Wang

entry.summary: DP-TabImage is a differentially private framework for synthesizing paired table-image data, factorizing the joint as table distribution via a private graphical model plus a table-conditioned diffusion model trained with DP-SGD. It addresses preserving cross-modal dependence under modality-specific private mechanisms. A solid privacy research contribution.

entry.title: On the Human and Computer Alignment of Attribute-Based Music Matches

author.name: Roser Batlle-Roca, Woosung Choi, Joan Serr\`a, Fabio Morreale, Wei-Hsiang Liao, Xavier Serra, Emilia G\'omez, Yuki Mitsufuji

entry.summary: Conducts a perceptual triplet forced-choice experiment on 300 music match cases across melody, harmony, rhythm, voice, and timbre to measure how well audio-based similarity metrics align with human judgments of potential training-data replication. It informs ethical debates on originality, attribution, and intellectual property in generative music AI.

entry.title: StateSwap: Probing Support-Elimination Hidden States in Multiple-Choice Questions

author.name: Chao Gao, Haijiang Liu, Qiyuan Li, Caicai Guo, Frank van Harmelen, Jinguang Gu

entry.summary: Investigates why LLMs answer multiple-choice questions inconsistently under support-oriented versus elimination-oriented framings, using a dual-framing protocol and a [STATE] token whose residual activations can be swapped between paired prompts. Swapping activations transfers framing-specific behavior, implicating separable intermediate-layer representations.

entry.title: Superposed Latent Autoencoder

author.name: Quanling Zhao, Jiaying Yang, Tianqi Zhang, Ziyang Hao, Fatemeh Asgarinejad, Flavio Ponzina, Tajana Rosing

entry.summary: Introduces the Superposed Latent Autoencoder, which preserves high-capacity latents under tight storage budgets by binding them with randomized keys and superposing multiple codes into a single memory tensor with learned recovery. It replaces irreversible dimensional bottlenecks with suppressible structured interference.

entry.title: Athena: Vulnerability-Affected Library Identification via Knowledge Graph Completion

author.name: Phong Trinh Duy, Trang Dang Yen, Hung Nguyen-Huu, Bach Le, Quyet-Thang Huynh, Dieu Hoang Vu, David Lo, Thanh Le-Cong

entry.summary: Proposes Athena, the first graph-based approach to vulnerability-affected library identification, modeling vulnerability databases as a knowledge graph and reformulating identification as knowledge graph completion. It addresses the fact that over half of vulnerability database entries contain missing or incorrect affected-library information.

entry.title: From Confusion to Clarity: Confusion-Aware Retrieval and Knowledge Injection for Text Classification

author.name: Manish Gupta, Chaitanya Giri, Jayasimha Talur

entry.summary: Proposes a confusion-aware retrieval framework for LLM text classification over large taxonomies: it identifies label pairs the model confuses, expands candidates with confusable labels, and injects targeted rules to help distinguish them. This addresses a real weakness of vanilla top-K retrieval-augmented classification.

entry.title: AdaptNTK: Adaptive Uncertainty Quantification and Active Learning for Neural Network Potentials

author.name: Prajwal Ananth, Shuwen Yue

entry.summary: AdaptNTK is a single-model uncertainty quantification and active learning framework for neural network interatomic potentials, measuring uncertainty as regularized Mahalanobis distance in empirical neural tangent kernel feature space. It handles redundancy when assembling acquisition batches, a weakness of existing UQ methods.

entry.title: GenONet: A Generative operator Network for High-Resolution Precipitation Nowcasting

author.name: Mohammad Kian Golkar, Luciano Alves de Oliveira, Mohammad Khanjani

entry.summary: GenONet is a Spatio-Temporal U-DeepONet that uses a Deep Operator Network as the generator inside a GAN for precipitation nowcasting up to 3 hours, aiming for sharp, physically consistent long-horizon forecasts. It addresses the blurring failure of deep learning nowcasting models at longer lead times.

entry.title: MUGEN: Generating Unlearnable Graph Examples for Multiple Learning Tasks

author.name: Ziyan Liu, Chengshuai Zhao, Huan Liu

entry.summary: MUGEN is the first framework for generating unlearnable graph examples that jointly protect against multiple downstream tasks (node classification, graph classification, link prediction), addressing the problem that protection against one task leaves data learnable for others. It offers data-level defense against unauthorized representation learning on graph releases.

entry.title: Edge-Girth as a Structural Edge Feature for Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Lilian Marey, Charlotte Laclau

entry.summary: Proposes edge-girth and its multiplicity (length and count of shortest cycles through an edge) as structural edge features for GNNs, avoiding the need to commit to a fixed subgraph size as in triangle or cycle counts. This strengthens message passing beyond the 1-Weisfeiler-Leman limit in a data-agnostic way.

entry.title: A Dataset for Modeling Iterative Problem-Solving

author.name: Fagun Patel, Sang T. Truong, Duc Q. Nguyen, Kazunori Fukuhara, Benjamin W. Domingue, Sanmi Koyejo, Nick Haber

entry.summary: Contributes a dataset from programming courses for modeling iterative problem-solving, capturing how learners revise code across attempts with automated grading feedback, supporting prediction of improvement, plateau, and regression dynamics.

entry.title: Beyond Magnitude: Contrastive Routing for Modular Mixture-of-Experts

author.name: Nikolaos Xiros, Dimitrios Damianos, Maria-Eleni Zoumpoulidi, Leon Voukoutis, Vassilis Katsouros, Georgios Paraskevopoulos

entry.summary: Proposes the Contrastive Routing Mechanism (CoRM) for MoE models, scoring experts against an exponential moving average reference state rather than absolute magnitude, producing routing boundaries aligned with linguistic structure and better expert specialization.

entry.title: Separating Syntax from Language: A Mechanistic Account of Translation in Multilingual LLMs

author.name: Mikhail Sonkin, Tanja Baeumel, Daniil Gurgurov, Josef van Genabith, Simon Ostermann

entry.summary: Provides a mechanistic account of translation in multilingual LLMs showing output language production separates into syntax and surface language processes, using controlled multilingual datasets isolating word-order differences.

entry.title: How Correct Is Your Answer? A Semantic Correctness Framework for Open QA Evaluation

author.name: Elitsa Yotkova, Violeta Kastreva, Petar Velkov, Hristo Boyanov, Dimitar Dimitrov, Ivan Koychev, Preslav Nakov

entry.summary: Introduces a semantic correctness taxonomy of eight ordered classes for open-ended QA evaluation, an 8.8k-example benchmark (CAP-Correctness), and metrics separating verbose-but-correct answers from hallucination-contaminated ones.

entry.title: Sources of Truth: A Multi-Platform, Multilingual Audit of Citations in AI Mental Health Information Queries

author.name: Phuong Anh Nguyen, Jill Noorily, Matthew Flathers, Haruka Notsu, Laura Ospina-Pinillos, Tommy Nguyen, Samantha Clark, Aoife Keane, Grace Thompson, John Torous

entry.summary: Audits 15,942 citations from ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Google AI Overview across 20 mental health questions in seven languages, classifying source types with a validated deterministic classifier and finding the platforms surface poorly characterized source mixes.

entry.title: Beyond Blind Compliance: Benchmarking Task Verification in OCR Reasoning

author.name: Yue Zhou, Yuan Wu, Yi Chang

entry.summary: VeriOCRBench introduces 1,800 human-verified samples testing whether OCR-grounded MLLMs verify task executability (image premise, textual premise, question consistency) before answering, covering illegible text, contradictions, and nonexistent targets.

entry.title: SlideMix: Enhancing Whole Slide Image Analysis via Multimodal Shuffling

author.name: Chad Wong, Sicheng Chen, Tianyi Zhang, Enhui Chai, Yueming Jin, Zeyu Liu, Fei Xia

entry.summary: SlideMix is a model-agnostic multimodal augmentation framework for multiple-instance-learning whole-slide-image analysis, using a VLM-based region selector to preserve diagnostic relevance, slide context, and cross-scale structure during augmentation.

entry.title: ViTAL-X: Video-Text Alignment with Cross-Modal Temporal Edits

author.name: Sethuraman T V, Savya Khosla, Onkar Kishor Susladkar, Aditi Tiwari, Seoung Wug Oh, Kushal Kafle, Joon-Young Lee, Derek Hoiem, Simon Jenni

entry.summary: Introduces XTE-Bench revealing that video-language models adapted from CLIP struggle with basic temporal reasoning, and proposes Cross-Modal Temporal Edits, a self-supervised framework injecting precise temporal supervision via synchronized video-text transformations.

entry.title: BrainDiff: Longitudinal Report Generation for Multimodal Brain MRI

author.name: Krish Patel, Peirong Liu

entry.summary: BrainDiff is the first longitudinal vision-language system for brain MRI report generation, outperforming frontier general-purpose and single-study neuroimaging models on patient pairs and retaining 91 percent of entity-relation F1 on an external cross-hospital cohort.

entry.title: Do Satellites See Commuters? A Critical Benchmark of Vision Foundation Models

author.name: Ashiq Shukoor Iqbal, Wilson Wongso, Flora D. Salim

entry.summary: FTU-Seek uses frozen features from a pathology foundation model to select morphology-aware hard negatives for segmenting sparse functional tissue units like tertiary lymphoid structures and glands in whole-slide images. Targets the challenge of distinguishing rare structures from vast morphologically similar background.

entry.title: Training-Free Inpainting Across Domains with a Frozen Text-to-Image Diffusion Model

author.name: Zhenhuan Wang, Fengyi Yuan

entry.summary: Step-PI enables training-free conditional inpainting across three image domains with a frozen text-to-image diffusion model and one fixed controller configuration, combining known-region projection with boundary-interior latent feedback and a release schedule developed only on CelebA-HQ pilots.

entry.title: PredErase: Training-Free Object-and-Effect Removal with Predictive Latent Guidance

author.name: Waikit Xiu, Qiang Lu, Junbiao Chen, Xiying Li

entry.summary: PredErase performs training-free object-and-effect removal on frozen FLUX.2 by separating where Fill may rewrite pixels from what structure should occupy the hole, expanding the editable region to cover cast shadows and contact shading outside the instance mask using I-JEPA predictive latent guidance.

entry.title: ReFlowSET: Representation-Aligned Latent Flow Matching for SAR-to-EO Image Translation

author.name: Jeonghyeok Do, Seungchul Lee, Munchurl Kim

entry.summary: ReFlowSET is a conditional latent flow-matching framework for SAR-to-EO translation that selects its latent codec through a joint SAR-EO reconstruction audit rather than inheriting a natural-image-pretrained autoencoder, addressing codec-dependent round-trip fidelity.

entry.title: CQF-HMR: Continuous Quaternion Flows for Probabilistic 3D Human Mesh Recovery from a Single Image

author.name: Cuong Le, Bao-Long Tran, Pavlo Melnyk, Tahereh Dehdarirad, Bastian Wandt, M{\aa}rten Wadenb\"ack

entry.summary: CQF-HMR proposes probabilistic 3D human mesh recovery from a single image using quaternion-constrained continuous normalizing flows, generating SMPL-based hypotheses that respect the non-additive nature of joint rotations.

entry.title: Dotting the Eye: An Intent-Driven Image Retouching Agent for Visual Focus Enhancement

author.name: Chujie Qin, Zilong Zhang, Zewei Chang, Chunle Guo, Ruixing Wang, Tao Hu, Ming-Ming Cheng, Chongyi Li

entry.summary: EyeControl is an MLLM-driven agent with a diffusion-based retouching executor enabling intent-driven visual focus enhancement from weak user signals like a few clicks or coarse strokes, coordinating global and local adjustments to direct viewer attention naturally.

entry.title: S$^2$Prune: Spatially Structured Visual Token Pruning for Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Yuanyuan Jia, Shunpu Tang, Qianqian Yang

entry.summary: S2Prune observes that importance/redundancy-based visual token pruning produces spatial biases and may underperform uniform grid sampling, and proposes a training-free method guaranteeing spatial coverage while adapting density to local structure via Laplacian variation.

entry.title: ExBind: A Controlled Diagnostic Benchmark for Visual-to-Executable Correspondence

author.name: Ziqian Wang, Yuxiao Cheng, Tingxiong Xiao, Jinli Suo

entry.summary: ExBind isolates visual-to-executable correspondence as a controlled diagnostic layer between semantic localization and action execution, with representation-independent latent binding instances compiled into SVG, DOM, canvas, tree, graph, and table cases with deterministic reference mappings.

entry.title: Gaussian Core LoRA: Distribution-Aware Dynamic Adaptation for Broad Concept Erasure

author.name: Qinghui Gong, Xunlei Chen, Yu-Xuan Zhang, Hua Meng, Zhengchun Zhou

entry.summary: Gaussian Core LoRA improves concept erasure in text-to-image diffusion models by replacing static per-concept erasure directions with distribution-aware dynamic adaptation that handles multiple latent semantic prototypes within broad target concepts.

entry.title: PyDoseRT Proton: A GPU Pencil-Beam Engine with a Convolutional Residual-Correction Network for Fast Proton Dose Calculation

author.name: Lukas Zimmermann, Hermann Fuchs, Attila Simk\'o, Gerd Heilemann

entry.summary: Presents PyDoseRT Proton, a GPU-accelerated analytical pencil-beam engine for proton therapy dose calculation augmented by a 3D convolutional residual-correction network (RepVGG-U-Net) to approach Monte Carlo accuracy. The differentiable PyTorch physics engine allows gradient-based calibration of the double-Gaussian kernel, a nice hybrid of physics simulation and deep learning for radiotherapy.

entry.title: MultiGait: A Multi-Sensor Multi-Perspective Multi-Session Biometric Inference Benchmark and its Dataset

author.name: Julian Todt, Felix Morsbach, Philip Dissert, Thorsten Strufe

entry.summary: Introduces MultiGait, the first multi-sensor, multi-perspective, multi-session gait dataset with thermal, depth, and lidar sensors covering 199 individuals, designed to quantify privacy risks of smart-city sensing. It enables like-for-like comparisons of biometric inference risk across sensor types that were previously studied in isolation.

entry.title: Visual Attention Faithfulness in Vision-Language Models is Heterogeneous

author.name: Xurui Song, Weishi Wang, Zhongqi Yue, Kuluhan Binici, Tao Bai, Hongxin Shao, Daniel Dahlmeier, Jun Luo

entry.summary: EEG-VID is a task-guided latent predictive pretraining framework for EEG decoding under session and subject shifts, improving accuracy in 41 of 42 matched comparisons including all leave-one-subject-out settings, with gains up to 16 points. It demonstrates self-supervised-style pretraining benefits for neural decoding and assistive target selection. A strong applied neuroscience result.

entry.title: How Temporal Correlations Shape Memory in Linear Recurrent Neural Networks

author.name: Arnol Manuel Fokam, Fasseu Sieyondji Akpevwoghene, Edem Fiifi Dawson

entry.summary: Solves learning dynamics exactly for linear recurrent neural networks trained on correlated inputs, showing that input correlation lands entirely on the cost of keeping the past. It finds memory builds, overshoots, and is partially removed during training, with correlation reshaping the trajectory of learning and not just its endpoint.

entry.title: Overfitting Mitigation via Singular Value Decomposition in Minimum Bayes Risk Decoding

author.name: Riza Setiawan Soetedjo, Yusuke Sakai, Hidetaka Kamigaito, Katsuhiko Hayashi, Taro Watanabe

entry.summary: SVD-MBR frames the pairwise utility matrix in Minimum Bayes Risk decoding as a noisy signal, applying low-rank SVD approximation to decouple true consensus from metric noise and mitigate metric overfitting in text generation.

entry.title: InSight: A Benchmark for Agentic Claim Verification in Interactive Visualizations

author.name: Maeve Hutchinson, Syed Mahbubul Huq, Mohammad Albinhassan, Radu Jianu, Aidan Slingsby, Pranava Madhyastha

entry.summary: InSight is a benchmark for agentic claim verification over interactive visualizations, with 21,349 claims from human-authored narratives grounded in interactive web-based environments where evidence is occluded or conditionally revealed.

entry.title: On the Design Fundamentals of Pixel Text Representation Learning

author.name: Chaohao Yuan, Ruifeng Yuan, Zhuoxu Huang, Yu Rong, Hong Cheng, Hou Pong Chan, Chenghao Xiao

entry.summary: Systematic controlled ablations identifying four critical design components for pixel-based text representation learning: variable resolution/font sizes, natural image-text pairs for grounding, layout-aware rendering against shortcuts, and multilingual visual text handling.

entry.title: A Glance Is All You Need: Single-Pass Fine-Grained Image Captioning with SimLoss

author.name: Suryaansh Jain, Rahasya Barkur, Vishal G, Ryan Rossi, Franck Dernoncourt, Jack Wang, Koustava Goswami, Nedim Lipka, Puneet Mathur, Samyadeep Basu, Seunghyun Yoon

entry.summary: SimLoss is a reference-free embedding-space objective enabling single-pass fine-grained image captioning by aligning projected hidden states with frozen image embeddings, avoiding the latency of multi-stage generate-verify-rewrite pipelines.

entry.title: Geometry-aware Latent Autoregressive Generative Model for PDEs in Complex Domains

author.name: Zi Wang, Minghui Xu, Tapan Mukerji

entry.summary: GeoLAMP is a geometry-aware latent autoregressive generative model for solving PDEs in complex, tortuous domains relevant to energy and chemical engineering. It uses a dual-encoder graph architecture to capture topology and fine-scale geometry, plus causal self-attention with flow matching for latent temporal dynamics. A solid scientific-ML contribution.

entry.title: Towards Effective Structured Context Modeling for Conversational Recommender Systems via Dual-node Monte Carlo Tree Search

author.name: Jincheng Zhang, Chen Huang, Wenqiang Lei, See-Kiong Ng, Yang Deng

entry.summary: DREAMS is a tree-structured context-modeling framework for conversational recommender systems that uses MCTS-based elicitation nodes to infer latent preferences and LLM-refined exploitation nodes to produce structured retrieval queries. It explicitly captures preference evolution across turns. A solid CRS contribution with a principled search structure.

entry.title: VOIM: Training-Free Open-Vocabulary 3D Instance Mapping for RGB-D and Monocular SLAM

author.name: Sangmin Song, Sarath Kodagoda, Marc G. Carmichael, Karthick Thiyagarajan, Amal Gunatilake, Kelly Prentice, Jodi Martin

entry.summary: VOIM is a training-free voxel-grounded instance manager that builds open-vocabulary 3D instance maps from RGB-D or monocular RGB, deferring label and instance decisions until per-voxel evidence accumulates across views. It shows the mapping stage, not the perception models, drives results across four perception configurations on ScanNet++. A robust systems contribution for embodied perception.

entry.title: Do LLMs Know Your Neighborhood? Auditing LLM Priors for Neighborhood-Level Mobility Prediction and Structural Alignment

author.name: Saad Mohammad Abrar, Eesha Kurella, Arnav Dadarya, Naman Awasthi, Kazi Tasnim Zinat, Vanessa Frias-Martinez

entry.summary: Audits zero-shot LLM priors for neighborhood-level mobility prediction across four US metropolitan areas using Census Block Group outcomes, comparing LLM predictions to supervised baselines. The work probes whether LLMs implicitly encode fine-grained human mobility structure relevant to urban planning and public health.

entry.title: VATO: A Vortex-Force-Aware Transformer Operator for Unsteady Separated Aerofoil Flows

author.name: Xingxin Yang, Zhan Zhang, Yichen Li, Juan Li

entry.summary: VATO couples the Vortex Force Map method to a geometry-aware neural operator for predicting unsteady separated aerofoil flows, adding training-only supervision of local force-contribution fields (VATO-S) at no inference cost. It targets the flow regions that dominate aerodynamic loads, which standard field-level surrogates ignore.

entry.title: Verdict Instability of OOD Scores under Reference Resampling

author.name: Donghoon Lee, Shinjin Kang

entry.summary: Studies verdict instability of post-hoc OOD detectors: how scores would change under resampling of the finite reference set. It derives a closed-form bootstrap standard deviation showing instability depends on within-class dispersion along the query direction divided by the square root of class reference count, identifiable only under class imbalance.

entry.title: Conditional Flow Matching for ML-Based Inverse Design Problems

author.name: Juliana Felder, Milad Habibi, Soheyl Massoudi, Mark Fuge

entry.summary: Adds conditional flow matching to the EngiOpt framework for engineering inverse design and compares it against conditional diffusion and conditional GANs on structural and thermal benchmarks using the same downstream optimization pipeline. Flow matching offers a middle ground between one-pass GAN sampling and iterative diffusion.

entry.title: Replicating TRACE: A Practitioner's Guide to Its Threshold and Particle Budget

author.name: Alex Chadyuk, Alicia Zhang, Roy Kucukates

entry.summary: An independent replication of TRACE, which extracts causal graphs over event types from pretrained autoregressive models via thresholding conditional mutual information estimates. The replication confirms headline F1 results and provides a practitioner's guide showing the optimal threshold is pinned to the ground-truth margin rather than any universal constant.

entry.title: One-Layer Transformer Provably Learns Multiclass One-Nearest Neighbor in Context

author.name: Skanda Athreya, Yutong Wang

entry.summary: Extends the equivalence between one-layer transformers and nearest-neighbor classifiers to the multiclass case using simplex encoding, showing a one-layer transformer with an argmax head behaves exactly as a one-nearest-neighbor classifier. This closes a gap left by prior work that relied on non-standard rounding-based heads.

entry.title: TRIAGE: Three-level Routing and Intelligent Agent Guidance for Efficient Execution

author.name: Ruocan Wei

entry.summary: TRIAGE reduces token consumption in ReAct-style LLM agents via three-level routing that reuses historical execution trajectories, abstracting them into reusable skills via Trajectory-as-a-Skill. Queries are classified into direct reuse, skill substitution, or full reasoning, realizing experience-as-a-service.

entry.title: It Takes Two to Match: Co-Evolving Generative Retriever with Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Runpeng Dai, Kaili Huang, Changsung Kang, Ciya Liao

entry.summary: CoGR trains LLMs with RL to construct retrieval representations on both query and item sides, producing compact keyword sets matched via inverted index, co-evolving the generative components for compatibility with keyword-based retrieval infrastructure.

entry.title: Citing Less Critically: LLMs Reshape the Rhetoric and Reach of Scientific Citation

author.name: Yixuan Liu, Lin Chen, Zhuoqi Liu, Jianglin Lu, Dakota Murray

entry.summary: Uses a masked-citation task to compare human and LLM citation behavior, finding LLMs cite less critically, with shifts in rhetorical intent and cited-author social distance measured via a 20-million-edge coauthorship network.

entry.title: SCAFFOLD: A Large-Scale Structured Dataset of Computer Science Research Figures with Diagram QA and Chain-of-Thought Reasoning Traces

author.name: Ranjit Raut, Aarav Subedi, Sagun Rai, Sudan Jha

entry.summary: SCAFFOLD is a large-scale structured dataset of computer science research figures paired with captions, context, question-answer pairs, and chain-of-thought reasoning traces, built from arXiv papers. It targets training vision-language models to understand architecture diagrams, flowcharts, and pipeline schematics. Fills a genuine dataset gap for diagram understanding.

entry.title: Asymmetries in Spontaneous and Instructed Deception

author.name: Josiah Luikham

entry.summary: This single-author study examines the relationship between instructed and spontaneous (uninstructed) deception in Llama-3.1-70B-Instruct using direction geometry, cross-setting classifiers, and cross-setting steering. It finds the two share a direction component (cosine ~0.5) with asymmetries in transfer: spontaneous-trained classifiers detect instructed deception better than vice versa. Relevant to interpretability-based deception monitoring.

entry.title: Flawed in Nature, Perfect through Evolution

author.name: J. M. Diederik Kruijssen (Allora Foundation)

entry.summary: This paper shows that deliberately mutating model coefficients away from optimality within a swarm of ML models can sustain performance under distribution drift, mimicking natural selection by maintaining diversity. The statistical-physics framing of evolving model ensembles is the main novelty. It speaks to the persistent problem of model degradation under data drift.

entry.title: Counterfactual Fragility Certificates: Exposing High-Confidence Brittleness under Structured Evidence Failure

author.name: Filippo Cenacchi, Longbing Cao, Runze Yang

entry.summary: Counterfactual Fragility Certificates provide a recomputable audit object that traces what evidence-failure trajectory would make a high-confidence tabular prediction lose support. Unlike scalar uncertainty scores, CFCs answer structured audit questions under declared failure protocols. A thoughtful addition to trustworthy decision systems.

entry.title: (V)LMs generalize beyond surface co-occurrence: Evidence from cross-modal number agreement

author.name: Zach Studdiford, Kanishka Misra

entry.summary: Using cross-modal number agreement, the authors teach VLMs new noun pairs via added embeddings and test whether grammatical number generalizes beyond surface co-occurrence when cues are restricted to the visual modality. The results indicate VLMs learn abstractions rather than only lexical co-occurrence patterns. A careful linguistic-probing contribution.

entry.title: Does Reasoning Mitigate Backdoor Attacks? A Neuro-Symbolic Perspective

author.name: Marco Antonio Corallo, Andrea Agiollo, Mauro Conti, Alberto Giaretta

entry.summary: The paper argues that neuro-symbolic models are not robust by design and investigates whether reasoning mitigates backdoor attacks, treating the neural-symbolic integration layer as a potential attack entry point. It provides an initial adversarial analysis of NeSy systems. Early but needed work on an underexamined attack surface.

entry.title: Exploring Collaboration between a language and a non-language agent

author.name: Harini S I, Somesh Singh, Yaman K Singla, Rajiv Ratn Shah, David Doermann, Balaji Krishnamurthy

entry.summary: LLAMIA-Bench introduces six collaborative chess tasks to test whether verbalization, the compression of a non-language agent's continuous representations into text, is a bottleneck when LLMs orchestrate specialized non-LLM agents. The results quantify where LLM-as-orchestrator integration breaks down. A neat testbed for heterogeneous agent collaboration.

entry.title: Agentic programs: an emerging form of scientific software in computational materials science

author.name: Yunsung Lim, Haekwan Jeon, Jaesun Kim, Jisu Kim, Seungwu Han

entry.summary: The paper argues that LLM agent harnesses enable a new form of scientific software, agentic programs, combining deterministic algorithms with bounded LLM judgment, task-specific verification, and episodic maturation, illustrated by DeMARS for constructing atomistic models of disordered crystal structures. A useful conceptual contribution for AI-for-science methodology.

entry.title: Semi-Supervised Virtual Staining via Morphology Preservation and Histopathological Realism Constraints

author.name: Baoshun Wang, Weiping Lin, Linwu Wang, Yihuang Hu, Baptiste Magnier, Liansheng Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a semi-supervised virtual staining framework that jointly uses limited paired data and abundant unpaired source images, with morphology preservation and histopathological realism constraints to prevent training collapse. It reduces dependence on expensive strictly paired and registered training data.

entry.title: Inspicio: Open-Vocabulary, LLM-Based Sense Retrieval for Historical Languages

author.name: Michele Ciletti

entry.summary: Presents Inspicio, an open-vocabulary retrieval pipeline linking tokens in historical and low-resource languages to Open English WordNet synsets without requiring a source-language sense inventory, using an instruction-tuned LLM to produce translations and candidate senses. It removes core assumptions of standard word sense disambiguation.

entry.title: A Network Science Perspective on Evaluating Deep Graph Generative Models

author.name: Tianrui Mao, Abele Malan, Megha Khosla, Lydia Chen, Huijuan Wang

entry.summary: Evaluates deep graph generative models from a network science perspective, assessing whether synthetic networks can substitute for privacy-restricted real social contact networks in epidemic modeling. It compares them against classical configuration models on topological fidelity.

entry.title: Hints Help But Do They Teach? Evaluating Skills Transfer in Code Generation

author.name: Will Badr

entry.summary: Tests whether hints that rescue failing code generations convey missing information or merely steer models toward solutions they could already produce, using executable evaluation on HumanEval+ and MBPP+ with small open models. Unhinted resampling recovers most relevant-hint rescues, suggesting hints often help via steering rather than new knowledge.

entry.title: Quantum Sparse Autoencoders for Q-Matrix Estimation in Cognitive Diagnosis

author.name: Arif Hassan Zidan, Yi Pan, Bowen Guo, Xiang Li, Yu Bao, Yingfeng Wang, Tianming Liu, Wei Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces a quantum sparse autoencoder (QSAE) for estimating Q-matrices in cognitive diagnosis, claimed as the first application of quantum machine learning to educational data mining. It embeds binary response vectors into a quantum circuit and compresses them into a sparse latent representation mapped to skill-item matrices. The work is conceptually novel but sits in a niche application area with limited immediate practical impact given current quantum hardware limits.

entry.title: A Certificate-Producing Cascade for Equational Implication: The SAIR EQT2 Stage 2 Solver

author.name: Haobo Ma, Wenlin Zhang, Manuel Israel C\'azares

entry.summary: Presents a cascade solver for the SAIR equational theories challenge that classifies magma identity implications and returns Lean-verifiable certificates for either verdict. It combines finite-model search, algebraic coefficient tests, and a proof-producing superposition procedure with search kept outside the trusted base.

entry.title: TEIDAN: A Multilingual Multiparty Dialogue Corpus

author.name: Taiga Mori, Koji Inoue, Mikey Elmers, Divesh Lala, Tatsuya Kawahara

entry.summary: TEIDAN is a multilingual multimodal corpus of Japanese and English three-party face-to-face conversations recorded with individual microphones, microphone arrays, and cameras, providing IPU-based transcripts for spontaneous triadic discussion.

entry.title: Subword Segmental BabyLMs: Learning to Tokenise for Sample-Efficient Pretraining

author.name: Francois Meyer

entry.summary: BabyLM 2026 submission developing subword segmental language models (SubSegGPT, SubSegDeBERTa) that learn tokenization jointly with pretraining, achieving strong sample-efficient results in the Strict tracks.

entry.title: Ready to Speak: Aligning LLMs for TTS-Friendly Text Generation

author.name: Thibaut Thonet, Jos Rozen, Laurent Besacier

entry.summary: Frames TTS-friendly text generation as a preference alignment problem for LLMs, contributing two preference datasets (CORA, Recipe), an evaluation suite combining heuristics, TTS-to-ASR pipelines, and MUSHRA listening tests, and aligned models producing speech-optimized text directly.

entry.title: SDARE-Bench: Evaluating Large Language Models on Conversational Stigma Detection and Response in Dyadic and Group Dialogue

author.name: Stephanie Fong, Yiwen Jiang, Zimu Wang, Hongxi Yang, Yaling Shen, Hiu Weh Naomi Chow, Heung Ying Lai, Xiangyu Zhao, Qingyang Xu, Zhongxing Xu, Jiahe Liu, Guilherme C. Oliveira, Vincent Lee, Zongyuan Ge, Dominic Dwyer

entry.summary: SDARE-Bench is the first scenario-based benchmark for stigma detection and response in LLMs, with 1,138 dyadic and 1,388 group dialogue queries; across eight LLMs, stigma identification is poor, especially in group dialogue.

entry.title: Puppeteer: Object-Grounded Posture-Aware Co-Speech Gesture Generation

author.name: Vida Adeli, Soroush Mehraban, Jacob Rommann, Harrison Sanborn, Cole Clifford, Babak Taati

entry.summary: Puppeteer generates co-speech gestures with a posture-aware, object-grounded causal diffusion model operating over temporally ordered latent primitives, capturing correlations between body motion and surrounding physical space.

entry.title: GenScale: A Benchmark for Relative Object Scale in Image Generation and Editing

author.name: Lingxiao Li, Max Whitton, Ledell Wu, Boqing Gong

entry.summary: GenScale is a benchmark for relative object scale in image generation and editing with 900 entries and 1,643 pairwise scale relations, plus a human-calibrated ordinal judge and Rescale, a post-processing agent for localized scale correction.

entry.title: Streaming4D: Accelerate 4D World Models via Block-wise Video Generation and Incremental Reconstruction

author.name: Xiaoyan Liu, Jiaxin Liu, Kangrui Li, Sifan Zhou

entry.summary: Streaming4D couples block-wise autoregressive video generation with incremental 3D reconstruction, triggering reconstruction per completed block so the world representation evolves online with generation, reducing interaction latency for 4D world models.

entry.title: Beyond Landmark Extraction: A Framework for Robust Geometric Feature Construction in Structured Image Classification

author.name: Saravana Mauree, Sakshi Arya

entry.summary: Argues that structured image classification research overemphasizes classifier choice and instead builds a framework for constructing robust geometric features capturing spatial relationships between semantic parts. Targets gesture recognition, facial expression analysis, and medical imaging where interpretable part-level geometry matters more than raw pixels.

entry.title: EarthLD: Towards Unified Open-World Landslide Understanding via Vision-Language Guided Diffusion Models

author.name: Yuanchao Su, Lianru Gao, Mengying Jiang, Jiangyi Chen, Jiaxin Cheng, Yicong Zhou

entry.summary: EarthLD formulates open-world landslide understanding as a diffusion process guided by vision-language signals, unifying recognition, mapping, and trigger interpretation with probabilistic inference of presence, extent, and pixel boundaries.

entry.title: Efficient and Robust Absolute Pose Estimation via Gravity-Prior-Driven Transformation Decoupling and Pose Refinement

author.name: Hu Cao, Qianyi Yang, Xinyi Li, Jiong Liu, Yinlong Liu, Alois Knoll

entry.summary: Proposes a gravity-prior-driven transformation decoupling strategy that splits 6-DoF absolute pose estimation into simpler subproblems, improving robustness and efficiency for robotic applications plagued by correspondence mismatches.

entry.title: ReBridge-Flow: Re-Coupling Posterior Bridges in Flow Matching for Image Restoration

author.name: Jiaqi Zhang, Yiqi Wang, Hongjie Wu, Bohan Guo, Xinan Wang, Zichen Luo, Taotao Cai, Zhi Chen, Mingkai Zheng

entry.summary: ReBridge-Flow addresses disruption of source-clean endpoint coupling in flow-matching image restoration by decoding local endpoints and re-coupling them with measurement information via clean-side anchoring.

entry.title: EvoGS: Modeling Deformation Evolution for Dynamic Gaussian Splatting

author.name: Wei Dong, Shahram Shirani, Jun Chen, Han Zhou

entry.summary: EvoGS models Gaussian deformation in dynamic 3D Gaussian Splatting as a temporal evolution process with persistent per-Gaussian states, extrapolation from history, and adaptively weighted MLP corrections, improving robustness to large or abrupt motions over per-timestamp deformation MLPs.

entry.title: Does This Moment Justify the Recommendation? Counterfactual Behavior-Grounded Evidence Retrieval for Personalized Video Recommendation

author.name: Xin Liu

entry.summary: Studies counterfactual behavior-grounded evidence retrieval for personalized video recommendation, separating where personalized evidence occurs from whether it exists, and introduces CBGER-10K with 5,000 controlled factual-counterfactual pairs to test whether predictions respond consistently when evidence is replaced.

entry.title: Fleets Need a Context Plane: Rethinking Cooperative Perception for Autonomous Drones

author.name: Liangkai Liu, Xiaoxiao Wu

entry.summary: MeshSplatBench is a unified benchmark for triangle-based neural rendering that evaluates methods from native optimization through deployment in production game engines, with a standardized protocol reproducing published results within 0.8%. It addresses the gap between custom research renderers and practical deployability on rasterization hardware.

entry.title: Mapping global methane emissions from space with deep learning

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Google Research describes applying deep learning to satellite data to map global methane emissions from space, advancing climate monitoring at planetary scale. This represents applied AI for climate with direct policy and industrial relevance.

entry.title: GeoPAR: Large-Scale Multi-Agent Combinatorial Optimization with Geometry-Guided Parallel Autoregressive Learning

author.name: Wenjian Wu, Zesheng Jia, Jiaying Tang, Benyuan Yang, Jin Wang

entry.summary: GeoPAR is a geometry-guided parallel autoregressive reinforcement learning framework for large-scale multi-agent combinatorial optimization, combining projection-window sparse geometry with conflict-aware action handling. It improves scalability over prior parallel autoregressive solvers. A competent neural-combinatorial-optimization contribution.

entry.title: Neural means and kernel corrections for operator learning

author.name: Yitzchak Shmalo

entry.summary: Combines neural network means with exact Matern kernel regressions of residuals and learned features for operator learning, evaluated on structural mechanics and OCO-2 radiative transfer emulation benchmarks. The hybrid matches or improves published baselines, notably in low-data regimes.

entry.title: Polish ModernBERT: The Long and Short of Polish Language Understanding

author.name: Micha{\l} Pere{\l}kiewicz, S{\l}awomir Dadas, Rafa{\l} Po\'swiata, Ma{\l}gorzata Gr\k{e}bowiec

entry.summary: Releases Polish ModernBERT, a family of four Polish encoders at Base/Large scales with 512-token and 8K context variants, plus a long-context benchmark, achieving the best overall performance among Polish encoders across 30 tasks.

entry.title: Instance-Guided Report Anchoring for Text-Free 3D Abnormality Segmentation in Chest CT

author.name: Zhenyu Bu, Haoyan Ding, Chushu Shen, Xinyuan Zheng, Peiyu Duan, Xueqi Guo, Sepehr Farhand, Yoshihisa Shinagawa, Gerardo Hermosillo, Chaowei Wu

entry.summary: IGRA is a model-agnostic module that preserves instance-to-report-finding correspondence for training 3D chest CT abnormality segmentation without inference-time text, leveraging routinely generated radiology reports as weak dense supervision.

entry.title: HarmoCore: Functional Latent Diffusion for Sparse Reconstruction of Oscillatory Wave Fields

author.name: Lihao Chen, Xinyu Zhang, Panqi Chen, Lei Cheng, Ting Zhang, Jianlong Li, Shikai Fang

entry.summary: HarmoCore places a generative prior in a compact, structured, complex-valued wave-field latent using functional Tucker cores, for sparse reconstruction of oscillatory wave fields from few sensors. It addresses failures of real-valued, pixel-space diffusion approaches on highly oscillatory complex fields and scales better to 3D.

entry.title: Frozen Cores Need Task Signal: Fisher-Whitened Cross-Covariance for Low-Resource LLM Adaptation

author.name: Wentao Ye, Zhanming Shen, Zhiqing Xiao, Yao Ding, Haobo Wang, Gang Chen

entry.summary: FCCA addresses low-resource parameter-efficient fine-tuning under severe trainable-state budgets via frozen-core adaptation: calibration fixes bases for each weight matrix and only a small r-by-r core is optimized. It estimates signed input-error cross-covariance, whitens it with diagonal Fisher moments, and derives stable core coordinates.

entry.title: SAGE: Subpopulation-Aware Generative Enhancement for Mitigating Spurious Correlations

author.name: Yiming Luo, Rongqiang Zhao, Jie Liu

entry.summary: SAGE mitigates spurious correlations without group labels by using subpopulation-aware generative enhancement to synthesize diverse minority-group examples rather than upsampling existing instances, avoiding overfitting from repetition. It targets the common setting where spurious attributes are unavailable.

entry.title: Let Confidence Change, Not the Prediction: Prediction-Preserving Repair for Post-hoc Calibration

author.name: Daehwan Kim, Haejun Chung, Ikbeom Jang

entry.summary: Observes that multiclass post-hoc calibrators can silently change top-1 predictions and proposes CORD, a post-fit adapter that repairs the calibrated probability vector to exactly preserve the original argmax while adjusting confidence. It also introduces the Top-1 Prediction Change Rate as a diagnostic metric.

entry.title: When Does Online Adaptation Pay on the Edge? A Leakage-Free Evaluation of Warmup, Learning-Rate Selection, and Resource Trade-offs for Time-Series Forecasting

author.name: Takumi Fujimoto, Hiroaki Nishi

entry.summary: Evaluates online adaptation for edge time-series forecasting under a leakage-free streaming protocol, identifying evaluation biases: warmup budget changes estimated adaptation benefit by 3-18.8 points across settings, and optimizer comparisons at shared default learning rates mislead. It provides guidance on when online adaptation genuinely pays on the edge.

entry.title: Unmasking Face Embeddings: Reading, Rendering and Naming with Foundation Models

author.name: Fizza Rubab, Yiying Tong, Arun Ross

entry.summary: Explores making face recognition embeddings interoperable with foundation models, enabling reading, rendering, and naming of face embeddings, raising privacy-relevant questions about semantic exposure of biometric representations.

entry.title: Learning What to Retain: Gated-Memory Routing for Efficient Collaboration in Multi-Agent LLM Systems

author.name: Rakibul Hasan Rajib, Mengxing Zheng, Qian Lou

entry.summary: Gated-Memory Routing addresses execution-history overload in multi-agent LLM systems by maintaining a compact gated memory state that captures useful progress without accumulating redundant context. It improves orchestration accuracy while controlling cost compared to routing from query alone or from full histories. Useful for scaling multi-agent collaboration efficiently.

entry.title: Cleaner Speech, Weaker Generalization: Revisiting Pitt-Derived Benchmarks for Alzheimer's Disease Detection

author.name: Luqi Sun, Shreeram Suresh Chandra, Lin Zhang, You-Jin Li, Brian MacWhinney, Yu Tsao, Emily Mower Provost, Berrak Sisman

entry.summary: The paper revisits whether common preprocessing steps on the Pitt Corpus, such as speech enhancement and demographic balancing, actually help speech-based Alzheimer's detection. It finds these transformations can weaken cross-dataset generalization, cautioning the field about benchmark curation choices. A useful negative result for clinical speech ML.

entry.title: Operational Regimes in Non-Convex Optimization: A Multiplier-Based Taxonomy

author.name: Seyed Mohsen Kazemi, Ali Movaghar, Shaahin hessabi

entry.summary: The paper introduces a taxonomy of constrained non-convex optimization based on Lagrange multiplier signatures at KKT points, showing a normalized multiplier vector partitions dual space into five operational regimes across eight algorithm families. A unifying game-theoretic interpretation underlies the classification. Ambitious theory contribution.

entry.title: HiveTraceGuard-Pro: A Compact Generative Guardrail for Prompt Injection, Jailbreaks, and Adversarial Obfuscation

author.name: Nikita Oblakov, Sabrina Sadiekh, Evgeniy Kokuykin

entry.summary: Presents HiveTraceGuard-Pro, a 0.6B generative guardrail LoRA-tuned from Qwen3-0.6B, trained bilingually in Russian and English with obfuscation transforms, and evaluated against thirty-four other guards on nineteen benchmarks. It fills an evidence gap on Russian prompt injection and obfuscation.

entry.title: Generative artificial intelligence for reliable mechanistic reasoning for corrosion

author.name: Bharath M N, R K Singh Raman, Alankar Alankar

entry.summary: Presents a domain-adapted retrieval-augmented generation framework for mechanistic corrosion reasoning, fine-tuning three open-weight 7-8B models on expert-verified corrosion knowledge. It targets safety-critical materials engineering where retrieval accuracy and mechanistically defensible explanations both matter.

entry.title: CRAD: Class-wise Reliability-Aware Distillation for Decentralized Heterogeneous Federated Learning

author.name: Baraa Bilbeisi, Mengchen Fan, Baocheng Geng, Qing Tian

entry.summary: CRAD builds decentralized federated learning via knowledge distillation, where clients distill from peers' soft predictions evaluated on their own local data, removing requirements of identical architectures, central servers, or public datasets. It adds class-wise reliability-aware distillation for heterogeneous, non-IID settings.

entry.title: Phrase-Localized Language-Contrastive Guidance: Training-Free Localized Accent Control for Code-Switching Text-to-Speech

author.name: Che Hyun Lee, Sangkwon Park, Donghun Kang, Dongwook Lee, Youngho Cho, Heeseung Kim, Sungroh Yoon

entry.summary: Proposes a training-free inference framework that restores native accent to code-switched phrases in TTS by applying per-region language-contrastive guidance, with phrase boundaries located via self-attention probing without external alignment.

entry.title: When Modality Gap Reduction Fails: Prediction-Level Hubness in CLIP

author.name: Shota Sato, Hajime Kiyama, Tosho Hirasawa, Mamoru Komachi

entry.summary: Shows that reducing the CLIP modality gap does not reliably improve zero-shot accuracy because gap correction can concentrate predictions on a few classes (prediction-level hubness), analyzed through decision margins and analytically tractable linear correction.

entry.title: CaRL-EM: Cost-Aware Reinforcement Learning for Entity Matching with LLMs

author.name: Chaohui Guo, Michel Klein, Zhisheng Huang

entry.summary: CaRL-EM formulates LLM-based entity matching with candidate sets as a cost-aware sequential decision problem, training an RL controller to adaptively choose among Match/Compare/Select/Decide operators to balance accuracy and inference cost.

entry.title: Where Should Experience Live? Hierarchical Hebbian Memory for Continual Vision Transformers

author.name: Mohammed Yusuf Mujawar, Noorbakhsh Amiri Golilarz

entry.summary: Proposes a three-level Hierarchical Hebbian Memory (working, episodic, semantic) with a learned controller and causal read-before-write lifecycle for continual vision transformers, evaluated on Omniglot and CORe50 with Swin-Tiny backbones.

entry.title: Candidate-Expanding Routing with Permutation-Stabilized Experts for Mixed-Format Medical VQA

author.name: Hai-Dang Nguyen, Huy-Hieu Pham

entry.summary: Addresses mixed-format medical VQA with an answer-text memory, a permutation-stabilized vision-language expert, and a sparse candidate-expanding router that treats expert top-2 as a routable candidate, improving router accuracy from 88.95% to 91.73% on a 1,403-case retrospective analysis.

entry.title: Conditional Flow Matching for Cross-Field MRI Harmonisation

author.name: Baris Imre, Aram Salehi, Levente Baljer, Andrew Webb, Marius Staring, Efe Ilicak

entry.summary: Formulates cross-field brain-MRI harmonization across five field strengths and three contrasts as conditional flow matching between registered source and target slices, trained from only three paired subjects via staged degradation-bridge pretraining for a challenge task.

entry.title: Low-Quality Face Recognition using Center Aligned Representations and Local Margin Constraints

author.name: Vedat Can Dilaver, Benjamin S. Riggan

entry.summary: Proposes a unified framework for low-quality face recognition combining center-aligned representations and local margin constraints to match degraded probe images against low-quality gallery imagery without sacrificing high-quality generalization.

entry.title: P-PatchDiff: Progressive Patch Diffusion Models for Low-light Image Enhancement

author.name: Ruoyu Guo, Haonan Zhong, Maurice Pagnucco, Yang Song

entry.summary: P-PatchDiff proposes progressive patch diffusion for low-light image enhancement, dynamically selecting patch sizes to balance image-level brightness context against computational cost and ensuring locally enhanced patches remain visually coherent.

entry.title: Different Changes Require Different Reasoning: Change-Type-Specialized Experts for Robust Change Captioning

author.name: Jiyoung Park, InJae Oh, Jung Uk Kim

entry.summary: MEDIC introduces change-type-aware change captioning with type-specialized memory experts that dynamically retrieve type-relevant visual patterns, recognizing that different change types require distinct reasoning processes.

entry.title: Agentic Multimodal Models for Environmental Hyperspectral Unmixing

author.name: Micha{\l} Cholewa, Luca Ciampi, Nicola Messina, Przemys{\l}aw G{\l}omb, Giuseppe Amato

entry.summary: Introduces an algorithm-agnostic agentic framework where a large vision-language model iteratively refines outputs of conventional hyperspectral unmixing pipelines through grounding and diagnosis rather than replacing the numerical algorithms.

entry.title: Scene Graph-based Driving Scenario Extraction for Automotive Egocentric Datasets

author.name: Stefan Ramdhan, Kyanna Dagenais, Vera Pantelic, Victor Bandur, Mark Lawford

entry.summary: Presents a method for extracting driving scenarios from egocentric automotive datasets by converting sensor data and HD maps into scene graph sequences, then using Linear Temporal Logic specifications with an off-the-shelf model checker to locate scenario instances. Enables scenario-based coverage analysis of automated-driving datasets without manual labeling.

entry.title: Aquarium Security and Other Organisational Priors

author.name: hal2k

entry.summary: This post raises the concern that consumer chat data used for training (per 2026 opt-out policies at Anthropic and OpenAI) may contain credentials and security details, letting models learn organizational security priors across many firms and potentially enabling semi-autonomous attacks. It outlines where in the training pipeline such data could enter and where mitigations could be applied.

entry.title: A Human-AI Theorem Connecting Spontaneous and Field-Induced Mechanisms of Collective Behavior in One Dimension

author.name: Weiguo Yin

entry.summary: The paper documents an AI-generated scientific hypothesis outside a human collaborator's active hypothesis space, realized as a theorem connecting spontaneous and field-induced collective behavior in one-dimensional O(n)-vector chains. It is both a statistical physics result and a case study in human-AI co-discovery. An unusual and interesting data point for AI-for-science.

entry.title: Risk-Aware Decision-Making for Autonomous Overtaking: A World Model-Based Mixture-of-Experts Framework

author.name: Yongzhi Liu, Sunan Zhang, Jinchang Xu, Jiawei Wang, Yushu Qiu, Chen Lv, Weichao Zhuang

entry.summary: WM-RMoE proposes a world-model-based Mixture-of-Experts framework for risk-aware autonomous overtaking, using learned latent dynamics for parallel multi-step rollouts so risk assessment captures long-horizon propagation rather than implicit value estimates. Targets the locally-safe-but-globally-risky failure of standard safe RL. Solid domain contribution.

entry.title: Restrict, Don't Retrain: Inference-Time VLM Guidance for Zero-Shot Aerial Segmentation

author.name: Teresa DiMeola, Charles Walter, Hong Xiao

entry.summary: The paper uses a consumer-GPU VLM to provide inference-time guidance for zero-shot aerial segmentation with frozen foundation models, producing structured, auditable evidence without retraining. It improves segmentation of small, safety-relevant objects in satellite imagery. Practical for global-welfare applications like flood and crop mapping.

entry.title: DeSyR: A Decoupled Symbolic Recovery Framework with PINN-Guided Structure Search and Physics-Informed Coefficient Refinement

author.name: Pancheng Niu, Jun Guo, Qiaolin He, Jingcai Guo, Yanchao Shi

entry.summary: DeSyR is a decoupled framework for symbolic recovery of differential equations, using a physics-informed neural network to guide topology search and then refining coefficients solely from the governing equation and constraints. It includes theory on teacher-error inheritance when imperfect neural teachers guide symbolic discovery.

entry.title: Manifold-Aware General Coded Computing for Straggler-Resilient Distributed Computing

author.name: Parsa Moradi, Mohammad Ali Maddah-Ali

entry.summary: Proposes manifold-aware general coded computing for straggler-resilient distributed computing, arguing coded-computing schemes should preserve and exploit intrinsic data structure rather than compress it away as in source coding. The design leverages the fact that ML computations are precisely meant to exploit data structure.

entry.title: Contribution-Aware Bandwidth Allocation for Multimodal Split Learning

author.name: Iason Ofeidis, Leandros Tassiulas

entry.summary: Makes inter-modality allocation an explicit decision in multimodal split learning: instead of dividing the uplink budget in proportion to activation dimension, bandwidth is allocated by each modality's contribution to the fused prediction. This improves training efficiency for edge clients that cannot host an encoder per modality.

entry.title: Incremental Risk Assessment of Progressive Elder Financial Scams via Instruction-Tuned Small Language Models

author.name: Parviz Ghafariasl, Weimin Fu, Xiaolong Guo, Shing I. Chang

entry.summary: The paper proposes a cumulative turn-based risk assessment framework that incrementally aggregates conversational turns to detect elder financial scams unfolding over email, SMS, or phone. It uses instruction-tuned small language models suited to resource-constrained deployment. The multi-turn framing matches how scams actually escalate across conversations.

entry.title: The Curse of Multilinguality in Lexical Normalization

author.name: Saman Rahbar

entry.summary: This study measures how accuracy in multilingual lexical normalization degrades as the number of jointly trained languages increases, finding a clear curse of multilinguality: accuracy drops about forty percent as languages go from few to twelve in a fixed-capacity model. It questions the common shortcut of many-language joint training when labeled data is scarce. A clean controlled experiment.

entry.title: Latent-Space No-Arbitrage Geometry of Generative Models for Implied Volatility Surfaces

author.name: Jing Wang, Shuaiqiang Liu, Cornelis Vuik

entry.summary: The paper studies static no-arbitrage constraints for generative models of implied volatility surfaces in latent space, characterizing an admissible latent set via a scalar margin and deriving level-set dynamics near its boundary. This gives quantitative finance a geometric lens for constraining generative models. Specialized but mathematically substantive.

entry.title: Adapting Without Gradients: Affine Statistics Transport and What Its Certificate Can Tell You

author.name: Salim Khazem, Ibrahim Mohamed Serouis

entry.summary: CASTER is a gradient-free test-time adaptation method that transports source class statistics to target batches via an estimated class-shared affine transformation, requiring no backward pass or stored feature bank. It suits frozen, third-party, or inference-only deployments where standard TTA fails. A practical niche contribution with an accompanying certificate analysis.

entry.title: Runtime-Independent Persistent Agents: Preserving Identity, Memory, and Code Across Models, Harnesses, and Servers

author.name: Zhenyu Zhao (Independent Researcher), Roy Zhao (Paul G. Allen School of Computer Science & Engineering, University of Washington)

entry.summary: The paper presents a runtime-independent architecture for persistent agents that decouple identity, durable memory, and versioned code from any particular model, harness, host, or interaction surface. It formalizes a continuity substrate plus replaceable deployment bindings. Conceptually useful for long-lived agent systems, though it is largely a design contribution.

entry.title: Breaking the Structural Identity: Personalized Federated LoRA Fine-tuning under Rank Heterogeneity

author.name: Lei Wang, Jieming Bian, Letian Zhang, Jie Xu

entry.summary: FedRoRA addresses personalized federated LoRA fine-tuning under rank heterogeneity, providing client-specific models rather than a unified global model per rank while bridging dimension mismatches for aggregation. It targets resource and data heterogeneity in privacy-sensitive distributed LLM adaptation. A competent federated-learning contribution.

entry.title: Vision-Language-Guided Pseudo-Labels for Unsupervised Domain Adaptation in Semantic Segmentation for Waste Sorting

author.name: Udo Schlegel, Shubhangi, Gabriel Dax, Sai Rahul Kaminwar, Florian Karl, Thomas Seidl

entry.summary: Builds a cross-modal pseudo-labeling pipeline for unsupervised domain adaptation in semantic segmentation, combining SAM region proposals with EVA-CLIP semantic labeling and optional BLIP verification, applied to industrial waste sorting. It removes the need for any target-domain annotations.

entry.title: Revisiting Face Recognition for Monozygotic Twins: The Celeb Twins Test Set

author.name: Michael Zang, Haiyu Wu, Mrinal Sharma, Kevin W. Bowyer

entry.summary: Introduces the Celeb Twins Test Set, 80 sets of celebrity twins with metadata on skin marks and mirror asymmetry, showing current deep face matchers reach over 76 percent verification accuracy but do not use facial marks or asymmetry. It revisits long-standing hypotheses about twin face recognition.

entry.title: Local Reference Geometry Residual Augmentation for Imbalanced Time Series Classification

author.name: Chuanhang Qiu, Yanran Xu, Yue Wang, Anthony Bagnall

entry.summary: Proposes Local Reference Geometry (LRG), a lightweight post-hoc feature augmentation module for imbalanced time series classification, diagnosing a training-local geometry failure where minority samples sit in sparse or mixed neighborhoods despite good global structure. LRG repairs the local feature space between a fixed extractor and classifier.

entry.title: CRAFT: Fine-Tuning Pre-hoc Explainability in AI-native 6G RAN

author.name: Pranshav Gajjar, Vijay K Shah

entry.summary: CRAFT addresses pre-hoc explainability for small language models embedded in AI-native 6G RAN, arguing that RANSTRUCT-style SFT produces only post-hoc rationalizations. It adapts RL reasoning methods such as GRPO so causal reasoning traces precede output labels, making telecom decisions auditable.

entry.title: Poisson-Gamma Dynamical Systems with Time-varying Transition Dynamics

author.name: Jiahao Wang, Yijun Wang, Nan Fang, Sikun Yang

entry.summary: Proposes TV-PGDS, a Poisson-Gamma dynamical system with time-varying transition kernels using specially designed Dirichlet Markov chains, to better capture evolving dynamics in count-valued time series. It extends a Bayesian model family valued for interpretable latent structure and uncertainty estimates.

entry.title: Staged Linguistic Seeding: Grounded Query Expansion for Verified-Unit QA in AI Contact Centers

author.name: Hyeonseop Yoon, Jeong-Eun Park

entry.summary: Describes a deployed AI contact center QA system that answers only from a verified closed set of QA units with abstain/clarify/handoff routing, enriched offline by staged linguistic seeding using gpt-4.1-mini variant generation with human gating. It improves retrieval recall under tight latency constraints.

entry.title: From Production Traffic to Post-Training: Building a Self-Hosted LLM That Covers the Corporate Request Mix

author.name: Olga Tsymboi, Dmitrii Stoianov, Ramil Latypov, Danil Taranets, Daniil Dryabin, Mikhail Gashkov, Viktor Zelenkovskiy, Aleksandr Fida, Gleb Alektorov, Nikita Gulyakov, Arthur Babkin, Aleksandr Medvedev, Pavel Gein, Anatolii Potapov

entry.summary: An enterprise case study consolidating traffic from over 200 internal applications onto a single self-hosted LLM by training separate GRPO experts per capability axis and merging them via staged merging to avoid cross-domain reward interference.

entry.title: CrossFeat: Bridging Imaging Modalities in Feature Descriptor Space

author.name: Paul Schneider, Nazim Haouchine

entry.summary: CrossFeat enables an existing monomodal keypoint descriptor to operate across imaging modalities (multispectral, RGB-depth, satellite, medical) by learning a crossing function in descriptor space, avoiding per-pair retraining.

entry.title: DGNet: Dual-knowledge Guided Network for Infrared Small Target Detection

author.name: Chenglong Yu, Mingzhu Xu, Jing Wang, Tongtong Wang, Pingping Miao, Liqiang Nie

entry.summary: Proposes DGNet for infrared small target detection, using dual knowledge guidance with multiple generalizable texts to avoid semantic entanglement between background and target and to remove inference-time dependence on CLIP-style external prompt models.

entry.title: An Intelligent Decision Support System for Emotion Monitoring using Microscopic Fixational Dynamics

author.name: Xiangyu Shen, Feiyang Deng, Zijian Dai, Aibin Chen, Jizheng Yi, Jie Li, Hongbo Jiang

entry.summary: Proposes an edge-computing decision support system using smart glasses to infer emotional states from microscopic fixation dynamics (microsaccades, ocular drifts, microtremors) with an interpretable hybrid AI pipeline, aimed at less intrusive emotion monitoring than facial or physiological signals.

entry.title: Lightweight Interpretable RGB-Guided Hyperspectral Super-Resolution under Real Cross-resolution Misalignment

author.name: Mohamad Jouni, Aur\'elien Godet, Mauro Dalla Mura

entry.summary: Proposes a lightweight, interpretable RGB-guided hyperspectral super-resolution method that handles real cross-camera misregistration rather than assuming aligned inputs. It targets snapshot hyperspectral cameras, transferring spatial detail from RGB while being robust to residual misregistration and less computationally demanding than learned unaligned-fusion methods.

entry.title: Beyond Object Selection:Markerless Gaze-based Robot Placement at Arbitrary Position

author.name: Yuzhi Lai, William Marx, Shenghai Yuan, Peizheng Li, Zhuoyu Ran, Andreas Zell

entry.summary: Introduces a markerless gaze-based robot manipulation framework allowing placement at arbitrary positions, with Graph-based Reference Selection and a dedicated cross-device dataset to study headset-robot alignment from a task-accuracy perspective. Shows that pose accuracy does not directly translate to task accuracy since translational and rotational errors can compensate.

entry.title: iPINN for Broadband CARS Phase Retrieval: A Framework for Function Approximation and Inverse Modeling Problems in Nonlinear Spectroscopy

author.name: Ravi Teja Vulchi, Carl Messerschmidt, Mohammadsadegh Vafaeinezhad, Rajendhar Junjuri, Tobias Meyer-Zedler, Juergen Popp, Thomas Bocklitz

entry.summary: Introduces an inverse physics-informed neural network for broadband CARS spectroscopy phase retrieval, predicting Lorentzian peak parameters from raw spectra via a transformer encoder with 24 learnable peak slots and multi-view consistency losses. The approach reconstructs resonant susceptibility through a differentiable analytical forward model.

entry.title: When Prediction Error Is Not Enough: Evaluating Nuisance-Function Prediction for Causal Estimation

author.name: Cong Cao

entry.summary: This Monte Carlo study evaluates whether nuisance-function prediction error is a good proxy for causal estimator performance in a partially linear model, comparing OLS, GAMs, XGBoost, and DML-XGBoost. It finds prediction error can mislead across different performance measures and examines a joint-error cross-product measure. A useful caution for ML-based causal inference practice.

entry.title: ADGNet: Asymmetric Dual-text Guided Network for Infrared Small Target Detection

author.name: Tongtong Wang, Mingzhu Xu, Chenglong Yu, Jing Wang, Xiaohui Lin, Weili Guan
