entry.summary: Formulates interactive medical diagnosis as a risk-sensitive sequential decision problem with severity-aware conformal calibration, maintaining diagnostic, safety, and masked-evidence beliefs and planning over whether to continue questioning or commit, explicitly modeling the asymmetric clinical cost of missing severe diseases. Addresses a real gap where uncertainty-guided information acquisition ignores clinical risk. A promising framework whose clinical validation remains to be seen.

entry.title: Stay Within Your Bounds: Distance-Guided Decoding for Guaranteed Context-Free Grammar Compliance

author.name: Vincenzo Collura, Karim Tit, Eleonora Giunchiglia, Mike Papadakis, Maxime Cordy

entry.summary: Proposes lookahead-guided decoding for context-free grammar constraints using offline pushdown-automaton summaries with reachability labels and upper-bound distances to acceptance, guiding horizon-aware pruning and beam search so that every completed output is syntactically sound even under tokenizer-grammar mismatch and finite token budgets. Addresses a real failure mode of prefix-feasibility decoders. A strong formal contribution with practical value.

entry.title: MAIL: Memory-driven, Adaptive, Incremental, and Literature-grounded Framework for Hypothesis Generation in Chemistry

author.name: Mahdi Babaei, Xueshen Li, Yutao Kuang, Jolene P. Reid, Yu Gan

entry.summary: MAIL is a memory-augmented, adaptive framework that uses LLMs to generate experimentally meaningful hypotheses in chemistry, drawing dynamically on the literature rather than static inspiration corpora. It targets the bottleneck of navigating an ever-expanding chemical knowledge base without heavy human-in-the-loop pipelines. If validated, this could accelerate discovery-driven chemistry research.

entry.title: VERA-8B: Evidence-Grounded Audit Risk Reasoning from SEC Filings

author.name: Menghan Liu, Elynn Chen

entry.summary: VERA-8B is an end-to-end audit reasoning system that predicts audit risks from SEC filings before enforcement actions, unifying supervised fine-tuning and GRPO reinforcement learning under a single evidence-grounding standard. It targets the grounding gap where standard financial LLMs produce plausible but unevidenced answers. It claims to be the first ML system aimed at pre-enforcement audit prediction.

entry.title: AcrossVAM1.0: Particle World Modeling for Text-Assisted Robot Video Prediction

author.name: Yafei Zhang, Nan Wu

entry.summary: AcrossVAM1.0 is a lightweight text-assisted video action model for robot video prediction that factorizes the future into object-centric motion (semantic particles from a frozen SAM3-DLP codec) and dense appearance, with a tiny 0.28M-parameter spatiotemporal Transformer rolling particle states forward. This factorization addresses the entanglement of motion and appearance in monolithic pixel models. Notable for extreme parameter efficiency in world modeling.

entry.title: The Effect of Emotional Context on Large Language Models' Endorsement of Premature Decisions: Comparing Emotional Vulnerability Across Six Commercial Models

author.name: Cheolho Shin, Yoojin Han, Donghun Shin, Kunho Lee

entry.summary: This study tests whether users' emotional expressions increase six commercial LLMs' endorsement of premature decisions (e.g., quitting a job on weak evidence), using a neutral multi-turn control to isolate emotion from conversation length. It documents emotional vulnerability as a systematic safety problem across top-tier and mid-tier models from major vendors. Directly relevant to consumer-facing advice assistants.

entry.title: PHR-VLA: Planning Horizon Reasoning for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Davood Soleymanzadeh, Kaidi Zhang, Zhiyuan Zhang, Bihao Zhang, Xiao Liang, Yu She, Minghui Zheng

entry.summary: PHR-VLA adds planning-horizon reasoning to vision-language-action models via a lightweight auxiliary future head that aligns the VLA's internal representations with latent dynamics extracted from future observations during training. This targets fine-grained, contact-rich manipulation where current-observation conditioning is insufficient. A targeted improvement to a fast-moving model family.

entry.title: Knowing Before Answering: Decoding Language Models for Reliable RAG

author.name: Syed Mahbubul Huq, Christopher Child, Tillman Weyde, Pranava Madhyastha

entry.summary: This paper frames RAG reliability as a three-way classification problem (sufficient, insufficient, conflicting evidence) and shows that hidden activations and attention-derived features of the model can predict when to abstain before answering. It includes a controlled benchmark with fictitious information to isolate the signal. Connecting internal representations to retrieval-sufficiency decisions is a valuable interpretability-to-application bridge.

entry.title: Efficient Auto-Interpretability of AI Models in Biology

author.name: Piotr Jedryszek, Oliver M. Crook

entry.summary: This paper builds a pipeline for efficient auto-interpretability of AI models in biology, assembling three distinct latent-quality questions (coherence, describability, predictive power) into one workflow with cross-seed dictionary stability for prioritizing sparse-autoencoder latents and intruder-detection tasks. It operationalizes SAE analysis for scientific discovery in a domain with superhuman model capabilities. Useful methodological scaffolding for scaling interpretability.

entry.title: When Can Conditional Flow Matching Replace Pointwise Negative Log-Likelihood?

author.name: Yansen Han, Hongxin Sun, Tao Lin

entry.summary: This theory paper characterizes when conditional flow matching losses can substitute for pointwise negative log-likelihoods in alignment methods, exactly decomposing endpoint NLL for linear Gaussian paths into entropy, a weighted CFM objective, and interior and boundary residuals. Ordinary CFM is not generally a pointwise NLL estimator at the population optimum, though a specific weighting removes the interior residual. Important correctness guardrails for a growing practice in RL-based alignment.

entry.title: Twin Worlds: Equivariance-Based Abstention for Evidence-Grounded Reasoning

author.name: Vy Nguyen, Ziqi Xu, Jeffrey Chan, Estrid He, Feng Xia, Renqiang Luo, Erik Cambria, Xiuzhen Zhang

entry.summary: Twin Worlds is a framework for evidence-grounded LLM reasoning that uses an equivariance-based abstention test: it checks whether the reasoning process actually depends on provided evidence rather than memorized associations activated by entity mentions. Unlike uncertainty or sufficiency heuristics, it probes whether generation is causally grounded in context. Addresses hallucination through a principled abstention criterion.

entry.title: Beyond Flat Netlist: Hierarchical Graph Representation Learning for Scalable Analysis of Sequential Circuits

author.name: Jingyi Zhou, Zhengyuan Shi, Jiaying Zhu, Ziyang Zheng, Qiang Xu

entry.summary: DeepSeq3 introduces hierarchical graph representations of sequential circuits, combining fine-grained combinational subgraphs with a Super-Node Graph for register-transfer structure learned via dual GNNs. Addresses scalability of circuit representation learning for industrial EDA tasks.

entry.title: LLM-Based Agents for Software and Systems Security: Approaches, Applications, and Assessment

author.name: Jingjing Nie, Jiawei Guo, Krishna Meda, Haipeng Cai

entry.summary: A systematic survey of LLM-based agents for software and systems security, taxonomizing approaches, applications, and assessment protocols while highlighting inconsistent use of the term agent and incoherent evaluation across a high-risk domain.

entry.title: Learning a Size-Weight Frontier for Synthetic-Augmented Inference

author.name: Chengpiao Huang, Kaizheng Wang

entry.summary: Develops a framework for synthetic-augmented inference across related tasks, defining a size-weight frontier that specifies the largest synthetic sample size preserving target coverage for each synthetic-data weight, with finite-sample guarantees estimated from historical tasks.

entry.title: Equivariant Sheaf Neural Networks: Learning Geometric Transport on Graphs

author.name: Alessio Borgi, Mario Severino, Fabrizio Silvestri, Pietro Li\`o

entry.summary: Introduces Equivariant Sheaf Neural Networks, learning directed matrix-valued transport over edges while keeping scalar and vector features first-order, preserving exact Euclidean equivariance with theoretical characterization of the transport class.

entry.title: Reward-guided Fine-Tuning of One-Step Generative Models via Wasserstein Gradient Flow

author.name: Hoseong Hwang, Woorim Han, Joungin Chun, Jinseong Park, Jaewoong Choi

entry.summary: Tests whether JEPA latent world models survive when observations are sparse, unordered point clouds rather than images, lifting three canonical JEPA designs to geometric observations on a re-sensed benchmark. Finds all three plan without collapse and the distribution-prior variant matches its image-based counterpart.

entry.title: A Target-Centric Survey of Quantization-Aware Training

author.name: Jiamin Song, Mengjie Zhao, Zijing Wang, Yongkang Liu, Qian Li, Shi Feng, Feiliang Ren, Daling Wang, Hinrich Sch\"utze

entry.summary: Provides a target-centric survey of quantization-aware training, organizing methods by target type and synthesizing differences in error characteristics, numerical formats, and strategy transferability for producing low-bit LLMs.

entry.title: Creation begins with understanding: LLMs as strategy designers for privacy-preserving tabular data synthesis

author.name: Jinmeng Li, Quan Zhang, Hangting Ye, He Zhao, Firas Laakom, Dandan Guo, J\"urgen Schmidhuber

entry.summary: Introduces TabSSD, which uses an LLM to design privacy-preserving tabular synthesis procedures (Python programs executed locally) from tree-derived dependency summaries rather than raw records, balancing fidelity, utility, and privacy across twelve datasets.

entry.title: The Intervention Gap in Latent World Models

author.name: Donna Vakalis

entry.summary: Defines planning-time intervention fidelity as a measurable property of world models and shows it is not revealed by reward fit: TD-MPC2 checkpoints show return degrading with an operator-error diagnostic while reward-prediction error stays flat, with self-supervised models preserving interventions better.

entry.title: How do World Models and Policies Compose in LLM Agents? A Joint Spectral and Behavioral Account

author.name: Ruize Xu, Xiao Yu, Yujin Tang, Chenming Shang, Nikhil Singh

entry.summary: Dissects how world-model and policy training compose in LLM agents via spectral analysis of additive parameter updates, finding low-rank world-model updates sharing input subspaces with but writing orthogonal output directions relative to policy updates, with sequential updates inducing robustness to projection interventions.

entry.title: Strong Drafts Need Compact Memories: Long-Context Speculative Decoding with Compressed KV Cache

author.name: Tong Yuan, Chengxi Liao, Zeyi Wen

entry.summary: Proposes memory-augmented speculative decoding, equipping a strong independent draft with compressed draft-side KV cache updated by a lightweight adaptor, resolving the trade-off between draft acceptance and KV-access latency at long contexts.

entry.title: CateKV: On Sequential Consistency for Long-Context LLM Inference Acceleration

author.name: Haoyun Jiang, Haolin Li, Jianwei Zhang, Fei Huang, Qiang Hu, Minmin Sun, Shuai Xiao, Yong Li, Junyang Lin, Jiangchao Yao

entry.summary: Discovers sequential consistency in certain attention heads and proposes CateKV, a hybrid KV cache method retaining critical tokens only for consistent heads while preserving KV pairs in adaptive heads, reducing long-context inference memory and latency.

entry.title: Convergence rates for the RMSprop optimizer with full control of the hyperparameters

author.name: Steffen Dereich, Arnulf Jentzen

entry.summary: Derives convergence rates for RMSprop with full control over hyperparameters including the regularization parameter epsilon and second-moment decay beta, closing a gap in the theoretical understanding of the optimizer underlying Adam and AdamW. The analysis is rigorous and directly relevant to widely used defaults. A strong theory contribution to optimizer analysis.

entry.title: Data Diversity, Not Frequency Invariance: A Controlled and Self-Audited Study of Compression-Robust Deepfake Detection

author.name: Abbas Aliyev, Samir Rustamov

entry.summary: The authors run a controlled, pre-registered study of compression-robust deepfake detection, reporting a negative result: data diversity, not frequency-invariant representations or compression-conditioned architectures, drives robustness. Their self-audit methodology (finding and repairing four defects biased against their own hypothesis) is a notable part of the contribution.

entry.title: Efficient GPU Retrieval for Semantic Search

author.name: Dhritiman Das, Chujie Zheng, Ronak Kaoshik, Pratik Dixit, Vishal Shah, Yanbo Li, Jiahao Xu, Manika Agarwal, Chinmay Naik, Lingyu Zhang, Chetan Bhole, Chirag Bhanuprasad Mehta, Meng Zheng, Puneet Singh Ahluwalia, Shirisha Singh, Ping Jin, Manas Apte, Gokulraj Mohanasundaram, Tugrul Bingol, Raghavan Muthuregunathan, Fedor Borisyuk

entry.summary: LinkedIn engineers present a policy-aligned GPU retrieval framework for semantic search over hundreds of millions of profiles, partitioning embeddings into eight category-supervised segments whose scores follow the same min/median aggregation as the deployed LLM graded-relevance policy. This avoids cosine similarity averaging away facet failures and improves first-stage recall.

entry.title: Sharp Restricted Isometry Thresholds for Global Minima of Rank-Restricted Matrix LASSO

author.name: Richard Y. Zhang

entry.summary: Determines the sharp restricted isometry threshold at which the rank-restricted matrix LASSO recovers low-rank matrices at global minima, with constants independent of search rank. The result unifies the rank-restricted and fully convex cases under one characterization.

entry.title: QCell: Recombining and Aligning Cell Queries for Overlapping Instance Segmentation

author.name: Yaroslav Prytula, Anton Popov, Dmytro Fishman

entry.summary: Introduces QCell, a query-based model for segmenting overlapping cells in microscopy, combining an instance recombination module that reasons about complete object structure under overlap with a contrastive query alignment objective to separate overlapping instances.

entry.title: Explanations, Prompts, and Formalizations: Arguments for New Norms in LLM-Enabled Mathematical Research

author.name: Axel Boldt

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that emerging norms for publishing LLM-assisted mathematical results should additionally require disclosure of prompts and software setup, machine-verifiable formalization of results, and human-authored intuitive explanations of LLM-obtained findings.

entry.title: Deciding When to Decide: Testing Operational Suboptimality Under Distributional Shift

author.name: Minxing Zheng, Holly Wiberg, Shixiang Zhu

entry.summary: Proposes RADAR, a decision-focused framework using inverse optimization to infer whether a deployed decision has become materially suboptimal under distribution shift, addressing the gap where standard shift tests flag decision-irrelevant changes without informing re-optimization timing.

entry.title: Influence-Directed Distillation: Solving the Diversity Bottleneck in Sampled-Token On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Run Yang, Runpeng Dai, Jie Sun, Jielei Zhang, Fan Zhou, Hongtu Zhu, Peiyi Li, Longwen Gao

entry.summary: Identifies diversity distillation failure in sampled-token on-policy distillation, where student pass@1 improves but pass@k plateaus, and introduces a first-order entropy-influence proxy to diagnose it. Proposes IDA-OPD, an influence-directed adaptive distillation method to preserve teacher diversity.

entry.title: Implementing neural network mixed-effects models in Template Model Builder (TMB)

author.name: Nan Zheng, Hoi Yiu Cheung, Vibhu Sharma, James T. Thorson, Noel G. Cadigan

entry.summary: Introduces a general framework for fitting neural network mixed-effects models using Template Model Builder, requiring users to specify only the joint log-likelihood via automatic differentiation and Laplace approximation. This removes the need for manual gradient derivations and could broaden adoption of flexible NMMs in ecology, fisheries, and other statistical domains.

entry.title: SHADOWBENCH: Toward Reliable Automatic Evaluation of Semantic Alignment in Autoformalization

author.name: Hojae Han, Jongyoon Kim, Sanghyuk Park, Dongwook Cheon, Myungjae Jeon, Sunjong Choi, Soonho Kong, Wonseok Heo, Seung-won Hwang, Donghoon Hyeon

entry.summary: Proposes SA-Pass (Semantic Alignment Pass) for evaluating autoformalization in Lean 4, testing generated statements against auxiliary shadow statements via forward and backward implication checks. Instantiated in ShadowBench with 178 postgraduate-to-research-level problems.

entry.title: Modality Fault Lines: Structural Corruptions Reveal Fragile Omni-Modal Reasoning

author.name: Zhaolu Kang, Meixin Wu, Yu Xue, Yingjie He, Qiming Shi, Lei Wei, Yidi Wang, Richeng Xuan, Zhichao Hu

entry.summary: Defines modality fault lines and introduces SCEval, a protocol that keeps questions and modality channels fixed while structurally corrupting internal evidence, revealing that omni-modal LLMs' clean-input success often rests on fragile cross-modal structure.

entry.title: SemTrace: Source-Grounded Semantic Signatures for Tracing LLM Exposure to Protected Documents

author.name: Junyan Zhang, Yudong Zeng, Yongwei Huang, Zuhao Ouyang, Hong Chen, Xuming Hu

entry.summary: Introduces SemTrace, a source-grounded semantic watermark that detects whether generated text (e.g., peer reviews) was influenced by a protected document, embedding a binary signature from document-supported factual propositions carried invisibly in the PDF. Avoids token-probability biasing entirely.

entry.title: ImageEval 2026: Culturally Grounded Arabic Multimodal Evaluation

author.name: Samir Abdaljalil, Hunzalah Hassan Bhatti, Ahlam Bashiti, Farina Amir, Md Arid Hasan, Basel Mousi, Nadir Durrani, Fahim Dalvi, Zien Sheikh Ali, Erchin Serpedin, Hasan Kurban, Mustafa Jarrar, Shammur Absar Chowdhury, Firoj Alam

entry.summary: Overview of the ImageEval 2026 shared task on culturally grounded Arabic multimodal evaluation, featuring two tracks: spoken visual question answering with hallucination detection (AynVQA) and cultural accuracy of text-to-image generation (CRAI-Bench). Fourteen teams participated using approaches spanning prompting, fine-tuning, ASR pipelines, and ensembling.

entry.title: Opinionated, Hesitant and Stressed: Three Studies of How Politicians Speak in Four Slavic Parliaments

author.name: Ivan Porupski, Nikola Ljube\v{s}i\'c

entry.summary: Three large-scale studies of parliamentary speech across four Slavic languages using 6,000+ hours of the ParlaSpeech 3.0 corpus, linking sentiment to acoustic realization and modeling filled-pause frequency. Finds consistent cross-lingual effects of negative speech on pitch, intensity, and rate, plus contrasting gender effects across language groups.

entry.title: The First Token Is a Clue: Verbalizing Multi-Token Concepts from the J-lens

author.name: Xijie Gong, Tonghan Wang

entry.summary: The paper asks whether multi-token concepts can be recovered from the Jacobian Lens interpretability tool with a frozen model, finding the first token of a multi-token concept is as readable as a single-token concept. Given the correct first token and prompt, the frozen model recovers the second token 88.3 percent of the time. This offers a cheaper alternative to Template and Oracle Lens phrase-representation machinery.

entry.title: Super Library Agent: Joint Generation and Maintenance of Multiple Applications Beyond the Single Codebase

author.name: Daegyu Sung, Yukyeong Lee, Geon Park, Yumin Choi, Sung Ju Hwang

entry.summary: This paper introduces the Super Library Agent problem, where an LLM coding agent sequentially generates a portfolio of N related applications while maintaining a shared library of reusable cross-application components. It addresses verbosity, dead code, and structural erosion that accumulate in naive application-by-application agent workflows. The problem formalizes portfolio-level software maintenance for coding agents.

entry.title: LaMoC: Loss-Aware Modular Compression for LLMs

author.name: Mohanad Odema, Jacob Song

entry.summary: LaMoC is a loss-aware modular compression method for LLMs that blends activation statistics with Empirical Fisher statistics to better align module-level reconstruction error with downstream loss. It improves joint modular compression (pruning/low-rank style reduction) over activation-only baselines. Relevant to efficient deployment of large models.

entry.title: Inter-3D VQA: A Roadside Multimodal Benchmark for 3D Spatiotemporally Grounded Visual Question Answering

author.name: Shaozu Ding, Linan Song, Dajiang Suo

entry.summary: Inter-3D VQA is a large-scale roadside multimodal benchmark built from synchronized point clouds and multi-view images, containing 407K QA pairs for 3D spatiotemporally grounded VQA at intersections including near-miss interaction reasoning. Fills a real gap versus ego-vehicle-centric benchmarks for infrastructure perception.

entry.title: Dynamic-Robust Photometric-Semantic Reconstruction for Open-Vocabulary 3D Scene Understanding

author.name: Boyu Cai, Li Yang, Yan Xu, Wei Liu, Nian Liu, Sikui Zhang, Yan Wang, Chunfeng Yuan, Weiming Hu

entry.summary: Proposes SPAR, a joint semantic-geometric architecture for open-vocabulary 3D scene understanding in dynamic environments, isolating transient dynamic noise before latent aggregation. It couples motion estimation with multi-view visual and semantic learning to handle scenes violating static assumptions. Relevant to feed-forward 3D foundation models that currently fail on moving scenes.

entry.title: RAGDiffusion++: From Macro-Retrieval to Micro-Fidelity Alignment for Garment Generation

author.name: Yuhan Li, Xianfeng Tan, Fangao Zeng, Wenxiang Shang, Pipei Huang, Hao Zhou, Zhiyu Jin, Wenjun Zhang, Bingbing Ni

entry.summary: RAGDiffusion++ extends a prior retrieval-augmented garment generation system by targeting High-Frequency Trajectory Collapse, where supervised fine-tuning converges to smooth low-frequency texture means and loses fabric weave detail. They add micro-fidelity alignment on top of macro-retrieval constraints. An industrially motivated follow-up that names and attacks a specific generative failure mode.

entry.title: RIDGE: Region-Informed Derivative-Guided Evidence Selection for Long Video Understanding

author.name: Shanqing Xu, Meng Luo, Mengchen Qian, Yuhui Gao, Siyue Peng, Xiaohan Zhong, Xiaojin Zhang, Zhongyu Wei, Wei Chen, Xiang Bai

entry.summary: RIDGE reinterprets frame-query similarity as an ordered signal whose shape reveals how relevant evidence rises and fades over time, improving frame selection for long-video understanding in LVLMs. This addresses a core bottleneck in long-context video reasoning under fixed visual-token budgets.

entry.title: RealCAD: Towards Real-World Image-to-CAD Reconstruction under Domain Shift and Parameter Bias

author.name: Yihe Sun, Ziyu Lu, Kaihua Tang, Xian-Sheng Hua

entry.summary: RealCAD exposes two obstacles in image-to-CAD reconstruction: the synthetic-to-real domain gap and a previously overlooked parameter bias in DeepCAD normalization that lets models exploit frequent discrete parameter values for deceptively high accuracy. Defines a more honest real-world benchmark.

entry.title: APT: Anchor-aligned Perturbations for Tamper Localization in Fully Regenerated Images

author.name: Suhyeon Ha, Woo Jae Kim, Joonsung Jeon, Sooel Son, Sung-eui Yoon

entry.summary: APT addresses proactive tamper localization in the fully regenerated setting where diffusion inpainting disrupts background signals, via semi-fragile latent-space perturbations aligned to fixed anchor directions for dense vector-wise localization. Extends watermarking to real diffusion manipulation workflows.

entry.title: Uncertainty-Aware Trajectory Forecasting from Imperfect Tracking

author.name: Stephane Da Silva Martins, Victor Petrovic, Emanuel Aldea, Sylvie Le H\'egarat-Mascle

entry.summary: This work proposes a plug-in uncertainty-aware trajectory forecasting framework that treats imperfect tracker outputs (jitter, missed detections, association ambiguity) as informative reliability signals rather than noise to be removed. It addresses the gap between clean training data and real deployment conditions.

entry.title: RedLight-VLA: Models for traffic-rule grounding and behavioral emphasis in driving policies

author.name: Bala Murali Manoghar Sai Sudhakar, Sourab Bapu Sridhar, Sandipan Das, Rahul Ahuja, Meda Lazar, Ashish Garg, Pratik Likhar, Senthil Yogamani

entry.summary: RedLight-VLA improves behavior-cloned vision-language-action driving policies at signalized intersections using trajectory-derived behavioral reweighting for rare braking/launching events plus auxiliary heads supervising traffic-light and stop-line states, without manual rule annotation. It targets rare rule-governed maneuvers that average losses underweight.

entry.title: SCoPE-Reg: Efficient Rigid Ultrasound Slice-to-Volume Registration via State-Space Correlation and Closed-Form Pose Estimation

author.name: Niklas Schwarz, Jens Kleesiek, Moritz Rempe

entry.summary: SCoPE-Reg performs rigid ultrasound slice-to-volume registration by combining state-space slice-volume interaction, dense 3D coordinate prediction, and parameter-free weighted Kabsch pose estimation, avoiding costly dense cross-attention. It achieves low target registration errors on CAMUS and mu-RegPro.

entry.title: Efficient JPEG Restoration in the Wavelet Domain via Mean Flows

author.name: Stefan-Alexandru Asandei, Mihai-Alexandru Radu

entry.summary: A 65M-parameter wavelet-domain generative restorer for JPEG artifacts replaces the VAE with an exactly invertible Haar transform and uses a linear-attention DiT with mean-flow training, achieving best LPIPS at severe compression while running about 4.9x faster than one-step SODiff at one-twentieth the parameters. It targets on-device deployment.

entry.title: The MYOSAIQ Challenge: Myocardial Segmentation with Automated Infarct Quantification

author.name: Olivier Bernard, William A. Romero R., Cyprien Bouton, Celia Goujat, Hang Jung Ling, Pierre-Marc Jodoin, Fumin Guo, Calder Sheagren, Graham Wright, Abdul Qayyum, Moona Mazher, Steven A. Niederer, Hairui Wang, Xiaomei Wu, Franz Thaler, Gernot Plank, Martin Urschler, Ricardo M. Rosales, Esther Pueyo, Nicolas Duchateau, Frederic Cervenansky, Patrick Clarysse, Loic Belle, Thomas Bochaton, Nathan Mewton, Magalie Viallon, Pierre Croisille

entry.summary: The MYOSAIQ challenge establishes benchmarks for myocardial segmentation and automated infarct quantification in late gadolinium enhancement cardiac MRI, addressing small datasets and limited generalizability that keep infarct quantification out of routine clinical practice. It defines tasks and evaluation for the community.

entry.title: GHOST in the Robots: Real-Time Exocentric Dual-Robot VR Teleoperation from Onboard Cameras

author.name: Yichen Wei, Faisal Zaghloul, Soujanya C Aryal, Aanya K. Agrawal, Chengfan Li, Jason Xinyu Liu, James Tompkin, Stefanie Tellex

entry.summary: GHOST is an open-source VR teleoperation system letting a single operator control two mobile manipulators via low-level commands using only onboard RGB-D sensing, creating an exocentric 3D workspace from aligned real-time point clouds. It removes the need for multiple operators or restrictive autonomy.

entry.title: CGFM-Nav: Cognitive Graph-Field Memory for Semantic-Guided Lifelong Multimodal Embodied Navigation

author.name: Yuxiang Xiao, Xibei Chen, Xin Zhou, Jie Chen, Yifeng Zhang, Guillaume Sartoretti

entry.summary: CGFM-Nav proposes a persistent cognitive graph-field memory for vision-and-language navigation, coupling an explicit multimodal scene graph for semantic memory with a continuous goal-conditioned field for exploration guidance when no reliable target match exists. It supports lifelong, semantic-guided embodied navigation.

entry.title: AGM: Achievement-Grounded Memory for Closed-Loop Agents with Frozen VLA Policies

author.name: Hongbo Gao, Zeyu Ni, Xin Wen, Siyu Xu, Ruifeng Li

entry.summary: AGM is a lightweight closed-loop framework for frozen VLA policies that represents tasks as subgoal sequences with a progress pointer, advancing memory only when the current subgoal is verified by physical evidence such as proprioceptive cues. This prevents execution errors from becoming persistent task-state errors in open-loop action chunking.

entry.title: EMERGE-Policy: A Robot Mind Emerges Beyond a Single Policy

author.name: Zhirui Fang, Qingchi Yu, Ziyang Chen, Longfei Li, Haoran Ma, Keru Zhou, Xinrun Xu, Samith Va, Yuxuan Hu, Peixuan Song, Qiang Du, Bin Qian, Yongkang Deng, Xin Li, Yezhen Wang, Zhe Li, Hao Luo, Shuyan Li, Ziwei Wang, Weijian Deng, Xiu Li

entry.summary: EMERGE-Policy proposes a graph-structured agentic framework in which a Main Agent retains task-level state while role-specific Sub Agents handle perception, execution monitoring, verification, and memory in isolated contexts, returning structured evidence. The robot mind emerges from orchestrated specialized components rather than a single monolithic policy.

entry.title: Rethinking Language's Role in Efficient VLA for Autonomous Vehicles: Toward Smarter, Trustworthy Driving

author.name: Tongfei Guo, Lili Su

entry.summary: Reframes language use in autonomous-driving VLA models around when and where language should act at inference, proposing a Language Residue taxonomy: train-time-only supervision, latent non-textual reasoning, conditional invocation, and full per-frame decoding. Positions inference cost as the central design constraint for trustworthy driving.

entry.title: Contrast-Free Autonomous Navigation of Untethered Endovascular Microrobots Using Single-Plane Fluoroscopy

author.name: Husnu Halid Alabay, Tuan-Anh Le, Ping Wang, Hakan Ceylan

entry.summary: VISTA is a digital twin framework enabling contrast-free autonomous navigation of magnetically actuated untethered endovascular microrobots under single-plane fluoroscopy, reconstructing vascular depth information without biplane imaging or repeated contrast angiography. Reduces radiation and contrast burden for potential clinical translation.

entry.title: PAVE: Predictive Alignment and Value-Guided Evolution for World-Action Policies

author.name: Botong Zhao, Fang Yu, Tim, Senhua Zhu, Xinyuan Chen, Yue Lu

entry.summary: PAVE combines outcome-agnostic predictive learning with outcome-aware policy improvement in a world-action policy: a JEPA-style objective extended with multi-horizon transition alignment, plus value-guided filtering of deployment trajectories to separate useful dynamics from undesirable behavior.

entry.title: Temporal Forcing: 4D Representation Alignment for Vision-Language-Action Models

author.name: Xingyu Ding, Yuzhong Zhao, Chunhai Zhao, Yinghuan Shi, Chaoyang Zhao, Yifan Zhang

entry.summary: Temporal Forcing adds a 4D representation alignment method for VLA models: a history pathway summarizes observation history into temporally aware latents aligned with pre-trained geometric features, addressing observation aliasing between visually similar states and improving long-horizon manipulation.

entry.title: Value generalisation Theory of Change: putting it into practice

author.name: Stuart_Armstrong

entry.summary: Stuart Armstrong's follow-up giving the practical theory of change for value generalisation research: solving three components (recognizing value-relevant off-distribution status, establishing decision features, and making good off-distribution decisions), with outputs, dangers, and mitigations laid out formally.

entry.title: Developing provably correct Rust code with Verus

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Amazon Science explains Verus, an open-source automated verifier for Rust that mechanically checks code against formal mathematical specifications, going beyond Rust's memory-safety guarantees to prove functional correctness and prevent out-of-bounds and secret-leakage classes of bugs.

entry.title: AcCoRD: Evaluating User-Agent Collaboration Under Realistic User Preference Dynamics

author.name: Tejas Srinivasan, Shikib Mehri, Nandita Shankar Naik, Anirban Das, William M. Campbell, Jesse Thomason

entry.summary: Introduces AcCoRD, a user-agent collaboration benchmark requiring agents to handle dynamic preference formation, revelation, adjustment, and relaxation in online shopping and travel planning, moving beyond static underspecified preferences, and evaluates five frontier LLMs under vanilla ReAct versus uncertainty-guided prompting. Reveals systematic weaknesses under realistic preference dynamics. A good addition to interaction-focused evaluation.

entry.title: When Teacher Guidance Misleads: Reward-Aligned On-Policy Distillation

author.name: Siyuan Gan, Yuhan Li, Xiran Wang, Linjian Meng, Boyan Wang, Zhen Zhao, Jing Huo, Yang Gao

entry.summary: Shows that in on-policy distillation the teacher can misguide the student on student-generated prefixes, discouraging movement toward correct trajectories in ways misaligned with outcome reward, and proposes reward-aligned on-policy distillation to filter or reweight teacher guidance. Sharpens a growing post-training paradigm with a practical correction. A good conceptual contribution to the OPD literature.

entry.title: No Equivariant Architecture Covers All Equivariant Attention

author.name: T\=ikun \^Ong

entry.summary: Provides a complete characterization of G-equivariant multi-head self-attention, proving that any fixed polynomially-parameterized architecture achieving exact equivariance inevitably loses expressivity within the class of equivariant maps. The proof uses the Zariski-irreducible structure of the equivariance locus. A significant theoretical result constraining the design of equivariant transformers.

entry.title: Q-Strata: Hierarchical Bit Allocation for Mixed-Precision Quantization of Mixture-of-Experts LLMs

author.name: Deokjae Lee, Sihun Chu, Hyun Oh Song

entry.summary: Proposes Q-Strata, a bi-level allocator for mixed-precision quantization of Mixture-of-Experts LLMs that ranks within-block assignments with a cheap proxy and allocates across blocks using a model-level objective, addressing the combinatorially larger allocation space of MoE models. Timely as MoE architectures dominate open-weight frontier models. Strong efficiency contribution.

entry.title: TEMPO: Temporally-grounded Multi-task Post-training for Large Audio-Language Models

author.name: Apoorva Kulkarni, Kaousheik Jayakumar, Sreyan Ghosh, Utathya Aich, Ramani Duraiswami, Dinesh Manocha

entry.summary: Presents TEMPO, the first unified post-training framework for audio, speech, and music timestamping in large audio-language models, using atomic timestamp tokens, a time-aware projector with sinusoidal encodings, and a distance-aware Gaussian loss under a synthetic-to-real curriculum. Fills a key capability gap in LALMs.

entry.title: ECGQuest: Benchmarking and Fine-Tuning Language Models for Electrocardiography

author.name: Mohammadsina Hassannia, Matthew A. Reyna, Reza Sameni

entry.summary: ECGQuest is a literature-grounded resource of 10,904 unique True/False ECG questions (21,808 with negated forms) generated from 23 references and Computing in Cardiology proceedings, for evaluating and fine-tuning ECG-specific language models. It targets contextual cardiology knowledge beyond single-signal interpretation.

entry.title: MMDS-Bench: Benchmarking Multimodal Large Language Models on Dynamic Stance in Social Media Interactions

author.name: Yuzhe Ding, Kang He, Li Zheng, Shengwu Zheng, Teng Shi, Fei Li, Chong Teng, Donghong Ji

entry.summary: MMDS-Bench benchmarks multimodal dynamic stance classification in social media parent-reply interactions with 3,482 instances and a seven-label taxonomy, plus an 800-instance diagnostic subset requiring structured reasoning. Extends stance research from text-only to multimodal contexts including memes and screenshots.

entry.title: State-Conditioned Visual Evidence Retrieval for Fine-Grained Perception in Document Vision-Language Models

author.name: Mingxu Chai, Chenyu Liu, Ziyu Shen, Jiazheng Zhang, Kaidi Zhang, Ruoyu Chen, Jun Long, Jihua Kang, Tao Gui, Qi Zhang

entry.summary: Formulates document VLM perception as state-conditioned visual evidence retrieval during autoregressive decoding, replacing globally compressed visual tokens with localized, decoding-state-conditioned evidence access. Addresses an efficiency-fidelity mismatch in document parsing. Technically substantive VLM-architecture work.

entry.title: Hyper3-CLIP: Hierarchy-Conditioned Hyperbolic Vision-Language Training

author.name: Matin Mahmood, Antonio Rueda-Toicen, Mohamed ElBassat, Seifeldin Elkerdany, Weixing Wang, Gerard de Melo

entry.summary: Hyper3-CLIP unifies hyperbolic vision-language training with query-conditioned fine-grained alignment, combining global, local, and global-local contrastive objectives with hierarchy-conditioned entailment. This encodes part-whole and parent-child structure that Euclidean CLIP embeddings miss. Bridges two previously separate research lines in VLM geometry.

entry.title: Hypothesize, Evaluate, Refine: A Scientific Agent for PDE Discovery with Unknown Spatial Coefficient Fields

author.name: YuJie Huang, WenWu He, ZhuoEr Lin, Congcong Liu, Dong Liang, Zhuo-Xu Cui

entry.summary: Presents HER-PDE, a scientific-agent framework that jointly discovers compositional PDE structure and nonparametric spatially varying coefficient fields from two noisy trajectories under different excitations, using a hypothesize-evaluate-refine loop over expression-tree hypotheses. Tackles the coupled identification problem where flexible fields can conceal structural error. Part of a fast-growing wave of agentic equation discovery.

entry.title: REINS: Refusal-Enhanced Inhibitory Steering with Sparse Autoencoder Features

author.name: Kai-Xuan Ding, Hao-Xiang Xu, Ji-Hua Peng, Zi-Qi Chen, Jiaqi Wang, Zhen-Hua Ling

entry.summary: Shows that single-direction sparse-autoencoder steering fails to induce refusal on harmful prompts wrapped in complex instructions, introduces the GUISE evaluation set of wrapped harmful prompts, and proposes refusal-enhanced inhibitory steering over SAE features to improve robustness. Contributes both a benchmark and a method to the interpretability-for-safety toolbox. Useful, though steering robustness is an arms race.

entry.title: Propagating construction-time knowledge quality into medical question answering: A framework grounded in clinical guidelines

author.name: Jie Hu, Junjie Wang, Shan Lu, Yifang Hu, Gong Cheng, Yun Liu

entry.summary: This work proposes modeling construction-time quality signals of knowledge graph triples extracted from clinical guidelines (schema conformance and evidential support) and propagating them into question answering evidence selection. It bridges a real disconnect between KG quality control at build time and evidence use at inference time. This improves reliability of graph-augmented clinical QA.

entry.title: Timing-Aware Repurchase Prediction for Web-Scale E-Commerce: Survival Models for Multi-Surface Grocery Recommendation

author.name: Akshay Kekuda, Shreeranjani Srirangamsridharan, Ishan Bhatt, Yanan Cao, Sinduja Subramaniam, Evren Korpeoglu, Kaushiki Nag, Kannan Achan

entry.summary: This industry study replaces per-horizon binary repurchase classifiers with survival models that predict time-to-repurchase directly, evaluated on millions of grocery e-commerce customers across 30+ ablations. A notable finding is a slightly decreasing marginal hazard, contradicting the common intuition that grocery repurchase probability rises with elapsed time. Log-Normal distributions performed best.

entry.title: Program Learning with Verifiable Rewards: Symbolic Backpropagation for Post-Training LLMs

author.name: Vishvesh Bhat

entry.summary: PLVR argues that for verifiable intermediate reasoning, learned capability should live outside model weights as an explicit program over deterministic and neural primitives, trained via a symbolic backpropagation mechanism from input-output examples. This makes reasoning inspectable, verifiable step-by-step, and transferable between models. It is a provocative alternative to standard SFT/RL post-training.

entry.title: InstructMesh: Selective Refinement of Generative 3D Models for Fabrication

author.name: Faraz Faruqi, Ahmed Katary, Demircan Tas, Theresa Hradilak, Ning Zhang, Jiaji Li, Fabian Manhardt, Martin Nisser, Vrushank Phadnis, Ruofei Du, Federico Tombari, Megan Hofmann, Stefanie Mueller

entry.summary: InstructMesh is an interactive tool for selectively refining generative 3D models for fabrication, letting users repair region-level geometric flaws (voids, thickness, sealing) via natural language or sliders by editing intermediate latents. Generative 3D outputs are visually plausible but often unusable for manufacturing, and this bridges that gap. From a strong HCI/fabrication group at MIT.

entry.title: Beyond Search-Imitation: Prior-Directed Exploration for Searchless Chess

author.name: Szymon Mi{\l}osz, Piotr Duch, Szymon Grabowski

entry.summary: This paper improves searchless chess networks, which distill MCTS visit counts into a single forward pass, by replacing entropy-bonus exploration with forward, mass-covering KL toward the network's own MCTS prior plus entropy-adaptive sampling temperature in self-play RL. This moves beyond search imitation toward genuine single-pass strength. A neat RL exploration contribution in a clean game domain.

entry.title: Compositional Failure in Audio-Visual LLMs: Late-Layer Prior Dominance Under Cross-modal Conflict

author.name: Adarsh Sudheer, David Li, Omar Elbanna, Ishaan Kodarapu, Arjun Bahuguna, Vasu Sharma

entry.summary: This paper identifies prior dominance as a compositional failure mode in audio-visual LLMs under cross-modal conflict: late layers commit to an internally preferred answer weakly grounded in conflicting inputs, with InternVideo2 losing 32.3 percent accuracy under conflict. It connects the failure to late-layer behavior via analysis of alignment configurations. Valuable mechanistic insight into multimodal reliability.

entry.title: PCBnet: A Dataset and Automatic Construction of SPICE Netlists from Schematic Images

author.name: Zhen Huang, Yuhao Gao, Yuzhi Liu, Daian Cheng, Chengyuan Shao, Yucheng Chen, Yongjian Jia, Futing Zhang, Yichen Shi, Wenhao Wang, Zuyan He, Yangbo Wei, Zhanfei Chen, Jinlong Yan, Yu Zhang, Haoying Wu, Ting-Jung Lin, Lei He

entry.summary: PCBnet provides a large-scale dataset of over 300 real-world PCB schematics with annotated pins and paired SPICE netlists (50k+ components, 150k wires, 400k characters), plus an automated schematic-to-netlist pipeline combining visual recognition, topology construction, and domain-knowledge-guided matching. It removes a key data bottleneck for AI-driven PCB design automation. Valuable new resource for circuit-understanding research.

entry.title: A Method for Layer Bit-Width Allocation in LLM Quantization via Performance Maximization Under a Quality-Degradation Constraint

author.name: Artem Safronov

entry.summary: FIsGuard defends against membership inference in federated fine-tuning of LLMs, specifically against ProjRes-style attacks that distinguish members from projection residuals between candidate representations and subspaces induced by observable gradients. Existing gradient-based defenses are insufficient, so it fixes input subspaces to block the leakage channel. Relevant to privacy-preserving distributed LLM training.

entry.title: Dynamic Alignment Compensation for Hallucination Mitigation in Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Kairong Yu, Zixin Zhu, Le Yu, Hongwei Wang

entry.summary: DAC is a training-free inference-time method that detects cross-modal representation divergence across decoder layers and generation steps in large vision-language models and selectively applies lightweight residual compensation to stabilize token prediction and reduce hallucination. It targets an internal representation-dynamics failure mode left unexplored by external-supervision or calibration approaches. Practical mitigation without retraining.

entry.title: Conformal Risk-Averse Decision Making with Optimized Certainty Equivalent Risk Control

author.name: Amirmohammad Farzaneh, Osvaldo Simeone

entry.summary: Develops risk-averse decision making using optimized certainty equivalent (OCE) risk metrics generalizing CVaR and mean-variance, showing the optimal policy reduces to conformal prediction sets under CVaR. Provides data-driven calibration with high-probability risk control for unknown distributions.

entry.title: A comprehensive and trustworthy benchmark of AI methods for change detection in Earth observation

author.name: Tadej Tomani\v{c}, Alice Baudhuin, Jan Soto\v{s}ek, Jure Brence, Pan\v{c}e Panov, Nikola Simidjievski, Dragi Kocev

entry.summary: A standardized open-source benchmark evaluating ten deep learning architectures (CNNs to ViTs) for Earth observation change detection across ten datasets with identical protocols, covering both accuracy and computational efficiency. Addresses inconsistent evaluation in the field.

entry.title: On the Maintenance and Co-evolution of Agent Plugins: An Empirical Study of Claude Code Plugin Marketplaces

author.name: Ahmed Hereiz, Yingzhe Lyu, Hao Li, Bram Adams, Ahmed E. Hassan

entry.summary: An empirical study of Claude Code plugin marketplaces examining how agent plugins composed of instruction files, scripts, and configs are maintained and co-evolve, in contrast to traditional software packages. Early empirical grounding for an emerging software ecosystem.

entry.title: HalluPrism: When Multimodal Uncertainty Should Diagnose, Not Decide

author.name: Aman Prakash, Sourish Dasgupta, Tanmoy Chakraborty

entry.summary: HalluPrism is a behavioral diagnostic for multimodal LLMs that re-runs answers under targeted probes (visual degradation, blank images, grounding checks) to produce failure-family signatures, showing image-removal confidence retention dominates and coordinates must be read jointly.

entry.title: SS-ESOAP: Self-Scaled Adaptive Preconditioning for Physics-Informed Learning

author.name: Guangyuan Wang, Mads Toftrup, Sebastian Loeschcke, Yixuan Wang, Anima Anandkumar

entry.summary: Introduces SS-ESOAP, augmenting SOAP-style Kronecker preconditioning for PINNs with a scalar secant-energy correction and adaptive basis updates with variance-state downscaling. Achieves lowest final PDE residual on six of eight benchmarks with theoretical characterization.

entry.title: Structure Aware Neural Architecture Search for Mixture of Experts

author.name: Petr Babkin, Oleg Bakhteev

entry.summary: Proposes a NAS framework for Mixture-of-Experts that jointly optimizes data-cluster-to-expert assignment and per-expert architectures via a cluster-aware likelihood maximization solved with generalized EM and an adaptively refined surrogate.

entry.title: Tensor Methods for Language Models: From Token Representation to Training, Adaptation, Inference, Compression, and Interpretability

author.name: Matvei Tarasov, Salman Ahmadi-Asl, Andre L. F. de Almeida, Andrzej Cichocki

entry.summary: A comprehensive survey of tensor methods for LLMs organized by a seven-stage lifecycle taxonomy covering tokenization, embeddings, pretraining, adaptation, compression, inference, and interpretability, plus a component view of attention and feed-forward layers. Authored by leading tensor-decomposition researchers including Cichocki. A useful unifying reference for an underexploited structural perspective on LLMs.

entry.title: PLC-DPO: Posterior Label Correction in Noisy and Ambiguous Preference Optimization

author.name: Boryeong Cho, Sumyeong Ahn, Se-Young Yun

entry.summary: Proposes PLC-DPO, which routes each preference pair as clean, flipped, or tie using the calibrated policy-reference margin as online evidence, reframing noisy preference learning as active correction of supervision direction and strength rather than filtering. Validated across 57 dataset-model-benchmark cells. Addresses a real weakness of DPO under noisy preference data.

entry.title: Reward-Oracle MCTS for Formal Theorem Proving: Sample-Efficient Search and the Need for Kernel-Level Proof Auditing

author.name: Bodla Krishna Vamshi, Haizhao Yang

entry.summary: The authors propose a three-role MCTS framework for Lean 4 theorem proving that treats the compiler purely as a scalar reward oracle rather than feeding verbose error text into context, improving sample efficiency. They also argue for kernel-level proof auditing to ensure search-time guarantees.

entry.title: mmIR: Frequency-Space Inverse Rendering for 3D Millimeter-Wave Radar ADC Synthesis

author.name: Adnan Armouti, Yixuan Gao, Rajalakshmi Nandakumar

entry.summary: mmIR is an open-source differentiable FMCW radar inverse renderer that fits a physics-based forward model to real captures and re-renders from dense virtual apertures, synthesizing high-resolution 3D radar ADC data to address radar data scarcity. It targets the bottleneck where learned synthesis methods lack the very data they need.

entry.title: Optimally Selecting Representative Agents from a Metric Space

author.name: Benjamin Cookson, Eva Deltl, Yeeseok Oh

entry.summary: Proves that proportionally fair clustering satisfying the 2-Droop core always exists when centers can be placed at agent locations, matching a known lower bound and improving the best previous approximation from 1+sqrt(2). Also shows such clustering can be achieved using a restricted set of centers.

entry.title: Signed random Fourier features for fast density estimation with indefinite kernels

author.name: Xie Wang, Nicolas Langren\'e, Wen Chen

entry.summary: Extends random Fourier features to indefinite kernels via signed feature constructions, enabling fast O(N) kernel density estimation with kernels popular in KDE (such as the parabolic kernel) that violate positive definiteness.

entry.title: ARMOR: Manifold-Oriented Training for Adversarially Robust Aerial Object Detection under Data Scarcity

author.name: Haoran Wang, Matthew Lau, Alec Helbling, Matthew Hull, ShengYun Peng, Mansi Phute, Martin Andreoni, Willian T. Lunardi, Duen Horng Chau, Wenke Lee

entry.summary: Introduces ARMOR, an adversarial defense for aerial object detection under training-data scarcity, adapting on-manifold adversarial training to low-data regimes where deployment sites have hundreds rather than tens of thousands of labeled images, targeting robustness to universal adversarial patches.

entry.title: Towards a Systems Foundation for Agentic Skills: Architecture, Lifecycle, and Security

author.name: Sanket Badhe, Deep Shah, Priyanka Tiwari, Nehal Kathrotia

entry.summary: Establishes a systems foundation and reference architecture for agentic skills - modular, reusable, executable procedural artifacts that externalize execution knowledge for LLM agents - delineating lifecycle management, architecture layers, and security considerations for a skills ecosystem.

entry.title: Enabling Proactive Spoken Turns via a Generalized Style-Aware Full-Duplex Framework

author.name: Tianrui Pan, Qinglin Zhang, Chong Deng, Luyao Cheng, Qian Chen, Wen Wang, Jie Tang, Gangshan Wu, Jie Liu

entry.summary: Proposes a generalized style-aware full-duplex dialogue framework with LPS-TC, a lightweight plug-and-play proactive speech turn controller covering reactive and proactive turn behaviors. Enables half-duplex dialogue models to gain full-duplex capabilities like timely interruptions and backchannels.

entry.title: When to Adapt: Conditional Memory Adapters for Retention-Preserving Domain Specialization

author.name: Jiayu Hou, Lei Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Engram Adapter, which repurposes pretraining-time conditional memory as a post-hoc adapter for frozen LLMs, using n-gram matching with occupancy tracking and a learned gate to apply residual injection selectively on in-domain inputs. Preserves out-of-domain performance better than always-on PEFT.

entry.title: AlgoWorlds: Benchmarking Tool Use for Global Optimization in Algorithmic Worlds

author.name: Zixiang Xu, Jiaan Wang, Fandong Meng

entry.summary: Introduces AlgoWorlds, a benchmark transforming formally specified combinatorial optimization problems into partially observed tool-use environments with verifiable global optima, testing whether agents can turn tool-gathered information into globally optimal decisions rather than merely feasible ones.

entry.title: SIC-Agents: Benchmarking and Building an Adaptive Simulator for Pediatric Serious Illness Communication Training

author.name: Zihan Wang, Anita Marie Slominska, Rennie Bimman, Elizabeth Di Flumeri, Amanda Mayappo-Neeposh, Conall Francoeur, Tamara Ellen Carver, Xiao-Wen Chang, Doina Precup, Esin Darici Haritaoglu, Ismail Haritaoglu, Akshatha Arodi, Naomi Goloff

entry.summary: Builds the first benchmark suite and adaptive simulator for pediatric serious illness communication training, developed with educators and clinicians, with PitfallBench and DialogueBench evaluating turn-level and dialogue-level simulator behavior. Targets multi-party, emotionally complex clinical training scenarios.

entry.title: Beyond Surface Alignment: Grounding the Dynamics of Situational Understanding and Generative Control in LLMs

author.name: Chenghao Yang

entry.summary: A thesis proposing Grounded Alignment, arguing current alignment tuning optimizes surface behaviors while leaving models situationally brittle; introduces SitTest showing SOTA models fail to maintain consistent mental models of changing environments and ReCode for generation grounding.

entry.title: MI-Distillation: Selecting from Model-Interpolated Instruct-Reasoning Data Spectrum for Chain-of-Thought Distillation

author.name: Yangsong Lan, Renkai Hu, HongKai Zheng, Bo Zhang, Renzhi Wang, Hongliang Dai, Piji Li

entry.summary: Analyzes why Long CoT distillation underperforms Short CoT from a gradient-centric perspective, showing Long CoT induces larger gradient magnitudes and more concentrated update directions, worsening with student capacity, and proposes MI-Distillation to select from model-interpolated instruct-reasoning data accordingly.

entry.title: Not All Fallbacks Are Failures: Understanding and Recovering from Fallbacks in Mobile Voice Assistants

author.name: Phillip Schneider, Alexandre Mercier, Joshua Oehms, Kristiina Jokinen, Florian Matthes

entry.summary: Studies fallback handling in a deployed smartwatch voice assistant using six months of data from 500+ users, yielding 3,030 real fallback-triggering interactions. Shows generic fallback messages fail to resolve interaction failures and proposes recovery strategies.

entry.title: CLIN: an Objective Framework for Evaluating Creativity in Short Persian Literary Text

author.name: Mohammad Reza Modarres, Armin Tourajmehr, Yadollah Yaghoobzadeh, Mohammad Taher Pilehvar

entry.summary: CLIN evaluates how reliably LLMs judge creativity in short Persian literary texts across multiple strategies, finding stronger agreement on structured TTCT-derived dimensions than subjective ones like Emotion and Attractiveness. Few-shot prompting, ensembling, and multi-agent debate give no consistent improvement.

entry.title: Context-Aware Interleaved Batching for WhisperX

author.name: Carlos Bain, Max Bain

entry.summary: The authors propose Context-Aware Interleaved Batching for WhisperX, using VAD-derived segment boundaries to maintain continuous historical context across batched audio segments while retaining high throughput. This resolves the trade-off between WhisperX batching speed and Whisper sequential context, reducing word error rate and improving proper noun transcription. Author credibility is strong given overlap with the original WhisperX team.

entry.title: RegDivergence-101: An LLM Benchmark for Cross-Jurisdiction Regulatory Contradiction Detection in Life Sciences

author.name: Chuchu Wu, Zhiyin Zhou, Jingzhuo Hu, Liang You

entry.summary: RegDivergence-101 introduces cross-jurisdiction regulatory divergence detection for life sciences, classifying FDA versus EMA requirement pairs as AGREE, DIVERGE, or directional SILENT. It targets a task currently done manually by regulatory-affairs experts when sponsors file in both the US and EU. The benchmark operationalizes a real, high-stakes compliance problem for LLMs.

entry.title: Multi-Agent Self-Improving Reinforcement Learning for Video Reasoning

author.name: Mingwen Zhang, Jisheng Dang, Minqiang Yang, Bimei Wang, Bin Hu, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: The paper proposes a multi-agent RL framework for video reasoning coupling a trainable Grounder with a frozen Verifier that assigns query-conditioned segment scores, using a group-relative policy gradient favoring trajectories that outperform within-input peers. This extends verification from inference-time reranking to training-time guidance for grounded video QA and temporal grounding. Co-author Tat-Seng Chua adds credibility.

entry.title: Rate-Coding Bundle Memory: A Unified Model of Memory and Control for Symbolic Computation in the Brain

author.name: Teun van Gils, Rowan P. Sommers, Markus Ostarek, Peter Hagoort

entry.summary: RCBM proposes a neurobiologically plausible hybrid model combining rate-coded symbols in continuous space with a bundle memory system, grounded in the Symbolic Subsystem Hypothesis. It aims to explain cognitive phenomena including one-shot learning, pattern separation, and binding, bridging connectionist and symbolic systems. The work is a theoretical contribution bridging neuroscience and cognitive architectures.

entry.title: ContextBias: Controlled Evaluation of Bias Persistence Under Context Shift in Text-to-Image Models

author.name: Shaghayegh Kolli, Sina Emami, Moreno D'Inc\`a, Pouyan Nejadi, Nicu Sebe, Massimiliano Mancini, Jana Diesner

entry.summary: ContextBias is a controlled evaluation framework and benchmark (92 roles, 1,656 prompts, 66,240 generated images) testing whether role-linked stereotypical associations in text-to-image models persist under contextual shift. Evaluating four state-of-the-art models, it isolates the effect of contextual variation on visual representations of professions. The question of bias stability versus context sensitivity is a genuine open issue in generative fairness.

entry.title: Geometry of Divergence: Tracking Hidden-State Trajectories for Adaptive Multi-Turn Reasoning

author.name: Jie Liang, Zhengxin Yu, Hamid Nasiri, Peter Garraghan

entry.summary: Formulates multi-turn LLM agent reasoning as a hidden-state trajectory characterized by temporal curvature and variance slope, using these geometric signals to detect representation drift and adaptively manage context under resource constraints. Evaluated across four tasks and three LLMs. Offers a mechanistic lens on long-horizon agent reliability.

entry.title: Defending Wearable VLMs Against Private Attribute Inference

author.name: Zhimin Li, Pan Wang, Jingxian Chen, Yuantao Tang, Anthony Chen, Qian Lou, Jingtong Hu

entry.summary: Investigates privacy leakage in split VLM inference for wearable devices, where intermediate visual tokens transmitted off-device can reveal private attributes about the wearer even when final responses are benign, and proposes defenses for this joint privacy-utility problem. Addresses an underexplored leakage surface in egocentric AI.

entry.title: Foundational feature fusion for conditional flow matching in 6D pose estimation

author.name: Amir Hamza, Davide Boscaini, Fabio Poiesi

entry.summary: FunFlow6D uses features from geometric and appearance foundation models with conditional flow matching for 6D pose estimation, removing the need for task-specific encoder training. A cross-attention fusion mechanism resolves pose ambiguities. This shows foundation-feature reuse can replace supervised encoders in a state-of-the-art pose pipeline.

entry.title: LightFuse: Relightable Interactive Gaussian Scene Reconstruction via Multi-Scan Fusion and 2D Gaussian Ray Tracing

author.name: Haonan Zhou, Gaoxiang Linghu, Youlin Jia, Hongyu Cui, Kewei Wei, Kaiyue Zhou, Bruce X. B. Yu, Gaoang Wang

entry.summary: LightFuse reconstructs relightable interactive scenes from multi-object scans using 2D Gaussians with explicit material-illumination decomposition and physically based ray-traced relighting. It fuses observations across arrangements into a shared background plus movable objects and refines geometry for consistent shadows under edits. Advances interactive scene reconstruction beyond baked lighting.

entry.title: Neural video codecs quality assessment dataset and benchmark

author.name: Nikolay Safonov, Nikita Gornostaev, Alexandra Dubonos, Dmitriy Vatolin

entry.summary: Presents a large-scale subjective dataset and benchmark for quality assessment of neural video codecs versus traditional codecs, targeting the novel temporal compression paradigms NVCs introduce. Fills an infrastructure gap as deep learning enters video compression. Valuable community resource from an established video-quality group (MSU/Vatolin).

entry.title: TRINITY: A Multi-Perspective Benchmark for Personal-Style Video Highlight Detection

author.name: Qianqian Chen, Hyun Bin Kim, Denzel Elden Wijaya, Yang Yi, Bo Liu, Yangkai Ding

entry.summary: GATE fuses reliability-gated Gaussian evidence for training-free transductive test-time adaptation of vision-language models with all parameters frozen.

entry.title: Efficient and High-Quality Depth Estimation via Pixel-Space Diffusion with Linear Attention

author.name: Bingde Liu, Wu Ran, Jinglei Zhang, Huanhuan Yuan, Chao Ma

entry.summary: Lapis combines linear attention with one-step pixel-space diffusion for efficient high-fidelity monocular depth estimation, using a coarse-to-fine hierarchy to fix structural consistency issues of naive linear attention. Targets the O(N^2) cost of scaling generative depth models.

entry.title: Dynamic Hub-and-Spoke Memory for Streaming Video Understanding

author.name: Xinru Jiang, Lin Zhao, Xi Xiao, Yunbei Zhang, Janet Wang, Chenrui Ma, Haolin Li, Yanzhi Wang, Yifan Gong, Octavia Camps

entry.summary: D-HSM is a training-free streaming video understanding framework that compresses distant history into an entity-centered hub-and-spoke textual memory while keeping recent frames as visual tokens, retrieving question-aware evidence on demand. Balances long-range memory with fine-grained perception.

entry.title: ImageCAS-X: a dataset and benchmark for coronary artery segmentation and centerline extraction in coronary CT angiography

author.name: Kit M. Bransby, Esther {\O}ksnebjerg, Kristoffer Kj{\ae}r, Jacob Kirkeby, Yasmin El Youssef, A\"ida Jim\'enez, Philip R. Pedersson, Martina C. de Knegt, Klaus F. Kofoed, Rasmus R. Paulsen

entry.summary: ImageCAS-X provides voxel-wise lumen annotations, centerlines, and mesh surfaces for 800 coronary CT angiography scans, plus benchmarks of established segmentation methods. Addresses a key data bottleneck for quantitative atherosclerosis analysis.

entry.title: MEOM: Multi-View Expected-OKS Maximization for Human Pose Triangulation

author.name: Ziliang Xiong, Henglin Shi, Per-Erik Forssen

entry.summary: MEOM formulates multi-view human pose triangulation as Multi-view Expected-OKS Maximization, using full 2D heatmap probability mass rather than collapsed peaks, with highest-density-region calibration for heatmap reliability. Principled fix to a known fragility of algebraic triangulation.

entry.title: Failure or Drift? Evaluating Monocular SLAM under Synthetic and Real-World Corruptions

author.name: Abhay Skaria Thomas, Shashank Agnihotri, Margret Keuper

entry.summary: Presents UFPR-PEs, a Brazilian face recognition bias-evaluation benchmark from videos of elected politicians annotated with official self-declared census race/color categories including parda, absent from US/Europe-centric schemas. Built from compressed public video preserving hard samples.

entry.title: Rad-R: A Raw-ADC Radar Dataset and Capture-Invariant SSM for Hardware-Fault Diagnosis

author.name: Mainak Mallick, Junghwan Yim, Seung-Kyum Choi

entry.summary: Rad-R introduces a raw-ADC automotive mmWave radar dataset paired with calibrated hardware faults (vibration, antenna misalignment, radome blockage) at measured severities, plus a capture-invariant state-space model for fault diagnosis. It fills a genuine data gap since radar hardware faults require physical measurement.

entry.title: Multimodal Shared Latent Representation of Narration, Microscope and iOCT Images for Phase Recognition in Vitreoretinal Surgery

author.name: Onur Izmitlioglu, Shervin Dehghani, Tarek Ghannoum, Benedikt Schworm, Nassir Navab

entry.summary: The paper builds a shared latent representation across surgical narration, microscope video, and intraoperative OCT for phase recognition in vitreoretinal surgery, using microscope views as an anchor to bridge modalities. It exploits abundant online narration as semantic supervision where synchronized intraoperative multimodal data is scarce.

entry.title: Is Deformable Image Registration Ready for Brain Metastasis Reirradiation Dose Accumulation? A Longitudinal MRI Benchmark of Registration Accuracy

author.name: Hengjie Liu, Manju Sharma, Xinyi Fu, Di Xu, Ke Sheng

entry.summary: This benchmark evaluates deformable image registration methods for brain metastasis reirradiation dose accumulation on 87 manually screened longitudinal MRI lesion pairs, a controlled but clinically meaningful test case. It provides a rigorous clinical benchmark for learning-based and optimization-based DIR.

entry.title: RePair: Turning Retrieval Failures into Counterfactual Hard Pairs

author.name: Siyi Liu, Xiaorong Zhu, Enjun Du, Xinyu Zuo, Lisheng Duan, Haijin Liang, Jin Ma, Junfu Pu, Yongqi Zhang

entry.summary: RePair turns retrieval failures into counterfactual hard positives by minimally correcting the failure-causing residual of top-ranked false positives, then training CLIP-style dual encoders on these constructed pairs. It combines hard-sample mining and synthetic augmentation while conditioning hardness on actual model failures.

entry.title: Autoregressive Mosaics: Probing 2D Spatial Reasoning in Text-Only Language Models

author.name: Ashwin Nedungadi, Stefan Oehmcke, Stefan L\"udtke

entry.summary: Autoregressive Mosaics introduces AM-Bench, which separates geometry translation from open-ended 2D layout composition in text-only code-generating LLMs, finding all eight evaluated models translate specified geometry reliably but degrade on open-ended layout. It probes whether text-trained LLMs possess internal spatial representations.

entry.title: "More Is Different'' in Neural Circuits: Algebraic Emergence of Effective Theories in Canonical Recurrent Motifs of Biological Neuronal Networks

author.name: Nima Dehghani

entry.summary: This theoretical paper represents canonical neural circuit motifs (divisive normalization, winner-take-all) algebraically as finite transformation systems, analyzing transition monoids to distinguish emergent structure from inherited structure upon composition. It shows aperiodic updates can generate non-aperiodic monoids, formalizing emergence in neural motifs.

entry.title: Toward Trustworthy Robot-Assisted Sliding Palpation for Shallow Vessel Localisation with a Calibrated Digital Twin

author.name: Piotr Blaszyk, Wen Fan, Kaizhong Deng, Daniel Elson, Dandan Zhang

entry.summary: Presents a robot-assisted sliding palpation framework that uses a calibrated digital twin to generate labeled tactile training data for locating shallow subsurface vessels, reducing reliance on costly real-world sensor data. Bayesian-optimization-based domain adaptation calibrates the twin against real trajectories, and a spatio-temporal GNN performs vessel classification. Relevant to safe robot-assisted venous access and vessel-aware manipulation.

entry.title: Self-Aware Active Learning Enables Continual Improvement in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Dong Hu, Chao Huang, Carman K. M. Lee, Dimitrios Kanoulas

entry.summary: SAGE is an active learning framework for autonomous driving in which a predictive world model generates fear (short-horizon risk and uncertainty) and curiosity (novelty) signals, letting agents estimate their own incompetence, seek assistance, and convert safety-critical encounters into targeted improvement. Aimed at post-training adaptation for long-tail events.

entry.title: Learning to infer and manipulate through distributed whole-arm interaction in a soft robot

author.name: Chuhan Zhang, Ebrahim Shahabi, Kseniia Khomenko, Wei Pan, Cosimo Della Santina

entry.summary: Introduces a physical intelligence framework for soft robots in which distributed whole-arm compliant interactions jointly reveal task-relevant information and organize manipulation behavior, inspired by elephants and octopuses, treating contact as an information source rather than a disturbance to reject.

entry.title: SleepWalking: Privileged Representation Shaping for End-to-End Blind Locomotion in Legged Robots

author.name: Zheng Pan, Tenghui Wang, Peilin Li, Shiyu Zhou, Hao Sun, Yan Ma, Liang Yu, Liang He

entry.summary: SleepWalking reframes partial observability in blind legged locomotion as an information-retention problem and proposes SWAQ, a one-stage end-to-end framework using next-step privileged physical reconstruction to shape internal representations that retain task-relevant information, avoiding explicit state estimators or long histories.

entry.title: Autonomously Acquiring Robot Manipulation Skills with Language-Driven Quality-Diversity

author.name: \'Emiland Garrab\'e, Mahdi Khoramshahi, St\'ephane Doncieux

entry.summary: Combines quality-diversity algorithms with LLM-driven specification so robots autonomously acquire diverse motion primitive archives from free-form natural language task descriptions, removing the need for hand-written fitness and diversity metrics while retaining zero-shot adaptability.

entry.title: A Catalogue of Corrigibility Counter Arguments

author.name: Felix Moses

entry.summary: A catalogue of counterarguments to corrigibility as an alignment target, written in the context of renewed mainstream interest following the Hugging Face incident, engaging with the CAST strategy and industry incentives around helpfulness.

entry.title: Update on Security at METR

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: METR discloses two security incidents in 2026: a stolen inference API key in March and systematic infrastructure probing with an unsuccessful access attempt in May, reporting no sensitive data accessed and detailing their subsequent security investments. No evidence found of agents hacking third parties during evaluations.

entry.title: PCFBench: A Diagnostic Benchmark for Product Carbon Footprint Estimation

author.name: Krishna Rao, Andrew Dumit, Shaena Ulissi, Jacob Feintzeig, P. James Joyce, Daniel Frank, Steven Watson, Jonathan Glidden, Gizem Ilayda Dinc, Travis M. Kwee

entry.summary: Introduces PCFBench, reportedly the first benchmark to decompose product carbon footprint estimation into 614 expert-labeled independently evaluable tasks spanning decomposition, retrieval, ontology matching, and numerical extraction, exposing error sources that total-emissions scoring hides and that isolated sub-task scoring misses. Targets high-stakes domain workflows where intermediate correctness matters. A useful new evaluation surface for agentic systems.

entry.title: AERA: Adaptive Evidence Residual Allocation for Efficient Test-Time Reasoning

author.name: Ziming Wang, Ivor Tsang, Hangwei Qian

entry.summary: Demonstrates that checkpoint-level correctness during test-time scaling evolves non-monotonically, so observable evidence strength can mislead stopping decisions, and introduces AERA, a learned sequential controller that allocates additional computation where recovery is likely rather than trusting confidence or agreement. A conceptual insight plus an adaptive-stopping method. A solid contribution to adaptive test-time compute.

entry.title: Detecting AI Impostors: How Do Middle Schoolers Identify LLM Agents in a Live Collaborative Setting?

author.name: Dan Schumacher, Pragathi Durga Rajarajan, Haven Kotara, Roman Rendon, Kosi Atupulazi, Deepti Tagare, Ismaila Temitayo Sanusi, Fred G. Martin, Anthony Rios

entry.summary: Introduces DoppelBot, a cooperative social deduction game for studying how middle schoolers detect AI impersonation by LLM agents. Repeated exposure improves detection accuracy, driven by a shift from surface cues to deeper strategies, and the game prompts reflection on privacy and impersonation.

entry.title: Retrieving Relations, Detecting Fallacies: A RAG Approach to Political Debate Analysis

author.name: Deborah Dore, Greta Damo, Elena Cabrio, Serena Villata

entry.summary: Combines retrieval-augmented generation with argumentative discourse structure to detect fallacies in political debates, retrieving both topical world knowledge and relations among arguments rather than encoding structure as static classifier features. Targets a high-stakes misinformation-adjacent task where surface text alone is insufficient. A solid applied contribution to argument mining.

entry.title: ReToolSQL: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Robust Text-to-SQL

author.name: Pratik Kakkar, Chandra Dhir, Ravi Shankar, Pareekshit Reddy Gaddam, Anup Shirgaonkar

entry.summary: Combines a supervised warm-start on rejection-sampled reasoning traces with multi-turn agentic reinforcement fine-tuning over tool-use trajectories for text-to-SQL, arguing the two stages act on complementary axes of solution diversity and iterative recovery. Extends single-turn execution-feedback RL toward robust multi-turn refinement. Competent post-training work in a crowded area.

entry.title: CoRe-MoE: Compact Reusable MoE for Continual Multimodal Instruction Tuning

author.name: Runze Liu, Naibin Gu, Mingxu Ai, Yuqing Li, Peng Fu, Zheng Lin, Weiping Wang

entry.summary: Analyzes the SVD of task-specific LoRA updates in continual multimodal instruction tuning, finds substantial overlap in input and output subspaces across tasks, and proposes CoRe-MoE, which reuses shared subspace experts and learns lightweight task coordinates instead of full new LoRA experts per task, cutting parameter overhead while preserving prior knowledge. A practical efficiency contribution to continual learning. Competent and moderately novel.

entry.title: Rubric-to-Code Credit Assignment for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Rui Jin, Jikai Chen, Yihan Chen, Hao Zhou, Demin Zhu, Kaichen Yang, Dong Wang, Linjian Mo, Chenyi Zhuang

entry.summary: Tackles the weakness of GRPO-style sequence-level rewards in interactive web-app generation by converting rubric-level functional feedback into localized token-level credit over the code regions that satisfy each requirement. A targeted credit-assignment improvement for reinforcement learning on structured artifacts. Aligned with the broader move toward fine-grained rewards in RL from verifiable signals.

entry.title: Learning from Hard Prompts: Difficulty-aware Advantage Amplification in Dynamic Sampling

author.name: Siyuan Gan, Yuhan Li, Xiran Wang, Linjian Meng, Boyan Wang, Zhen Zhao, Jing Huo, Lei Bai, Yang Gao

entry.summary: Theoretically shows that dynamic sampling in DAPO wastes hard prompts by filtering them when zero advantages yield zero gradients, asymmetrically amplifying advantage estimates, and proposes difficulty-aware advantage amplification to exploit hard-to-sample correct responses. A useful theoretical refinement of a widely used RL recipe. Incremental but well motivated.

entry.title: MAP: A Benchmark on Multimodal Accessibility Planning for Real World Places

author.name: Jason Armitage, Ioannis Tsochantaridis, Linda Mazzone, Chuqiao Yan, Srini Narayanan, Sarah Ebling

entry.summary: MAP is the first benchmark evaluating multimodal AI systems as assistants for users with accessibility requirements when planning visits to real-world places. It introduces claim verification and visual evidence retrieval assessments around point-of-interest accessibility features. It highlights a socially impactful blind spot in current multimodal evaluation.

entry.title: RetailAgent: Structured Adverse Timing in Self-Conditioned Multimodal LLM Trading Agents

author.name: Yupeng Zhang, Liuyuan Jiang, Hongyi Huang, Bingheng Li, Lisha Chen

entry.summary: RetailAgent examines whether LLM agents acting as intraday equity traders exhibit predictable directional structure, using an exposure-matched measure on long/flat decisions. It finds persistent negative timing skill across modality, horizon, state, and model family, meaning the agents systematically buy at unfavorable moments. This is a cautionary result for deploying LLM agents in financial markets.

entry.title: Logos: An Agent Harness on a Cross-Process Bus

author.name: Hanzhang Jia, Liheng Zeng, Hao Cheng, Yi Gao, Bo Ma

entry.summary: Logos generalizes a formally treated spatiotemporal-composability calculus for agent capability assembly from a single process to a cross-process bus, exploiting the statelessness of language models to keep cross-step state outside the model. This removes the single failure domain that suspends all components when the host process dies. It connects formal agent theory with systems-level fault tolerance.

entry.title: SciReC: Diagnostic Evaluation of Multimodal, Multi-Turn Relational Reasoning with Adaptive Interaction

author.name: Nilay Yilmaz, Naga Sai Abhiram Kusumba, Stella Wenxing Liu, Yezhou Yang

entry.summary: SciReC is a model-adaptive multimodal academic dialog benchmark for relational reasoning (analogical, structural, cause-effect) in multimodal LLMs, paired with DMRA, a deficit-based diagnostic framework that quantifies contributions of visual understanding, knowledge, and memory recall. It moves evaluation from aggregate scores toward component-level diagnosis. Useful for locating specific capability gaps in MLLMs.

entry.title: Select, Don't Train: The Benefits of Modular Entity Disambiguation with LLM-Based Selection

author.name: Fina Polat, Daniel Daza, Pengyu Zhang, Klim Zaporojets, Paul Groth

entry.summary: This paper systematically studies modular entity disambiguation, separating candidate retrieval from LLM-based selection instead of training dual-encoder models that must balance recall and fine-grained selection in one embedding space. It clarifies the interplay between retrieval strategies and LLM selectors and avoids costly retraining as knowledge graphs change. Practical guidance for KG construction pipelines.

entry.title: XHotpotQA: A Benchmark for Cross-Lingual Knowledge Composition in Multi-Hop Question Answering

author.name: Iman Barati, Arash Ghafouri, Behrouz Minaei-Bidgoli
