author.name: Mahdi Babaei, Xueshen Li, Yutao Kuang, Jolene P. Reid, Yu Gan

entry.summary: MAIL is a memory-augmented, adaptive framework that uses LLMs to generate experimentally meaningful hypotheses in chemistry by navigating the chemical literature incrementally rather than relying on static inspiration corpora. It targets a real bottleneck in AI-driven scientific discovery, moving beyond human-in-the-loop pipelines.

entry.title: A comprehensive and trustworthy benchmark of AI methods for change detection in Earth observation

author.name: Tadej Tomani\v{c}, Alice Baudhuin, Jan Soto\v{s}ek, Jure Brence, Pan\v{c}e Panov, Nikola Simidjievski, Dragi Kocev

entry.summary: A standardized open-source benchmark evaluating ten deep learning architectures for Earth observation change detection across ten heterogeneous datasets under identical protocols, examining both predictive accuracy and computational efficiency. Addresses inconsistent evaluation practices in the field.

entry.title: PanelShield: Verifiable Closed-Loop Safe Planning for Robotic Industrial Panel Operation

author.name: Guipeng Xin, Jiahe Xu, Chenhui Wan, Jie Liu, Youmin Hu, Zhongxu Hu

entry.summary: PanelShield provides verifiable closed-loop safe planning for industrial panel operation, generating action primitives from manual evidence and enforcing correctness via dual formal verification with LTL and a Safety FSM. Offers computable, localizable, and reproducible violation detection and repair for foundation-model planners.

entry.title: Fidelity Is Not Enough: Dispatch-Level Instrumentation for Agentic Datasheet Extraction

author.name: Qing Ye, Meng-Hsuan Lin

entry.summary: Documents a silent failure in agentic datasheet extraction where a structured-output constraint disabled tool use and a model fabricated source text while passing fidelity checks, motivating dispatch-level instrumentation with per-tool traces, a failure-attribution classifier, and a silent-failure detector.

entry.title: Dandelion: A Spherical Flower for Neural Simulation of Planetary Dynamics

author.name: Till Muser, Giovanni Abati, Ivan Dokmani\'c

entry.summary: Dandelion is a natively spherical version of the Flower warp-based neural PDE solver, addressing distortions of Euclidean architectures on spherical domains relevant to planetary dynamics and other spherical simulations.

entry.title: Beyond Procrustes distances: a multilinear Gromov-Wasserstein distance capturing chirality

author.name: Cl\'ement Soubrier, Geoffrey Woollard, Andrew Warren, Khanh Dao Duc

entry.summary: The paper introduces a multilinear generalization of the Gromov-Wasserstein objective yielding the Chiral Gromov-Wasserstein distance, the first OT-based shape distance sensitive to chirality, with robustness properties and applications where mirror-image discrimination matters (e.g., molecular science).

entry.title: Localizing Global Discrepancies: Marginal Contributions and Contextual Anomaly Detection

author.name: Tommaso dorigo

entry.summary: DARTS analyzes representation bias in decoder-only model merging and proposes decoder-aware representation tuning via a surgery-style correction, addressing position-dependent bias accumulation caused by causal attention masks that encoder-focused prior work did not face.

entry.title: INSPIRE: An Internalize-Then-Improve Approach for Example-Driven Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Shuai Wang, Jiayi Kuang, Yinghui Li, Haojing Huang, Xinnian Liang, Ying Shen, Liang Lin

entry.summary: INSPIRE targets example-driven mathematical reasoning (e.g., constructing counterexamples) in LLMs, using a staged internalize-then-improve approach with preference optimization to overcome the difficulty of building effective preference pairs for a capability the model lacks.

entry.title: AI Writers Have a Consistent Stylometric Footprint, but AI Editors Do Not

author.name: Zhengyang Shan, Yukyung Lee, Sophie Hao

entry.summary: The study shows AI generation leaves a consistent stylometric footprint (mainly entropy and lexical diversity features) across 8 LLMs and 5 domains, but AI editing of human text does not leave a comparable trace, complicating detection of LLM-edited content.

entry.title: What Makes Agent Memory Useful for Reliable Unanswerable Question Handling?

author.name: Chuanyuan Tan, Junjie Yu, Yuxin Wang, Yining Zheng, Xipeng Qiu, Wenliang Chen

entry.summary: A systematic study of agent memory for handling unanswerable questions under a unified agentic RAG framework, finding that memory gains are selective, fragile under dataset shift, and that cross-model memory reuse works better than cross-dataset transfer.

entry.title: SURE-Challenge: Evaluating Speech Evidence Before Speech-LLM Generation

author.name: Mengzhe Geng

entry.summary: SURE-Challenge defines an admission-control benchmark deciding whether an audio waveform should even be sent to a speech LLM, testing rejection of unsupported silence, noise, tones, and babble; raw Qwen2-Audio rejects only 15/204 unsupported inputs while a simple energy-plus-Whisper rule rejects 196/204.

entry.title: Benchmarking large language model agent societies against human behavioural distributions

author.name: Raad Bin Tareaf

entry.summary: SILICA is an open instrument for benchmarking LLM agent societies against human behavioral distributions, testing agreement with human anchors, robustness to apparatus perturbations, and whether apparent social dynamics reflect genuine interaction or memorization of published experiments.

entry.title: Temporal Tree of Thought: Reasoning-Guided Visual Cue Search for Long-Video Understanding

author.name: Ziling Huang, Shin'ichi Satoh

entry.summary: Temporal Tree of Thought is a training-free framework for long-video understanding that builds a hierarchical temporal tree via recursive clustering and performs coarse-to-fine visual cue search guided by reasoning, mimicking how humans first locate relevant segments then zoom into details.

entry.title: Visual Token Coding for Video Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Chenxin Fang, Tao Chen, JunChao You, Jun Peng, Yiyi Zhou, Rongrong Ji

entry.summary: Visual Token Coding adapts classical video coding principles like HEVC I/P-frame prediction to compress tokens for video MLLMs, enhanced with dynamic resolution, token allocation, and top-K selection. Applied to three MLLMs it improves efficiency on multiple video benchmarks.

entry.title: NumBench: Diagnosing Counting Failures in Text-to-Image Models

author.name: Sandeep Wadhwa, Mayank Vatsa, Richa Singh, Parrva Chirag Shah, Prakhar Galriya

entry.summary: NumBench is a 640,000-prompt benchmark spanning 1,600 categories and counts from 1 to 100 that diagnoses counting failures in text-to-image models, paired with a process model predicting near-quadratic collision deficits and a scalable confidence-weighted evaluation metric.

entry.title: Focus Where It Counts: A Salience-Driven Vision-Language Model for Low Vision Assistance

author.name: Jiazhao Liang, Hao Huang, Shuaihang Yuan, Congcong Wen, Geeta Chandra Raju Bethala, Giles Hamilton-Fletcher, Yu Hao, John-Ross Rizzo, Mengyu Wang, Anthony Tzes, Yi Fang

entry.summary: This work presents a salience-driven captioning framework for low vision assistance, curating three salience-aware datasets with object-level importance annotations so that VLM outputs prioritize information most relevant to blind and low-vision users.

entry.title: GraspHOI: Full-Body 3D Human-Object Reconstruction with Finger-Level Grasps from a Single In-the-Wild Image

author.name: Semin Kim, Haechan Shin, Jongyoo Kim

entry.summary: GraspHOI is the first framework reconstructing full-body 3D human-object interaction from a single in-the-wild image while explicitly optimizing finger-level grasp articulation against category-agnostic reconstructed object geometry, with occlusion-aware palm alignment in metric camera space.

entry.title: LayerRecall: A State-Conditioned Memory Router for Long-Horizon Consistency in Video Generation

author.name: Yixuan Ding, Jiahao Kong, Wei Huang, Ruijie Quan, Yi Yang

entry.summary: LayerRecall observes that video DiT layers have distinct preferences for current, recent, and distant context, and introduces a layer-selective memory router that retrieves historical KV states and injects them only into appropriate layers for long-horizon consistency in autoregressive video generation.

entry.title: Low-Power End-to-End Cochlear Implant Speech Denoising with Spiking Neural Networks

author.name: Ludovic Boulanger, Sean U. N. Wood

entry.summary: TaintedPixels is a proactive defense embedding structured periodic perturbations into published facial videos that remain inconspicuous to viewers but become obvious when downstream black-box manipulation tools edit the content, extending proactive protection to video with a perceptual study.

entry.title: Beyond Relative Geometry: Metric-Aware Geometry Perception for Robotics

author.name: Fengjun Zhong, Congjia Chen, Zhaoxu Liu, Jinyang Du, Yuchen Gong, Enqi Mao, Ruihao Gong, ShuJie Wang, Xianglong Liu, Zhongliang Qiao

entry.summary: MAGP addresses the problem that embodied models reconstruct only relative, arbitrary-scale geometry, proposing a metric-aware plug-and-play framework with metric scale equivariant augmentation so predicted dimensions align with real-world robot actions.

entry.title: Distributed Model-Based Diffusion: Finite Horizon Contraction under Bounded Delay

author.name: Seth Golembeski, Keith L. Gibson, Alexander Gross, Shreyas Kousik, Anirban Mazumdar

entry.summary: This paper proves finite-horizon contraction and robustness to bounded communication delay for Distributed Model-Based Diffusion, a sampling-based MPC method for highly nonlinear, nonconvex multi-agent systems such as aerial vehicle fleets and intersections.

entry.title: openJiuwen: Beyond Static Harnesses for Long-Horizon Coding Agents

author.name: openJiuwen Team, Tao Yu, Xinyu Zhang, Qianqian Chen, Xiaoneng Xiang, Chia Kwangyang, Xingchen Huang, Ran Chen, Yangkai Ding, Zheng Wang, Yeo Boon Hong, Bingzheng Gan, Enrui Hu, Shuo Cheng, Deyang Li, Ruifeng Shi, Hongbo Wang, Qi Ye, Xuefeng Jin, Zhangchun Zhao

entry.summary: Presents openJiuwen, an open-source agent harness addressing structural composability and runtime adaptivity for long-horizon coding agents, allowing capability composition, reconfiguration, and evidence-driven runtime decisions across multi-agent coordination.

entry.title: REINS: Refusal-Enhanced Inhibitory Steering with Sparse Autoencoder Features

author.name: Kai-Xuan Ding, Hao-Xiang Xu, Ji-Hua Peng, Zi-Qi Chen, Jiaqi Wang, Zhen-Hua Ling

entry.summary: REINS improves SAE-based refusal steering with inhibitory feature directions, introducing the GUISE dataset of harmful prompts with complex wrappers after showing existing single-direction steering fails on them.

entry.title: ARC-CT: Anatomy-Routed Contrastive Vision-Language Learning for 3D Chest CT

author.name: Huseyin Umut Isik, Mehmet Alp Ozaydin, Sila Kurugol, \c{S}eyda Ertekin

entry.summary: ARC-CT introduces anatomy-routed contrastive vision-language learning for 3D chest CT, using region-aware objectives to handle small localized abnormalities and false negatives among co-positive scans, trained only with radiology report labels.

entry.title: LLM-Based Agents for Software and Systems Security: Approaches, Applications, and Assessment

author.name: Jingjing Nie, Jiawei Guo, Krishna Meda, Haipeng Cai

entry.summary: A systematic survey of LLM-based agents for software and systems security, covering approaches, applications, and assessment, while noting inconsistent use of the agent term, sharply differing application risk profiles, and incoherent evaluation protocols.

entry.title: More Data Cannot Break a Symmetry: Identifiability by Design

author.name: Jing Xu, Christopher Kanan

entry.summary: Shows that unsupervised representational alignment is bounded by the automorphism group of stimulus geometry before any data, turning this invariance into a design-time diagnostic and demonstrating structurally that dense symmetric sampling cannot be fixed by more data while asymmetric designs recover identifiability.

entry.title: Retrieving Relations, Detecting Fallacies: A RAG Approach to Political Debate Analysis

author.name: Deborah Dore, Greta Damo, Elena Cabrio, Serena Villata

entry.summary: Uses retrieval-augmented generation to detect fallacious arguments in political debates, incorporating world knowledge and argumentative discourse relations dynamically rather than as static classifier features. Targets high-stakes contexts where fallacies shape public opinion.

entry.title: ReToolSQL: Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Robust Text-to-SQL

author.name: Pratik Kakkar, Chandra Dhir, Ravi Shankar, Pareekshit Reddy Gaddam, Anup Shirgaonkar

entry.summary: ReToolSQL combines supervised warm-start on rejection-sampled reasoning traces with agentic reinforcement fine-tuning over multi-turn tool-use trajectories for robust text-to-SQL, arguing the stages act on complementary axes of solution diversity and recovery behavior.

entry.title: See, Hypothesize, Validate: Multimodal Agentic Framework for Discovering Governing PDEs

author.name: Sarang Manoj Pekhale, Amartya Roy, Rajat Sarkar, Souvik Chakraborty

entry.summary: Introduces MAGE, a multimodal agentic framework for discovering governing PDEs organized as a confidence-governed hypothesis validation loop, with four role-specialized agents for observation, visualization, hypothesis, and falsification, mitigating library constraints and hallucination of prior methods.

entry.title: When Evidence Shapes Collaboration: Knowledge-Conditioned Topology Generation for Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Yangxiao Jiang, Jiarun Fan, Mingcong Xu, Yanxi Guo, Jiwen Feng, Shanqing Xu, Mengchen Qian, Wei Chen, Xiaojin Zhang

entry.summary: K-GAT formulates multi-agent collaboration topology design as knowledge-conditioned structure learning, integrating external evidence directly into topology generation rather than as a reactive retrieval tool, addressing structure-knowledge misalignment in knowledge-intensive tasks.

entry.title: Under-Mattress Temporal Sensing for Next-Day Agitation Risk Scoring in Dementia Wards

author.name: Zhen Liu, Marta Bono, Robbe Decloedt, Ajda Flisar, Maarten Van Den Bossche, Maarten De Vos

entry.summary: Analyzes 423 patient-nights of under-mattress physiological sensing in a dementia ward to predict next-day agitation risk, benchmarking four paradigms and showing minute-level temporal structure beats conventional nightly summaries under patient-wise cross-validation.

entry.title: CrabOS: An Operating System for Human-AI Co-inhabitation

author.name: Qi Yang, Yun Ma

entry.summary: CrabOS is an operating system for human-AI co-inhabitation providing shared work state and seamless handoff between humans and long-running AI agents, replacing costly task-specific bridges and manual state transfer.

entry.title: RetailAgent: Structured Adverse Timing in Self-Conditioned Multimodal LLM Trading Agents

author.name: Yupeng Zhang, Liuyuan Jiang, Hongyi Huang, Bingheng Li, Lisha Chen

entry.summary: RetailAgent investigates whether LLM trading agents exhibit predictable directional structure, using an exposure-matched measure to compare returns during long versus flat intervals. It finds persistent negative timing skill across modalities, horizons, and model families, suggesting LLM agents systematically mistime markets.

entry.title: MaCoPlanner: LLM-Assisted Manual-Compiled Task Planning with Proactive Safety Verification for Robotic Industrial Panel Operation

author.name: Guipeng Xin, Jiahe Xua, Mohammad Deghat, Chenhui Wan, Jie Liu, Youmin Hu, Zhongxu Hu

entry.summary: MaCoPlanner is an LLM-assisted planning framework for robotic industrial panel operation that compiles equipment manuals into a typed intermediate representation and symbolically verifies plans against procedural and state constraints before actuation, with localized violation repair.

entry.title: Are These Modules Worth Their Cost? A Paradigm-Level Accuracy-Cost Analysis of In-context Learning Text-to-SQL

author.name: Jiayan Lin, Yujia Liu, Zijin Hong, Zheng Yuan, Yilin Xiao, Hao Chen, Qinggang Zhang, Xiao Huang, Feiran Huang

entry.summary: Presents a paradigm-level accuracy-cost analysis of in-context learning text-to-SQL pipelines, instantiating 17 configurations across five recurring modules to attribute marginal contribution and cost of each design choice rather than reporting only end-to-end accuracy.

entry.title: Exact Risk Ratios for Weighted Data Selection in Linear Regression

author.name: Guangjian Zhang

entry.summary: Resolves a COLT 2025 open problem on weighted data selection in linear regression, proving exact worst-case risk ratios for weighted least squares in several regimes, confirming and extending results on when selective data curation can fail catastrophically.

entry.title: SymboLLM-FE: LLM-Accelerated Symbolic Regression for Automated Feature Engineering on Tabular Data

author.name: Zi-Jian Cheng, Zi-Yi Jia, Zhi Zhou, Yu-Feng Li, Lan-Zhe Guo

entry.summary: SymboLLM-FE combines symbolic regression with LLMs for automated feature engineering on tabular data, aiming to produce interpretable features while avoiding the costly multi-round LLM iterations and hallucination risks of LLM-based AutoFE.

entry.title: Towards Large-Scale Heterogeneous Data Organization for Scientific Foundation Models: A Nuclear Fusion Case Study

author.name: Nathaniel Chen, Kouroche Bouchiat, Peter Steiner, Azarakhsh Jalalvand, SangKyeun Kim, Egemen Kolemen

entry.summary: A nuclear fusion case study characterizing heterogeneous, sparse sensor data (20+ sensor types, five orders of magnitude in sampling rate, mixed tensor structures) for building scientific foundation models, analyzing trade-offs between temporal context and frequency resolution.

entry.title: Entity-Memory Graph Retrieval Improves Evidence Coverage in Long-Conversation Question Answering

author.name: Shumao Sun

entry.summary: The paper proposes Entity-Memory graph retrieval over long conversations, linking verbatim memory nodes through shared entities and chronological edges, with a matched dense control isolating the benefit of graph structure; evidence recall at top-25 improves from 79.7% to 84.5% on LoCoMo.

entry.title: Beyond Global Scalars: Synergizing Token-Level Statistics and Deep Semantics for Adversarial AIGC Text Detection

author.name: Peiming Li, Yifan Wang, Zhiyuan Hu, Shiyu Li, Zheng Wei, Yang Tang

entry.summary: MOSAIC is a 16,000-sample adversarial benchmark spanning a full-granularity attack spectrum for machine-generated text detection, showing vulnerabilities of both perplexity-based global scalars and semantic-state detectors, and proposing token-level statistics fused with deep semantics for robustness.

entry.title: uScenes: A Multimodal RGB and 3D Sonar Dataset for Underwater Robot Perception

author.name: Trung Tien Dong, Zhenqi Wu, Aditya Penumarti, Zi-Hao Zhang, Micaiah Bartlett, Jane Shin, Xiaomin Lin

entry.summary: uScenes is a multimodal dataset pairing synchronized 3D multibeam sonar point clouds with RGB imagery for underwater robot perception, containing 110 scenes and roughly 96,000 synchronized observations. It addresses the elevation ambiguity of 2D forward-looking sonar that blocks 3D scene understanding underwater.

entry.title: Thread-Efficient Decoding for Neural Texture Compression

author.name: Janarbek Matai, Sho Ikeda, Lukasz Lipski, Takahiro Harada

entry.summary: This paper reduces GPU thread divergence in neural texture compression using a shared decoder MLP trained with gradual decoder freezing plus texture clustering, cutting divergence by 25-52 percent. Evaluations on over 500 textures show up to 8.48x speedup on a modern Radeon GPU while preserving rendering quality.

entry.title: Training-Free Temporal Abstraction for General Video Understanding

author.name: Etienne Casanova, Sevan Brodjian, Pietro Perona

entry.summary: STITCH is a training-free method that segments videos into semantically meaningful temporal chunks using a frozen video-text backbone and change detection over embedding sequences, supporting temporal grounding, moment retrieval, and frame selection within one framework.

entry.title: FUSED: Forensic-Semantic Mixture-of-Experts for AI Inpainting Detection and Localization

author.name: Anton Nuzhdin, Marcel Worring, Ivona Najdenkoska

entry.summary: FUSED jointly detects and localizes AI-generated inpainting by combining low-level forensic cues with semantic features in a sparsely-gated Mixture-of-Experts, adapting to generator-specific artifacts and robustness failures exposed by authentic-pixel restoration attacks on detectors.

entry.title: One year in a forest: Analyzing the challenges of autonomous navigation in subarctic environments

author.name: Mat\v{e}j Boxan, Nicolas Lauzon, Veronica Vannini, Mathis Turgeon-Roy, Fran\c{c}ois Pomerleau

entry.summary: This field report analyzes a year-long deployment of a mobile robot in a subarctic boreal forest, evaluating 64 km of data with nine odometry, localization, and mapping methods to characterize how cameras, lidars, and radars fail under canopy cover, snow, and extreme seasonal variation.

entry.title: Memristive-Friendly Hadamard Reservoir Computing: Structured, Multiplier-Free Recurrences at Scale

author.name: Andrea Ceni, Gianluca Milano, Carlo Ricciardi, Claudio Gallicchio

entry.summary: Replaces dense recurrent reservoir matrices with a structured, multiplier-free orthogonal operator built from sign diagonals, permutations, and fast Walsh-Hadamard transforms, achieving O(N) parameters and O(N log N) compute per step in memristive-friendly Echo State Networks.

entry.title: VERA-8B: Evidence-Grounded Audit Risk Reasoning from SEC Filings

author.name: Menghan Liu, Elynn Chen

entry.summary: VERA-8B is an end-to-end audit reasoning system that identifies audit risks from SEC filings before enforcement actions, unifying SFT and GRPO under a single evidence-grounding standard. It is reportedly the first ML work targeting pre-enforcement audit prediction.

entry.title: Time Capsule of Testable Human Knowledge: 41 Years of Jeopardy! in a Single Free Local Model

author.name: David Noever, Forrest McKee

entry.summary: Evaluates a single 9 GB quantized Qwen2.5-14B model over the complete open Jeopardy! dataset of 529,939 clues spanning 41 broadcast seasons, framing it as a portable, low-cost snapshot of queryable human knowledge compared to IBM Watson's 2011 corpus. Demonstrates how far open-weight small models have come in covering broad factual knowledge on consumer-scale hardware.

entry.title: Why Didn't It Check? Unsupported Final Claims and Their Repair in Two Tool-Equipped Language Models

author.name: Justin Bronder

entry.summary: Dissects why tool-equipped LLMs commit to final claims unsupported by gathered evidence, separating occurrence (rate of unsupported claims without ground truth) from conditional repair (rate of fixing them when evidence is supplied) on a fixed Qwen3-32B setup. Finds 33 of 512 responses ended with unsupported established claims despite explicit anti-guessing instructions.

entry.title: SpikeOPD: Stable On-Policy Distillation for Autoregressive Spiking Language Models

author.name: Enqiao Lu, Xingrui Yu, Yiwei Fu, Zhenglin Wan, Pengfei Zhou, Wangbo Zhao, Muqing Jian, Xueyi Zhang, Yang You, Ivor Tsang

entry.summary: SpikeOPD stabilizes on-policy distillation for autoregressive spiking language models, addressing prefix-source mismatch between fixed-corpus ANN-to-SNN distillation and self-generated inference prefixes through output-policy alignment and spiking-dynamics stabilization.

entry.title: SEPO: Evidence-Grounded Prompt Optimization via Structural Editing

author.name: Xiaoyu Ma, Haoyue Liu, Yiwen Li, Jionghao Zhu, Zhichao Wang, Ye Chen, Xiaoying Tang

entry.summary: SEPO is a prompt optimizer built on structural editing of typed prompt units with edit-effect lineage feedback linking each edit to examples it fixes or breaks, replacing opaque whole-prompt rewrites with localizable, machine-readable optimization traces.

entry.title: The Shape of Power: A Multilingual Framework for Social Power Reasoning in Dialogues

author.name: Farah Atif, Sougata Saha, Monojit Choudhury

entry.summary: Introduces a theoretically grounded, multilingual framework for annotating social power in naturalistic dialogue via movie screenplays, with a social-science-informed schema, native-speaker annotation pipeline, and an initial 15,836-instance corpus from French and other-language scenes.

entry.title: Beyond Task-Only Matching: Personalized Skill Routing with Counterfactual Evaluation

author.name: Tianle Wang, Yanghe Zou, Xiang Liu, Ziyao Huang, Chenchen Fu, Weiwei Wu

entry.summary: Formulates personalized skill routing for LLM agents as profile-conditioned retrieval with a counterfactual benchmark where user-profile changes while the task is fixed flip the correct skill, exposing the failure of task-only semantic matching.

entry.title: Propagating construction-time knowledge quality into medical question answering: A framework grounded in clinical guidelines

author.name: Jie Hu, Junjie Wang, Shan Lu, Yifang Hu, Gong Cheng, Yun Liu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a quality-aware framework that propagates construction-time triple quality signals (structural conformance and evidential support) from LLM-built clinical guideline knowledge graphs into downstream QA evidence selection. It addresses a real disconnect between KG construction quality control and inference-time retrieval.

entry.title: Timing-Aware Repurchase Prediction for Web-Scale E-Commerce: Survival Models for Multi-Surface Grocery Recommendation

author.name: Akshay Kekuda, Shreeranjani Srirangamsridharan, Ishan Bhatt, Yanan Cao, Sinduja Subramaniam, Evren Korpeoglu, Kaushiki Nag, Kannan Achan

entry.summary: This industrial-scale study replaces per-horizon binary repurchase classifiers with survival models predicting time-to-repurchase directly, evaluated on millions of grocery e-commerce customers across 30+ ablations. A notable empirical finding is a slightly decreasing marginal hazard, contradicting the intuition that grocery repurchase likelihood grows with time since last purchase.

entry.title: Gen-TAS: A Generative AI-Aided Hardware-Software Task Allocation Framework for FPGA-GPP Heterogeneous Systems

author.name: Mary Kong, Yuqin Zhao, Semih Vazgecen, Cristian Sestito, Themis Prodromakis

entry.summary: Gen-TAS uses a RAG-grounded LLM with task-graph analysis to allocate tasks between FPGA and GPP in heterogeneous embedded systems, generating explainable strategies under latency, power, and resource objectives. Includes human-in-the-loop selection and a deterministic backend.

entry.title: Embedding Models for Stance-Aware Argument Retrieval

author.name: Angelo Sparacino, Francesca Toni, Adam Dejl

entry.summary: Studies stance-aware argument retrieval with dense embedding models, showing existing models exhibit strong topical-overlap bias and struggle with asymmetric support/attack reasoning. Proposes adaptations for dual topic-relevance and stance assessment in retrieval.

entry.title: NL2AGBench: Benchmarking LLM Auto-Formalization for AlphaGeometry

author.name: Samuel Xiao, Judy Song, Rory Hu, Ziliang Zong

entry.summary: NL2AGBench benchmarks LLM auto-formalization of natural-language geometry problems into AlphaGeometry's domain-specific language, addressing the usability bottleneck that manual conversion poses for near-IMO-level neuro-symbolic provers.

entry.title: Temporal Memory-Aware Online Test-Time Adaptation on Dynamic Graphs

author.name: Bo Li, Xin Zheng, Ming Jin, Can Wang, Shirui Pan

entry.summary: DGOTA is a temporal memory-aware online test-time adaptation framework for dynamic GNNs, addressing distribution shift on dynamic graphs where structure and node semantics evolve continuously, a gap left by static-graph TTA work.

entry.title: Spectral Features Dominate BCG Respiratory-Event Detection: A Large-Scale Patient-Independent Comparison of Feature Groups in Sleep Apnea Patients

author.name: Israel Campero Jurado, Zoe Bousraou, Lara Benning, Sara Padilla Neira, Alexander Breuss, Robert Riener, Esther Irene Schwarz, Elisabeth Wilhelm

entry.summary: A large-scale patient-independent comparison of ten BCG feature groups for sleep-apnea respiratory-event detection using a 512-sensor pressure mat with 155 patients, finding spectral features dominate under strict leave-one-subject-out validation.

entry.title: Learning to Transfer Across Modes: Towards Unified Urban Mobility Forecasting

author.name: Yixuan Zhao, Man Luo

entry.summary: TransMod is a unified framework for urban mobility demand forecasting that transfers knowledge across transportation modes (e.g., bus, rail, bike) despite heterogeneous spatial structures and limited data for emerging modes. It addresses a practical gap since most forecasting methods assume compatible source-target spatial structures.

entry.title: QGPINNs: A Physics-Informed Neural Network Framework for Nonlocal Differential Equations on Quantum Graphs

author.name: Vaibhav Mehandiratta, Saket Ramchandra

entry.summary: QGPINNs is a PyTorch physics-informed neural network framework for solving nonlocal differential equations on quantum graphs, embedding continuity, Kirchhoff-Neumann vertex conditions, and boundary conditions into a unified graph-based loss.

entry.title: Optimal Transport for Network Comparison: A Review with Machine Learning Applications

author.name: James Hyun, Fran\c{c}ois G. Meyer

entry.summary: A review of optimal transport distances (Wasserstein, Gromov-Wasserstein, Bures-Wasserstein) for network comparison, covering their theory, transport plan interpretations, and machine learning applications.

entry.title: On the Computational and Statistical Efficiency of the Empirical Maximum Entropy on the Mean Method

author.name: Matthew King-Roskamp, Gabriel Rioux, Rustum Choksi, Tim Hoheisel

entry.summary: This paper establishes an O(n^-1/2) parametric convergence rate for the empirical Maximum Entropy on the Mean method for inverse problems, improving the previously known O(n^-1/4) guarantee, via novel stability analysis of primal-dual optimization under measure perturbations.

entry.title: I-FLOP: Fast Learning of Order and Parents from Interventional Data

author.name: Liuting Chen, Alex Markham

entry.summary: I-FLOP extends the fast FLOP causal discovery algorithm from observational to interventional data using the interventional BIC score with iterative Cholesky-based updates, with consistency guarantees and favorable runtime versus existing algorithms.

entry.title: Real-Time Monitoring of MHD Liquid Metal Flows with Shallow Recurrent Decoders

author.name: Claudio Scardino, Stefano Riva, Carolina Introini, Matteo Lo Verso, Eric Cervi, Antonio Cammi, Laura Savoldi

entry.summary: This work applies shallow recurrent decoders (SHRED) coupled with PCA to map sparse temperature measurements to full thermo-hydraulic states of magnetohydrodynamic liquid metal flows, enabling real-time monitoring of DEMO fusion breeding blanket configurations.

entry.title: Quantum Federated Learning Based on Bures--Uhlmann Geometry for Heterogeneous Noisy Clients

author.name: Haruki Emori, Masaki Uchihara, Yuuki Tokunaga

entry.summary: This paper extends quantum federated learning to heterogeneous noisy clients using full mixed-state Bures-Uhlmann geometry, where the Bures metric captures state sensitivity and the Uhlmann curvature captures parameter incompatibility, moving beyond pure-state and diagonal approximations.

entry.title: Generalized Splines and Gaussian Processes

author.name: Michael Unser

entry.summary: Michael Unser extends the classical equivalence between Gaussian MMSE estimation and regularized least squares to an infinite-dimensional setting, showing that generalized splines correspond to regressors for generalized Gaussian processes on nuclear spaces.

entry.title: Acquire, Repair, Preserve: A Diagnosis-Guided Post-Training Recipe for Small-Model Dialogue Game Agents

author.name: Nan Li

entry.summary: The paper diagnoses failure modes of a 2B dialogue-game agent (repeated guesses, malformed actions, ignored feedback) and proposes a three-stage post-training recipe: supervised acquisition of game participation, repair of mechanically verifiable failures with turn-local preference pairs, and capability preservation.

entry.title: On two proofs of $d^2$ mixing of weighted Dikin walks

author.name: Yuansi Chen, Yunbum Kook

entry.summary: The paper proves a general total-variation mixing bound for weighted Dikin walks under strong self-concordance and related metric regularity, yielding O~(d^2) mixing for polytope sampling and O~(d^4) for truncated PSD cones, unifying prior proofs of d^2 mixing.

entry.title: When Tokenizers Fail: Byte-Level Chunking for Zero-Shot Transfer to Low-Resource Languages

author.name: Sanjeev Kumar, Atsuki Yamaguchi, Nikolaos Aletras

entry.summary: This paper proposes a hierarchical byte-level network that bridges granularity mismatch for word-level tasks in non-Latin scripts, initializing byte embeddings from subword models to enable zero-shot transfer to low-resource languages without massive training data.

entry.title: Informational Antilocality and the Locality Bias in LLMs

author.name: Andrew McInnerney, Shane Storks, Steven Abney, Richard L. Lewis

entry.summary: This paper constructs k-antilocal languages (with no mutual information across any span of k symbols) and shows LLMs achieve comparable cross-entropy loss regardless of antilocality but converge more slowly on more antilocal languages, locating the locality bias in learning speed rather than learnability.

entry.title: Lexically conditioned realization ambiguity in Korean predicate morphology

author.name: Wonjun Oh, KyungTae Lim, Jungyeul Park

entry.summary: The paper develops a framework for localizing global goodness-of-fit discrepancies to individual observations via conditional/marginal contributions across random statistical contexts, connecting resampling diagnostics, data valuation, and event-level anomaly detection.

entry.title: CNeo-Bench: Diagnosing Large Language Models on Chinese Neologisms

author.name: Kaiyan Zhao, Zhongtao Miao, Zheyong Xie, Shaosheng Cao, Yoshimasa Tsuruoka

entry.summary: CNeo-Bench provides 4,759 Chinese neologisms with reference definitions organized by linguistic mechanism, plus a two-tier evaluation separating description from mechanism operation; 18 evaluated LLMs mostly fall below 40% on definition generation.

entry.title: Auditing Generative Audio Calls for Known-Task Audio-LLM Evaluation

author.name: Mengzhe Geng

entry.summary: This work reframes audio-LLM evaluation as a controlled call-decision problem where a policy chooses among transcript labels, encoder evidence (CLAP, AST, WavLM), or calling a generative audio model, isolating the value of acoustic evidence from the need to call a generative model.

entry.title: VidParse: Online Parsing of Egocentric Procedures Like a Pro

author.name: Anubhav Gupta, Archit Kambhamettu, Vatsal Agarwal, Pulkit Kumar, Abhinav Shrivastava

entry.summary: VidParse is a training-free online framework that converts egocentric video streams into temporally ordered action steps by treating activity understanding as graph-constrained inference over a temporal similarity matrix. It avoids the over-segmentation and structural collapse that plague frame-level temporal models under ego-motion and occlusion.

entry.title: CommerceVibe: Learning to Design E-Commerce Creatives as Executable Visual Code via Dual-Feedback Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yajiao Xu, Jin Zhang, Jiangbo Ai, Tao Jiang, Mo Xu, Lina Huang, Chengfu Huo

entry.summary: CommerceVibe represents e-commerce creatives as executable HTML/CSS visual code and formulates generation as conditional program synthesis trained with dual-feedback reinforcement learning. This yields editable, reusable designs with accurate text rendering, addressing raster diffusion limitations for production marketing assets.

entry.title: ZipMVS: Multi-View Stereo with Compressed Cost Volumes

author.name: Guanglin Jin, Hongshan Yu, Javier Civera, Zhaoxin Li

entry.summary: ZipMVS reduces the memory footprint of multi-view stereo by compressing cost volumes via a novel depth-hypothesis strategy, preserving reconstruction accuracy while making deployment feasible for aerospace and autonomous systems. Results on DTU and Tanks and Temples support the claims.

entry.title: UniLipi: A Unified Multi-Script OCR for Historical Indic Manuscripts

author.name: Tathagata Ghosh, Sai Madhusudan Gunda, Simran Singh Sandral, Ravi Kiran Sarvadevabhatla

entry.summary: UniLipi is a unified multi-script OCR model for handwritten Indic manuscripts trained jointly across 13 scripts, handling realistic manuscript conditions such as irregular line geometry, stains, and holes, supporting heritage digitization at scale.

entry.title: Learning the Target Priors Before Image Translation: A Decoupled Training Paradigm for Cross-Modal Image Translation in Remote Sensing

author.name: Keyan Hu, Mingtao Wang, Ziyu Zhou, Tiandong Shi, Haifeng Li, Ji Qi, Chao Tao

entry.summary: This work investigates OCR adaptation for VLMs in extreme data-scarce regimes for low-resource languages, finding that higher layers of specialized models diverge while lower layers share structure across languages. This structural inefficiency suggests cross-language knowledge transfer strategies for scripts lacking large datasets.

entry.title: The thermodynamic freedom of a thermodynamic computer

author.name: Stephen Whitelam

entry.summary: Whitelam analyzes the thermodynamic efficiency of a simulated thermodynamic computer performing an MLP-equivalent classification task using the Wasserstein speed limit, showing different inference protocols operate within 40 percent of the thermodynamic limit and characterizing the freedom in how such devices can run.

entry.title: CAVE-NAV: VLM-Based Autonomous 3D Navigation in Underwater Cave Environments

author.name: Zhenqi Wu, Yuanjie Lu, Yisheng Zhang, Miao Yu, Xuesu Xiao, Jaejeong Shin, Xiaomin Lin

entry.summary: CAVE-NAV leverages a vision-language model with chain-of-thought reasoning to infer navigable directions from environmental cues like light gradients in underwater caves, where visual degradation breaks feature-based localization and communication constraints preclude teleoperation.

entry.title: Physics-Guided Flow Matching for CT Image Reconstruction

author.name: Davide Evangelista

entry.summary: Explores flow matching as a generative prior for low-dose CT reconstruction, training a high-resolution rectified flow model with a two-stage strategy on Mayo Clinic data as a more stable, efficient alternative to diffusion priors.

entry.title: InstructMesh: Selective Refinement of Generative 3D Models for Fabrication

author.name: Faraz Faruqi, Ahmed Katary, Demircan Tas, Theresa Hradilak, Ning Zhang, Jiaji Li, Fabian Manhardt, Martin Nisser, Vrushank Phadnis, Ruofei Du, Federico Tombari, Megan Hofmann, Stefanie Mueller

entry.summary: InstructMesh is an interactive tool for selectively repairing generative 3D models for fabrication, letting users fix geometric flaws (voids, thickness) via natural language or sliders by editing the intermediate latent representation. It addresses the gap between visually plausible generation and manufacturable geometry.

entry.title: Text Restoration of Ancient Documents with Language Models

author.name: Shibingfeng Zhang, Edoardo Caraffa, Annafelicia Zuffrano, Maddalena Modesti, Giovanni Colavizza

entry.summary: Evaluates language models of varying architectures for restoring missing text (lacunae) in damaged ancient manuscripts, with scenario designs and decoding strategies addressing tokenization-lacuna mismatches. Concludes restoration cannot be fully automated but is a useful paleographer aid.

entry.title: Beyond Non-IID: Learner--Client Distribution Mismatch in Federated Learning

author.name: Yiming Xie, Lili Su, Ningfang Mi

entry.summary: Studies learner-client distribution mismatch in federated learning, challenging the assumption that aggregated client data represents the learner's target distribution, and proposes mitigation beyond standard client selection without requiring direct local data access.

entry.title: PhyMamba: Physics-Modulated Mamba for Robust Battery Health Prognostics

author.name: Sara Sameer, Yunyi Zhao, Wei Zhang, Minggang Zeng, Wenqing Li, Man-Fai Ng, Yonggang Wen

entry.summary: PhyMamba is a two-stage physics-modulated Mamba framework for battery health prognostics that integrates electrochemical aging features into sequence modeling of noisy BMS signals without intrusive parameter identification.

entry.title: StreamEMS: Streaming Video Understanding with Self-Evolving Memory Scheme for Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yuxin Liu, Peiqin Zhuang, Yali Wang

entry.summary: StreamEMS improves streaming video understanding for VLMs by restructuring the historical memory itself through a self-evolving memory scheme, complementing prior work that only optimized memory read and write operations. A semantic evolution module produces more informative and robust memory representations.

entry.title: Cyc3D: Evaluating Cyclic Structural Stability and Asset Usability in Image-to-3D Generation

author.name: Liwen Zhang

entry.summary: Cyc3D is a benchmark evaluating image-to-3D generation on cross-view object consistency and asset quality, including a view-cycle structural consistency protocol that repeatedly re-observes a generated asset from novel views to quantify stability beyond rendered-view plausibility.

entry.title: Token-Budget Distillation: Transferring Full-Token Semantics to Compressed Video Vision-Language Models

author.name: Xiaoyang Guo, Guoping Luo, Jusheng Zhang, Keze Wang, Wenhao Wang

entry.summary: Token-Budget Distillation adapts video VLMs under a fixed token budget by freezing the backbone, training LoRA adapters, and using a dual-path teacher-student design where a full-token teacher preserves semantics while the student consumes compressed visual tokens.

entry.title: Cut-ViT: Task-Specific Model Pruning via Gram Anchoring Subspace Consistency

author.name: Jianjian Yin, Liulei Li, Tao Chen, Yi Chen, Yazhou Yao, Wenguan Wang

entry.summary: Cut-ViT performs task-specific pruning of visual foundation models like DINOv3 by constructing Gram anchoring matrices from spatial and semantic perspectives and aligning subspaces between native and pruned models, aiming to preserve robustness and task specialization.

entry.title: WilLaGS: Latent-Conditional 3D Appearance Fields for Robust Gaussian Splatting In-the-Wild

author.name: Yuhao Bai, Qianqiu Tan, Lilong Chen, Huanhuan Lv, Lijun Chen

entry.summary: WilLaGS introduces a latent-conditional appearance model for 3D Gaussian Splatting in the wild, using a beta-VAE to learn a continuous manifold of global appearance that handles illumination variation and transient objects better than discrete embeddings.

entry.title: Prompt-Guided Interactive Segmentation of Interstitial Lung Disease in Thoracic CT

author.name: Vasilis Dedousis, Lubnaa Abdur Rahman, Lorenzo Brigat{\omicron}, Ethan Dack, Andreas Christe, Christoph Frank, Manuela Funke-Chambour, Justus Roos, Adrian Huber, Lukas Ebner, Stavroula Mougiakakou

entry.summary: This paper presents the first adaptation of MedSAM2 for interactive 3D segmentation of interstitial lung disease on thoracic CT, comparing fine-tuning strategies and clinically motivated prompt types for refinement of quantitative disease assessment.

entry.title: Coordinated Motion Planning for Multi-Arm Systems via Iterative LQ Games

author.name: Junyoung Kim, Hanwen Ren, Lei Zhang, Ahmed H. Qureshi

entry.summary: This paper presents an iterative Linear Quadratic game framework for coordinated motion planning of multiple high-DOF manipulators in shared workspaces, where each arm optimizes its own objective while interacting through shared states and collision avoidance constraints.

entry.title: Learning to Allocate Incentives for Incentivized Advertising via Offline Model-Based Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zilin Zhao, Han Yang, Tianpei Yang, Fangsheng Huang, Yanfei Cui, Kan Peng, Yi Li, Yiming Zong, Hao Zhang, Yinsong Xue

entry.summary: Formulates incentive allocation for incentivized advertising as a sequential decision problem with delayed revenue and carryover effects, solving it with offline model-based reinforcement learning in a setting no prior decision-making work covers.

entry.title: RECAST: Recent & Context-Aware Sampling for Test-Time Adaptation in Streaming Biosignals

author.name: Yong-Yeon Jo, Junho Song, Joon-myoung Kwon

entry.summary: RECAST is a lightweight sampling module for buffered test-time adaptation of streaming biosignals, building adaptation batches from recent, context-aligned, and reliable segments to handle subject drift in long-term monitoring.

entry.title: AcrossVAM1.0: Particle World Modeling for Text-Assisted Robot Video Prediction

author.name: Yafei Zhang, Nan Wu

entry.summary: AcrossVAM1.0 factorizes robot video prediction into object-centric motion and dense appearance using a frozen SAM3-DLP codec and a tiny 0.28M-parameter spatio-temporal transformer modulated by OpenCLIP instructions. The particle-based world model addresses the entanglement problems of monolithic pixel models.

entry.title: Real-Time Musculoskeletal Surrogates for Pediatric Cerebral Palsy: a Credibility Pilot

author.name: Mohammad Arif Ul Alam

entry.summary: Develops a subject-conditioned causal neural surrogate for real-time musculoskeletal modeling in pediatric cerebral palsy rehabilitation, with leave-one-subject-out and locked test subject evaluation showing strong musculotendon accuracy and calibrated uncertainty.

entry.title: Leveraging a Foundation Model for the EEG-Based Diagnosis of Alzheimer's Disease

author.name: Maggie Lin, Chung-Lin Hou, Tzyy-Ping Jung

entry.summary: Applies the LaBraM EEG foundation model with random forest classification to Alzheimer's diagnosis, achieving strong subject-independent performance (ROC-AUC 89.4%) in distinguishing dementia patients from controls.

entry.title: Node-wise Feature Encoding for Neural Performance Prediction

author.name: Matthew Grenier, William Hammer, Andrew Heuer, Nikhil Krishna, Yi Wang, Ramtin Zand

entry.summary: FeatureFormer is a neural performance predictor embedding explicit node-wise FLOPs, parameter, and memory encodings in a gated graph attention architecture for latency and energy prediction, with a new large-scale energy dataset (NNEQ) for NAS evaluation.

entry.title: Evidential-Based Higher-Order Set Argumentation Framework

author.name: Shuai Tang

entry.summary: Introduces EHSAF, an evidential-based higher-order set argumentation framework that unifies evidential support, higher-order relations, and collective (set-based) interactions, with two complete labelling semantics including one admitting multiple truth values in support cycles.

entry.title: Resource Constraints and Performance in Agentic AI Systems

author.name: Amaz Salman, Malka Halgamuge, Teo Susnjak

entry.summary: Compares two complete agentic systems (OpenClaw and NanoBot) under matched resource constraints on paired benchmarks, finding no statistically established full-completion advantage (31% vs 25%) and characterizing how tools, memory, and state management shape capability versus operational burden.

entry.title: From Documents to Reasoning: A Validated Synthetic Data Pipeline and Semantic-Aware Fine-Tuning for Financial Numerical Reasoning

author.name: Lokendra Birla, Milind Savagaonkar, Visnu Srinivasan, Sowmya Rasipuram, Shubhashis Sengupta

entry.summary: Provides a validated synthetic data pipeline and semantic-aware fine-tuning for financial numerical QA, plus critique of Exact Match metrics that miss unit and format variations, improving consistency on table/chart/narrative questions.

entry.title: Coverage, Not Credit: Failure-Credit Routing of Zeroth-Order Perturbation Budgets Does Not Improve On-Pool Sample Efficiency for LLM Agents

author.name: Yuxu Ge

entry.summary: Rigorous negative result: failure-credit routing of zeroth-order/evolution-strategies perturbation budgets for tool-using LLM agents shows no statistically detectable on-pool improvement over uniform allocation across three task families, six schemes, and exact sign-flip tests.

entry.title: Generative AI Alignment with Hinduism's Theological Plurality and Sacred Representation

author.name: Dipto Das, Arpita Kundu, Nusrat Jahan Mim, Shion Guha, Syed Ishtiaque Ahmed

entry.summary: Qualitative interview study (15 Bangladeshi Hindu participants) of how users interpret AI-generated religious representations, scriptural explanations, and synthetic devotional media, highlighting that alignment debates over-center secular, Western, Abrahamic assumptions.

entry.title: AGENT-O: A Semantic Agent Card Framework for Interoperable and Governed Healthcare AI Agents

author.name: Pengze Li, Cui Tao

entry.summary: AGENT-O defines a semantic Agent Card ontology (OWL 2/RDF) for describing and governing healthcare AI agents, covering runtime, models, workflow, governance, and provenance. It is evaluated with reasoning tests, SHACL suites, competency queries, and a reporting-completeness assessment of 279 papers.

entry.title: Program Learning with Verifiable Rewards: Symbolic Backpropagation for Post-Training LLMs

author.name: Vishvesh Bhat

entry.summary: PLVR proposes post-training LLMs to place reasoning outside model weights as explicit programs composed of deterministic and neural primitives, learned via symbolic backpropagation with verifiable rewards. The approach targets inspectable, transferable, step-checkable reasoning for tasks with verifiable intermediate steps.

entry.title: Spatial-Semantic Reasoning using Large Language Models for Efficient UAV Search Operations

author.name: Marin Maletic, Marijana Peti, Tamara Petrovic, Stjepan Bogdan

entry.summary: A real-time UAV semantic navigation framework where an LLM interprets natural-language instructions and performs spatial-semantic reasoning to prioritize search regions for object goal navigation, combined with 3D mapping and spline trajectory planning. Operates continuously in real time rather than offline.

entry.title: Optimal Adversarial Testing: Extracting Honest Test Results from Dishonest Test Takers

author.name: Owen Cox, April Xu, Weiyu Xu

entry.summary: Proposes optimal testing strategies that recover reliable metric estimates even when test takers (including AI-assisted cheaters) behave adversarially, by optimally re-testing selected groups under different conditions. Timely given AI-driven cheating.

entry.title: Anatomy-Aware Promptable Segmentation with Online Interactive Training for AUTOPET V

author.name: Pablo Lozano-Jimenez, Sergio Romero-Tapiador, Ruben Tolosana

entry.summary: An anatomy-aware promptable segmentation model for whole-body lesion segmentation in FDG and PSMA PET/CT built on nnU-Net, with two-stage training including online interactive refinement via scribble prompts and shared lesion-organ heads to reduce physiological-uptake false positives.

entry.title: Biologically Inspired Mechanisms for Facilitating Grokking in Multilayer Perceptrons

author.name: Florin Leon

entry.summary: Augments MLPs with biologically inspired mechanisms (input gating, structural plasticity, gain and threshold modulation, homeostasis, lateral inhibition, decorrelation) and shows via ablations that these actively promote grokking on sparse parity and noisy XOR benchmarks.

entry.title: Multiscale Community-Based Fingerprinting of Signed Functional Networks

author.name: Sema Athamnah, Selin Aviyente

entry.summary: This work proposes multiscale community-based fingerprinting of signed functional brain networks, using signed multilayer community detection that incorporates both correlated and anti-correlated activity to identify individuals across sessions more robustly than edge-level features.

entry.title: Quantum SEDONet: Spectrally-Embedded Quantum Deep Operator Networks for Partial Differential Equations

author.name: Muhammad Abid, Arth Sojitra, Bipin Tiwari, Omer San

entry.summary: Quantum SEDONet improves Quantum DeepONet by assigning spectral bases (Fourier for periodic, Chebyshev for bounded coordinates) per trunk coordinate according to boundary conditions, enhancing the representation of oscillatory features for PDE operator learning on quantum hardware.

entry.title: Personalized and Multi-View Representation for Federated Cold-Start Recommendation

author.name: Jaehyung Lim, Wonbin Kweon, Woojoo Kim, Junyoung Kim, Dongha Kim, Hwanjo Yu

entry.summary: The paper proposes a personalized multi-view representation method for federated cold-start recommendation, addressing the dual constraint that servers cannot see client interactions and clients cannot see proprietary item attributes, and fixing personalization, compositionality, and communication-efficiency limitations of prior approaches.

entry.title: Anchored Scenario Coverage for Failure-Aware First-Hit Batch Inverse Design

author.name: Chuhan Yang, Chenxi Wang, Linhan Wu, Yuyang Liu

entry.summary: ARC-SC is a batch acquisition method for failure-prone closed-loop inverse design that anchors strong marginal candidates and allocates remaining batch slots to maximize complementary scenario coverage under risk constraints, demonstrated on superconductivity and related design tasks.

entry.title: Load-Bearing Context: The Question Damage Score for Evaluating Context Reliance in Linguistic Reasoning

author.name: Neh Majmudar, Elena Filatova

entry.summary: The paper introduces the Question Damage Score, a diagnostic framework using deletion of individual context examples (random and targeted, inspired by error-correcting codes) in linguistics olympiad puzzles to measure how much LLM answers depend on specific context versus prior knowledge.

entry.title: Representation of syntax in LLMs through the lens of linear distance and similarity-aware entropy

author.name: Juan Pablo Vigneaux, Mary Kennedy, Khalil Iskarous, Robert Frank, Matilde Marcolli

entry.summary: The paper disaggregates structural probe evaluation by syntactic relation label (UASL) and identifies two predictive factors for probe accuracy variability: log-scale linear distance statistics and similarity-aware entropy between representations.

entry.title: PersonaEdit: Representative Sample Selection for Personalized Model Editing

author.name: You-Mei Huang, Chung-Chi Chen, An-Zi Yen

entry.summary: PersonaEdit adapts model editing to personalization by selecting representative samples via hidden-representation clustering, avoiding the cost and interference of editing large volumes of per-user data.

entry.title: A Unified Framework to Elicit Structured Feedback for Interpretable Multi-Trait Essay Scoring

author.name: Shihang Yang, Sanwoo Lee, Ningning Zhao, Yunfang Wu

entry.summary: HiFTS is a unified autoregressive framework for multi-trait automated essay scoring that generates hierarchical rubric-grounded CoT feedback before predicting trait-level and holistic scores, trained with distilled feedback and GRPO with a composite reward balancing agreement, calibration, and feedback quality.

entry.title: Is Prosody Lost in Translation? Fine-Grained Cross-Lingual Prosody Similarity Across Languages

author.name: Haopeng Xie, Ismail Rasim Ulgen, Sofia Son, Berrak Sisman, Philipp Koehn

entry.summary: The paper presents the first fine-grained cross-lingual analysis of prosody in speech-to-speech translation using multilingual dubbing data, analyzing pitch, energy, and temporal feature similarity across English-German, English-Spanish, and English-French pairs to inform expressive S2ST.

entry.title: DisCTI: Who Needs to Know Timely? Automated Sector-Aware Cyber Threat Intelligence Dissemination

author.name: Fajar Wijitrisnanto (National Cyber and Crypto Agency, Jakarta, Indonesia), Alsharif Abuadbba (CSIRO, Sydney, Australia), Yansong Gao (CSIRO, Sydney, Australia, The University of Western Australia, Perth, Australia), Nan Wu (CSIRO, Sydney, Australia)

entry.summary: DisCTI automates sector-aware dissemination of cyber threat intelligence, addressing the fact that 98% of MISP events remain uncategorized, so that shared intelligence reaches the right sectors in time for mitigation.

entry.title: Synth-JDoc: Synthesizing a Japanese Document Image Dataset for OCR with Diverse Layouts and Embedded Images

author.name: Keito Sasagawa, Shuhei Kurita, Daisuke Kawahara

entry.summary: Synth-JDoc introduces a synthetic Japanese document image dataset for OCR training that handles vertically and horizontally written text plus embedded images, generated by rendering text onto realistic layouts. It targets the documented weakness of LVLMs on vertical Japanese text, where high-quality OCR data is scarce and manual annotation is costly.

entry.title: ShiftSplit-AD: Separating Domain Shift from Defects in Foundation-Feature Visual Anomaly Detection

author.name: Muhamathu Ameer Ali Aacaas Muhamath

entry.summary: BEACON constructs cross-source knowledge graphs for cyber threat intelligence by anchoring entity resolution on MITRE ATT&CK attack behaviors, solving the problem of the same threat appearing under different names across reports. This enables integrating information that single-report extraction methods cannot connect.

entry.title: DensityKV: Density-Guided KV Cache Compression for Long Video Generation

author.name: Wenqu Zhao, Xuemin Chi, Xin Zhang, Guoqing Ma, Baorun Li, Jianjie Fang, Peizhi Tang, Chen Gao, Wei Wu

entry.summary: ShiftSplit-AD examines whether decomposing nearest-normal DINOv2 residuals into low-rank and row-sparse components can separate benign domain shift from true visual defects in anomaly detection. The honest headline finding is a trade-off rather than a clean separation, since real defects can themselves be low-rank.

entry.title: A-PAIR: A Benchmark and Identity-Consistent Grounding Framework for Air-Ground Cross-View Referring Person Detection

author.name: Zhoupeng Guo, Xinjie Yao, Yunqi Zhu, Zhihe Fan, Siqi Zhao, Jianjun Chen, Yichen Dong, Yan Fan, Pengfei Zhu

entry.summary: A-PAIR introduces the first benchmark for air-ground cross-view referring person detection, requiring language commands to ground the same physical identity across aerial and ground views despite weak aerial cues and similar distractors, plus an identity-consistent grounding framework.

entry.title: 3D-USE: From Image-Level to Scene-Level Underwater Enhancement

author.name: Jieyu Yuan, Yuanlin Zhang, Jihong Li, Chunle Guo, Huimin Lu, Chongyi Li

entry.summary: 3D-USE formulates underwater scene-level enhancement as learning a persistent, visibility-enhanced 3D scene representation from degraded multi-view observations, using a medium-aware Gaussian representation and consistent enhancement targets without paired enhanced 3D data.

entry.title: A Controlled Audit of Architectural Complexity in Uncertainty-Aware Multi-Organ Ultrasound Classification

author.name: Yang Song, Pengbo Sun, Shichang Feng, Ye Zhu, Xin Xu, Ziran Wang

entry.summary: This paper conducts a controlled audit of architectural complexity in uncertainty-aware multi-organ ultrasound classification, comparing six candidates across matched seeds, frozen partitions, and paired decision rules to test whether added components like MoE routing and evidential objectives actually help deployment decisions.

entry.title: Task-State Adaptation with Prototype Memory for Multi-Task Dense Prediction

author.name: Yangyang Xu, Haobo Yuan, Yuzhu Wang, Duo Su, Xi Ye, Yibo Yang, Jun Zhu

entry.summary: MemMTL is a multi-task dense prediction framework that estimates a compact task state from global context and refines it via a learnable prototype memory, producing task-conditioned expert logits combined with token-level logits under sparse top-k selection over a shared expert bank.

entry.title: Manifold4D: Denoising on Point Cloud Rendered Manifolds for Video Re-shooting

author.name: Yongqi Mao, Zijia Dai, Zhishuo Liu, Wei Xu, Kaiwei Wang, Guotao Meng

entry.summary: Manifold4D addresses video re-shooting by denoising on point-cloud rendered manifolds, arguing that pixel-aligned renders need not be supplied as an explicit conditioning stream, which resolves the trust dilemma between render and source video in diffusion-based camera-controllable video editing.

entry.title: RASA: Disentangled Spatial-Motional Priors for Cross-Identity Character Animation

author.name: Zhen Xiao, Zhen Shen, Zhaofan Qiu, Ting Yao, Xueliang Liu, Tao Mei

entry.summary: RASA disentangles cross-identity spatial mapping from motion control in character animation via structured priors injected into a Diffusion Transformer, using a spatial prior calibrator followed by motion refinement for reference-driven animation.

entry.title: Non-Uniform Quantisation for 3DGS Compression

author.name: Bert Van hauwermeiren, Patrice Rondao Alface, Adrian Munteanu

entry.summary: This paper proposes importance-weighted non-uniform quantisation with redundancy-eliminating merging for compressing 3D Gaussian Splatting models, achieving state-of-the-art compression on benchmarks and supporting interoperability for standardized 3DGS formats.

entry.title: Conditional Visual Evidence Utility: State-Dependent Rank Reversals in Frozen Vision-Language Encoders

author.name: Yunxuan Fang, Xinhe Wang

entry.summary: This analysis paper shows that frozen OpenCLIP and SigLIP encoders exhibit state-dependent rank reversals in the conditional utility of visual evidence during compositional visual search, with the effect robust across evidence constructions and query paraphrases but vanishing under derangement controls.

entry.title: DeicticVLA: Unifying Instruction Modes Based on Language and Deictic Gestures in a Single VLA

author.name: Kango Yanagida, Tatsuya Aoki, Yuichiro Yoshikawa, Takato Horii

entry.summary: DeicticVLA unifies language, vision-language, and visual instruction modes for robot manipulation in a single pretrained VLA by canonicalizing them into text prompts and deictic gesture masks, enabling pointing-based disambiguation among similar objects without mode-specific models.

entry.title: CASTANET: Causality-Aware Spatio-Temporal Adversarial Network Using Traffic Incident Effects

author.name: Toshiya Kitahara, Ryu Shirakami, Koh Takeuchi, Hisashi Kashima

entry.summary: CASTANET integrates spatio-temporal GNNs with causality-aware adversarial modeling of incident effects to predict non-periodic traffic congestion from sparse, spatially biased incident records.

entry.title: Cross-Spectral Dense Correspondence for Multimodal Spectral Medical Imaging

author.name: Eric L. Wisotzky, Jost Triller, Simon W. H\"artl, Oliver T. Bruns, Peter Eisert, Anna Hilsmann

entry.summary: Addresses dense correspondence across non-overlapping spectral ranges in multimodal medical imaging via a sensor-agnostic cross-spectral modulation protocol and a synthetic benchmark, enabling supervision where ground truth is scarce.

entry.title: SegBench-GC: Testing Segmentation Invariance in Multi-Step Offline Goal-Conditioned Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Musa Shams

entry.summary: Introduces SegBench-GC, a controlled stress test of segmentation invariance in offline goal-conditioned RL, holding everything fixed while varying artificial backup boundaries and continuation-valid targets, showing segmentation artifacts affect multi-step GCRL.

entry.title: Automated Analysis Framework for Multilingual Climate-Health Literature Based on Multi-Agent Large Language Model

author.name: Yuze Sun, Shihui Zhang, Jiancheng Pan, Yunjia Ye, Wentao Luo, Jiahao Li, Quan Zhang, Wenjia Cai, Xiaomeng Huang

entry.summary: A multi-agent LLM framework automating multilingual climate-health literature analysis end to end: screening, structured extraction, and standardized integration via a central coordinator and three specialized agents.

entry.title: DART-FL: Burst-Aware Multitask Federated Learning under Dynamic Inference Demand at the Edge

author.name: Yiming Xie, Pinrui Yu, Geng Yuan, Xue Lin, Ningfang Mi

entry.summary: DART-FL is an SLO-aware multitask federated learning framework for edge devices that jointly adapts the inference-training resource split and task-level training emphasis under dynamic, bursty inference demand.

entry.title: TI$^2$PS: A Topology-Informed Inverse Design Framework for Stochastic Multicellular Pattern Formation

author.name: Kenji Komiya, Andrew Kailiang Jin, Ryo Nishikimi, Kunio Kashino

entry.summary: TI2PS is a topology-informed inverse design framework estimating agent-based model parameters for target multicellular pattern formation, combining Betti vectors from topological data analysis with inverse surrogate modeling.

entry.title: Efficient Online Continual Foundation Model Fine-Tuning for Predictive Process Monitoring

author.name: Sjoerd van Straten, Marwan Hassani

entry.summary: COMPASS is the first framework for online continual fine-tuning of foundation models for predictive process monitoring, using loss-plateau drift detection to identify task boundaries and adaptive subspace updates to handle concept drift.

entry.title: Picking Bins Empty: A Hierarchical Hybrid Approach with Online Self-Learning of Grasp Points for Reliable Industrial Bin-Picking

author.name: Florian T\"oper, Samarth Kishor Yelvande, Jan Niklas Ewertz, Rudolph Triebel, Peter Ohlhausen

entry.summary: The paper presents a four-tiered hierarchical hybrid system for industrial bin-picking that combines model-based precision with model-free grasp flexibility, including online self-learning of grasp points to avoid deadlocks and achieve complete bin clearance. It targets a real manufacturing pain point where neither approach alone achieves reliability plus versatility. The engineering contribution is significant for production deployment.

entry.title: Not All Explanations Are Sought: Information-Seeking Psychology for Human-Centered XAI

author.name: Andrea Beretta, Salvatore Rinzivillo

entry.summary: A position paper arguing that human-centered explainable AI should incorporate the psychology of information seeking, modeling whether users engage with explanations via instrumental, hedonic, and cognitive expected utilities shaped by cognitive biases. Identifies failure modes of both excessive and insufficient information-seeking.

entry.title: An Empirical Evaluation of Cross-City POI Recommendation on a Large-Scale Benchmark

author.name: Peibo Li, Yang Song, Hao Xue, Maarten de Rijke, Flora D. Salim

entry.summary: Re-evaluates cross-city POI recommendation on the large-scale Trip World benchmark, finding that hometown-aware models rely more on destination priors than user preference transfer, and that the accuracy-efficiency tradeoff degrades at scale where the simplest model remains competitive.

entry.title: GOD: Govern, Observe, and Direct - A Real-Time Control Room for Agent Societies

author.name: Yige Luo, Ran Guan

entry.summary: GOD is a local-first control room for generative-agent societies combining setup, spatial replay, targeted questions, and live interventions through a command-and-artifact loop, making runs inspectable and portable for operators and researchers.

entry.title: Expert Knowledge & Machine Understanding: Bridging Reactome's Ontology with LLM Semantic Embeddings

author.name: Susanna Bravi, Riccardo De Luca, Rosa Sicilia, Christine Nardini, Mario Santoro

entry.summary: Tests whether LLM semantic embeddings of Reactome's expert-written pathway descriptions recover the manually curated global hierarchical structure, probing whether textual metadata mirrors higher-order biological relationships.

entry.title: Regime-Aware Portfolio Management via Retrieval-Augmented LLM-Guided Expert Switching

author.name: Ahmad Asadi, Reza Safabakhsh

entry.summary: Retrieval-augmented LLM-guided expert switching for portfolio management under regime changes, using a dual-stream VAE and a retrieval base of historical expert performance, with an LLM reasoning over evidence rather than directly generating actions, plus a monotonicity property.

entry.title: Learning to Use Tools: Reinforcement Learning for Tool-Integrated Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Minghui Xu, Zi Wang

entry.summary: The paper studies calculator tool calling for mathematical reasoning on the Countdown task, analyzing reasoning failures and building SFT datasets for tool-use patterns before applying on-policy RL methods including RLOO, GRPO, and DAPO with verifiable rewards. It also introduces more reliable evaluation of tool-integrated reasoning.

entry.title: Training-free Suction Grasp Detection for Deformed Aseptic Cartons Using Vision-Language Models and Geometric Surface Scoring

author.name: Marin Maletic, Goran Vasiljevic

entry.summary: A training-free robotic system for sorting deformed aseptic cartons combining an open-vocabulary VLM for detection, SAM2 for masking, and geometric surface scoring for suction-point selection. Validated on a real robot across deformation levels and cluttered scenes.

entry.title: Unsupervised Continual Learning with Growing Self-Organizing Maps and Synthetic Replay

author.name: Pujan Thapa, Alexander Ororbia, Travis Desell

entry.summary: Presents an unsupervised continual learning framework using growing self-organizing maps with distributional statistics for exemplar-free synthetic replay, eliminating raw data storage without requiring task boundaries or labels.

entry.title: Conditional Diffusion Models for Energy-Efficient Driving

author.name: Hemanth Neelgund Ramesh, Andr\'e Snoeck, Chyi-Fu Hong, Shijing Sun

entry.summary: A conditional diffusion framework generating EV battery-current profiles conditioned on route features (velocity, temperature) for energy-aware delivery fleet routing, providing distributional trajectories rather than point estimates for operational decisions.

entry.title: D-TAIA: Domain-Aware LLM Adaptation for Multi-Task Predictive Process Monitoring

author.name: Sjoerd van Straten, Christine Jacob, Marwan Hassani

entry.summary: D-TAIA adapts LLMs for multi-task predictive process monitoring under data scarcity, high process entropy, and distribution shift, using domain-aware training and inference-time adaptation rather than direct regression heads.

entry.title: Advancing Interaction-Sensitive Feature Selection: Novel Relief-Based Algorithms, Expanded Comparisons, and Recommendations for Biomedical Data Mining

author.name: Kia Kazemi-Nia, Harsh Bandhey, Philip J. Freda, Ryan J. Urbanowicz

entry.summary: This work refactors and expands the scikit-rebate package of Relief-based feature selection algorithms and benchmarks them rigorously on genomic simulation data, offering recommendations for biomedical data mining where feature interactions matter.

entry.title: Physics-informed learning for the inverse problem in resonant ultrasound spectroscopy

author.name: Alejandro Cubillos Mu\~noz, Manuela Rivas, Julian Rincon

entry.summary: The paper formulates the inverse problem in resonant ultrasound spectroscopy as a constrained inverse-isospectral problem and builds a physics-informed learning pipeline that regresses on reduced spectral and geometric features before reconstructing elastic constants.

entry.title: A Shaky Voice Is Not Always a Dodge: Benchmarking Textual and Vocal Evasion Detection in Earnings Calls

author.name: Mirae Kim, Seonghun Jeong, Youngjun Kwak

entry.summary: DualEvasion is a benchmark of 505 annotated earnings-call QA pairs with independent textual evasion and vocal confidence labels, showing that vocal cues carry complementary evasion signal beyond transcripts and that state-of-the-art multimodal models still struggle.

entry.title: Phoneme- and Word-Level Metrics Using Self-Supervised Speech Representations for Forced Alignment Evaluation

author.name: V. S. D. S. Mahesh Akavarapu, Michael Daniel, Gerhard J\"ager

entry.summary: The paper introduces two reference-free corpus-level metrics (PCMI and WACS) based on self-supervised speech representations for evaluating forced alignment without manual timestamp annotations, validated under random and systematic perturbations.

entry.title: GAAT: Geometry-Aware Alignment Transformer for Multimodal UAV Perception

author.name: Jingpu Yang, Debin Tang, Yilin Sun, Fengxian Ji, Jiahua Zhu, Wenrui Ding, Yufeng Wang

entry.summary: GAAT is a geometry-aware alignment transformer for UAV multimodal perception that estimates local correspondence reliability before cross-modal interaction across RGB, infrared, SAR, and depth, handling parallax, platform motion, and lens distortion that break token alignment.

entry.title: Ex-Sim(3)-Reg: 2D-3D Correspondence Pruning via Extended Sim(3) Registration

author.name: Pei An, Muyao Peng, Junfeng Ding, Jiaqi Yang, Liangliang Nan

entry.summary: Ex-Sim(3)-Reg recasts 2D-3D correspondence pruning as an extended Sim(3) registration problem that explicitly models noisy monocular depth priors, improving robustness on unseen, low-inlier, and distorted cases.

entry.title: Dual-Stream Semantic Guidance with Prototype Anchor Calibration for Source-Fully-Free Adaptation of Vision-Language Models

author.name: Weiwei Xiang, Shun Peng, Guangyi Xiao, Hao Chen, Lei Yang

entry.summary: DSSG tackles source-fully-free domain adaptation of VLMs by identifying a dual semantic drift problem, fixed class embeddings plus drifting generated captions, and resolving it with a dual-stream module balancing caption-based plasticity against global stability.

entry.title: GeoFF3D: Coordinate-Anchored Feed-Forward Reconstruction for Large-Scale UAV Mapping

author.name: Xiang Yang, Yongli Wang, Yunsheng Zhang

entry.summary: GeoFF3D combines a coordinate-anchored feed-forward reconstruction model predicting gravity-aligned metric poses and point maps with a spatial chunked aggregation framework, targeting large-scale UAV mapping where Sim(3) alignment becomes unstable on near-collinear trajectories.

entry.title: Abstract4D: A Large-Scale Dataset and Framework for Understanding the Visual Language of Abstract Art

author.name: Haowei Zhang, Yuanpei Zhao, Ji-Zhe Zhou, Mao Li

entry.summary: Abstract4D is the largest dataset of abstract paintings to date, over 120,000 images with multi-dimensional perceptual annotations produced by a hybrid human-VLM pipeline, used to analyze the semantic structure of abstract art and support downstream modeling of its visual language.

entry.title: Denoising-Aware Temporal Point Cloud Completion for 3D Crop Architecture Recovery and Phenotypic Trait Extraction

author.name: Mrudul Mittal, Soumyashree Kar

entry.summary: This paper introduces SynthCrop4D, a procedurally generated synthetic dataset of temporally evolving plant point clouds with controllable noise and complete geometry, plus a two-stage denoising and temporal completion pipeline for crop architecture recovery and phenotyping.

entry.title: Lossy Event Compression: From Event Stream Distortion to Task Performance

author.name: Zahra Rezaee, Catarina Brites, Jo\~ao Ascenso

entry.summary: This work introduces two lossy event-camera compression pipelines, one histogram-based and one stream-based, and studies how event stream distortion metrics relate to task-level performance, addressing the gap that existing metrics poorly predict downstream degradation.

entry.title: GeBDA: Building Damage Assessment as Text-Based Sequence Prediction

author.name: Olivier Dietrich, Krishna Sapkota, Konrad Schindler, Genady Beryozkin

entry.summary: GeBDA casts building damage assessment from bi-temporal satellite imagery as autoregressive text-based sequence prediction of variable-length bounding box sets with damage labels, using an open Gemma model and a suitable prompt without dedicated architectures.

entry.title: SignRR: Retrieve and Refine Real Motion for Sign Language Production

author.name: Fidel Omar Tito Cruz, Angie Sanchez Marquina, Summy Farfan, Gissella Bejarano

entry.summary: SignRR combines retrieval of real sign language motion segments with learned refinement to fix rhythm and style inconsistencies when concatenating across signers, aiming to preserve rare hand configurations in sign language production.

entry.title: Ada-TokenCom: Rate-Adaptive Token Communications via Large-Model-Driven Token Compression and Generation

author.name: Zijun Zhang, Li Qiao, Mahdi Boloursaz Mashhadi, Zhen Gao, Mehdi Bennis, Kaibin Huang

entry.summary: Ada-TokenCom develops rate-adaptive token communications where an autoregressive large model transmits only highly informative leading tokens and the receiver predicts the rest, integrating next-token prediction with arithmetic coding for ultra-low bitrate semantic transmission.

entry.title: Generalized Context in Cross Attention for Transfer Learning of Disjoint Tabular Data

author.name: Kazi F. Akhter, Ibna Kowsar, Manar D. Samad

entry.summary: Introduces generalized context learning for transfer between tabular domains with disjoint features, using transformer projection weight interactions (source key with target query) to provide rule-based generalization without shared features.

entry.title: CareGraph: An Auditable Hybrid AI Framework for Evidence-Grounded Personalized Longitudinal Health Intelligence

author.name: Pratik Ghawate, Tanvi Patil

entry.summary: Presents CareGraph, an auditable hybrid AI framework that converts heterogeneous clinical, self-reported, and wearable records into prioritized trends, provenance-linked explanations, and bounded next steps without making autonomous clinical decisions. Includes deterministic analysis, graph construction, constrained LLM synthesis, and release gating, tested on synthetic 400-patient cohorts.

entry.title: Agents for Everyone: A Workshop Framework for Building Agentic AI Capabilities in a Distributed Curation Community

author.name: Seth Carbon, Sierra Moxon, Kimberly Van Auken, Pascale Gaudet, Christopher J. Mungall

entry.summary: Describes a cloud-based JupyterHub agentic environment using Claude Code as a universal harness, plus an interactive workshop, to bring agentic AI curation to the Gene Ontology Consortium's distributed community. Focuses on access, training, and centralized deployment for domain curators.

entry.title: COVER: Identifiable Evaluation of Coalition Routing

author.name: Raghul Sugumar, Amrit Gopinath

entry.summary: COVER introduces an evaluation contract for multi-agent coalition routing that fixes an information boundary and legal team family before outcomes are generated, enabling identifiable estimation of oracle regret and policy contrasts. It validates the instrument with controlled tables on MuSiQue-12.

entry.title: SafeStep: An Interactive Demonstration of Semantic Communication for Pedestrian Safety Monitoring

author.name: Christian McDowell, Andrea Panebianco, Jeremiah Yang, Sirin Chakraborty, Samuel Chamoun, Travis Ross, Yin Sun
