entry.summary: Measures invocation-level reliability of tool-using agents, separating wrong-tool from wrong-argument failures, and finds roughly 70 percent of clean-context capability lost by depth 6 due to self-induced context corruption. It also proves that exact-match scoring against gold trajectories makes propagation parameters artifacts of the scoring rule. A careful measurement-methodology critique with practical implications.

entry.title: AgentFold: Closed-Loop Agentic Search for Protein Folding Model Design

author.name: Mingquan Liu, Jiangyu Chen, Hanqun Cao, Xujun Zhang, Pengsen Ma, Xiangru Tang, Shuting Jin, Zhuo Yang, Tianfan Fu, Fang Wu, Xiangxiang Zeng

entry.summary: AgentFold treats protein folding model development as a closed-loop search over executable code variants, with a multi-agent system starting from ESMFold that proposes hypotheses, implements and debugs code modifications, and evaluates variants with multi-objective, domain-aware analysis. Tests whether scientific LLM agents can autonomously improve large coupled ML systems. Strong AI-for-science contribution.

entry.title: Rethinking Message Passing as Retrieval for Text-Attributed Graph Learning

author.name: Jintang Li, Yuhong Chen, Ruofan Wu, Binli Luo, Jiayi Ji, Hui Li, Rongrong Ji

entry.summary: This paper reframes GNN message passing as retrieval, showing each layer can be viewed as an MLP applied to a node representation plus a permutation-invariant summary of retrieved graph context. It proposes RTA, an MLP-based framework replacing structural message passing with label-aware retrieval, backed by theoretical analysis of why neighborhood aggregation outperforms plain MLPs.

entry.title: FaulT-Bench: Towards Benchmarking Network Troubleshooting LLM Agents under Unreliable User Tickets

author.name: Kuan-Hao Tseng, Niruth Bogahawatta, Yasod Ginige, Kunjan Patel, Kosta Dakic, Suranga Seneviratne

entry.summary: FaulT-Bench benchmarks LLM agents for network troubleshooting under unreliable user tickets, spanning genuine faults, false reports, and incorrect root-cause claims across eight topologies. It shows how ticket wording and reporter personas affect diagnosis quality, a factor prior benchmarks ignore.

entry.title: Mitigating Strong-Modality Collapse in Multimodal Learning via Inverted Asymmetric Fusion

author.name: Mary Ogbuka Kenneth, Foaad Khosmood, Abbas Edalat

entry.summary: Identifies strong-modality collapse, where fusing modalities degrades the dominant one (text accuracy drops 74.9% to 56.4% in their setting), explaining why some multimodal models underperform unimodal baselines. Proposes Inverted Asymmetric Fusion, which passes the dominant modality through unchanged. Includes an ablation-backed diagnosis.

entry.title: Generative Monte Carlo Sampling for Constant-Cost Particle Transport

author.name: Joseph A. Farmer, Aidan Murray, Johannes Krotz, Ryan G. McClarren

entry.summary: Generative Monte Carlo integrates generative AI into particle transport simulation by reformulating cell transmission as conditional generation, using conditional flow matching to sample particle exit states without simulating scattering histories, with optical coordinate scaling for material generalization. Validated on reactor-lattice and hohlraum benchmarks.

entry.title: DeflectBench: A Benchmark for Evaluating Rhetorical Fallacy Generation in LLMs

author.name: Art Kanke

entry.summary: DeflectBench evaluates whether LLMs can be prompted to generate rhetorical fallacies (whataboutism, ad hominem, red herring) on demand, analyzing 23,990 generations from four frontier models. A key finding is that refusal is governed by request structure rather than claim content, with single prompt-frame changes swinging refusal nearly 100 percentage points.

entry.title: TwinKV: A Composable Repair Pass for KV Cache Eviction via Pairwise Key Redundancy

author.name: Hong Chen, Yudong Zeng, Yongwei Huang, Zuhao Ouyang, Junyan Zhang, Xuming Hu

entry.summary: TwinKV finds attention magnitude is essentially uncorrelated with a token's causal contribution (Spearman rho about -0.004), challenging the premise of dominant KV-cache eviction methods, and proposes an attention-free near-duplicate key redundancy signal as a composable repair pass on existing policies. It is training-free and targets long-context inference under memory budgets.

entry.title: TemporalFlow-VLA: Learning Physically Grounded Execution History for Long-Horizon Robot Manipulation

author.name: Jiarui Yang, Yehao Lu, Yuning Su, Yu Zhong, Yufeng Xie, Yazhou Zhang, Haiyu Lan, Kaixiang Lu, Peiwen Lin, Chuang Wang, Junwei Liang, Enyu Li

entry.summary: This work presents an online learning framework enabling a bimanual robot to learn juggling on physical hardware within minutes despite large sim2real gaps, using regularized memory-based learning that combines a learned local model with a retained global prior model for extrapolation where experience is sparse.

entry.title: LAAF: A Layered Accountability Architecture Framework for LLM Applications

author.name: Prachi Chaturvedi, Shahnawaz Ahmad, Ehsan Nowroozi, Muhammad Waqas, George Loukas, Alireza Jolfaei, Lucas Cordeiro, Pierre Dantas

entry.summary: A PRISMA-guided systematic review of 122 primary studies plus 12 regulatory documents on accountability for LLM applications in high-stakes settings like hospitals and courts. It formalizes accountability as an actor-forum relation across five dimensions and synthesizes concrete mechanisms for tracing and acting on responsibility.

entry.title: Inductive Correlation Clustering with Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Francesco Paolo Nerini, Francesco Bonchi, Arijit Khan, Andr\'e Panisson

entry.summary: Leverages GNNs to solve inductive correlation clustering, a generalization that transfers clustering across instances without re-executing combinatorial optimization per input, addressing scalability and transductivity limits of prior CC algorithms. Bridges combinatorial optimization and graph learning.

entry.title: MM-Spectrum: Multimodal Multi-spectral Molecular Structural Elucidation with a Stable MoE Framework

author.name: Hai-tao Yu, Nan Min, Zheng Fang, Hongyu Zhan, Yusen Tan, Yuhan Wang, Jun Xia

entry.summary: MM-Spectrum is a sparse Mixture-of-Experts framework for inferring molecular structures from multimodal multi-spectral data, with modality-aware routing that exposes spectral identity to the router to combat multimodal imbalance seen in naive sequence concatenation. Targets chemistry structure elucidation.

entry.title: AdaThinking-E: One-Token Entropy Regulation for Adaptive Thinking

author.name: Zining Wang, Tongkun Guan, Boming Chen, Zhentao Guo, Jianqiang Liu, Chao Jin, Chen Duan, Kai Zhou, Pengfei Yan, Wei Shen, Xiaokang Yang

entry.summary: AdaThinking-E is an RL framework for multimodal LLMs that learns adaptive thinking via one-token entropy regulation, engaging deep reasoning only when question complexity warrants it, cutting unnecessary compute on easy inputs. Addresses uniform-reasoning overhead in document reasoning.

entry.title: Dynamical phase selection controls compute scaling in looped transformers

author.name: Gunn Kim

entry.summary: Shows that looped transformers trained to identical accuracy realize distinct dynamical phases depending on initialization, with bifurcation mechanisms (saddle-node fold, Neimark-Sacker transition) determining how test-time compute scales; a normal-form reduction predicts relaxation-time scaling in the fold phase.

entry.title: Reward-Informed Sparse Autoencoders and the Solution-Completeness Confound

author.name: Tanvi Nagilla, Alexander Jameson, Daniel Manta, Shayaan Uddin

entry.summary: Reward-Informed Sparse Autoencoders train JumpReLU SAEs on activations from high- versus low-reward GRPO reasoning trajectories and ask what the resulting separation measures. On Llama-3.1-8B, the good/bad feature separation turns out to be largely solution completeness rather than reasoning quality, a cautionary confound for reward-guided interpretability.

entry.title: Not Just Reason, Not Just Scan: Reinforcement Learning for Proactive Scientific Error Verification over Academic Paper

author.name: Rongjin Li, Yuanxin Liu, Hao Zhou, Fandong Meng, Jie Zhou, Xu Sun

entry.summary: VERA-RL formulates scientific error detection in academic papers as a reinforcement learning task with a Reason-Verify-Scan loop, training multimodal LLMs to find and justify errors without prespecified issues. It addresses issue- and evidence-absent verification toward autonomous research assistants.

entry.title: Parameter-Efficient pretrained-CT-to-MRI Transfer for Rectal Cancer Segmentation: Performance-Calibration Trade-offs

author.name: Aneesh Rangnekar, Jorge Tapias Gomez, Joseph O Deasy, Harini Veeraraghavan

entry.summary: SWIFT adapts a Swin V2 encoder pretrained on 10,444 public 3D CT volumes via DINOv2-style self-supervision to T2-weighted MRI rectal cancer segmentation using parameter-efficient fine-tuning variants (decoder compression, LoRA, LoRA ensembles). It systematically evaluates accuracy, detection, calibration, and efficiency trade-offs for adaptive radiotherapy.

entry.title: The Reasoning Tax: Token Economics of LLM Reasoning Across Task Types and Deployment Contexts

author.name: Sachin Gopal Wani, Ajay Dholakia, David Ellison

entry.summary: Introduces the Token Economy Score, measuring the accuracy gain of reasoning models over non-reasoning baselines normalized by the generated-token multiplier, evaluated across 151 model-benchmark runs on seven benchmarks. Quantifies when extended thinking tokens earn their cost across task types and deployment contexts. A practical deployment-oriented benchmarking metric.

entry.title: ProofEvolve: Neuro-Symbolic Evolution for Formal Automated Theorem Proving

author.name: Wenqian Ye, Ziwei Guan, Eric Xie, Bohan Liu, Shivani Modi, Buyun Zhang, Ellie Dingqiao Wen, Henry Kautz, Aidong Zhang

entry.summary: ProofEvolve evolves explicit, formally verified symbolic proof structures alongside neural models, enabling recursive self-improvement in automated theorem proving and exploiting partial-proof feedback rather than sparse whole-proof signals. Targets the limitation that existing provers lock experience into weights or discard it per problem. A substantive neuro-symbolic theorem-proving contribution.

entry.title: Finding the Right Evidence: Factor-Guided Coarse-to-Fine Reasoning for Long Videos

author.name: Baixuan Xu, Yinyui Xu, Tianshi Zheng, Zhaowei Wang, Weiqi Wang, Haochen Shi, Jiayu Liu, Qing Zong, Xiyu Ren, Xinyu Geng, Zhitao He, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: PACE is a factor-guided coarse-to-fine evidence acquisition framework for long-video QA, diagnosing that prior agentic systems improve cue retrieval without corresponding accuracy gains because relevant evidence is not option-discriminative, then indexing clip-level descriptions and refining evidence selection.

entry.title: Generative Semantic Scene Completion

author.name: Shi Chen, Weifeng Ge

entry.summary: Recasts outdoor LiDAR semantic scene completion as a single discrete-diffusion formulation with three roles: paired sparse-dense synthesis (PS3), semantic-guided generative completion, addressing extreme class imbalance (>7000x) and 1% observed volume. Includes a new corpus trained alongside SemanticKITTI.

entry.title: Representation Measurements Under Function-Preserving Reparameterizations

author.name: Abdullah Karasan

entry.summary: This study shows that common representation measurements on language models are not invariant to function-preserving reparameterizations: permutation-based parallel analyses can change conclusions while the model function is fixed. It proves no data-internal reference procedure can preserve all desirable invariance properties simultaneously.

entry.title: SPT: Skills as Pre-Training Data for Agentic Language Models

author.name: Yufei Sun, Yudong Li, Yiming Cheng

entry.summary: Skill Pre-Training (SPT) applies causal language modeling to a corpus of public multi-file skill packages as mid-training for agentic LLMs, with reference-injection to preserve intra-package relations. This exploits freely available skill documents as supervision, avoiding expensive trajectory collection.

entry.title: Warning Shots: A Theory

author.name: David Scott Krueger

entry.summary: David Krueger argues that catastrophic warning shots are not necessary to generate governmental action on societal-scale AI risk, citing accelerating expert concern, political will from labor-market effects, and less harmful attention-drawing events like the HuggingFace incident. The piece offers a theory of how risk salience changes without mass-casualty events.

entry.title: A Safety-Gated Multimodal AI Backend for Mental-Health Support: Hierarchical State Representation, Conservative Risk Fusion, and Controlled Generation in Anian

author.name: Lei Wang, Xiao Wang, Lei Li

entry.summary: Anian is a safety-gated multimodal backend for perinatal mental-health support that places generative AI downstream of structured state representation, conservative risk fusion, and response gating across emotion, psychosocial, safety-risk, and intervention layers. It explicitly blocks free-form generation in unsafe contexts rather than relying on model refusals. A thoughtful architecture for a safety-critical deployment.

entry.title: AffectOmni: RL-Verifiable People-Centric Grounded Affective Reasoning for Social and Art-Related Scenes

author.name: Yibo Wang, Rui Yang, Jisheng Dang, Bimei Wang, Yitao Wu, Pengfei Cao, Wencan Zhang, Hong Peng, Bin Hu, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: AffectOmni trains multimodal LLMs with GRPO using People Focus and Temporal Order rewards to enforce attention to human evidence in affective reasoning, combating shortcut behavior where models answer correctly while ignoring micro-expressions and body language. Also addresses LLM-as-judge score clustering for reward discriminability. A solid RLVR contribution for grounded affective understanding.

entry.title: GameWAM: A World Action Model for Video Games

author.name: Yuncheng Guo, Zhanqiu Zhang, Yiwen Guo, Weijia Li

entry.summary: GameWAM is presented as the first World-Action Model for native closed-loop video game play and GUI control, jointly generating future visual observations and executable keyboard-mouse trajectories through parallel generative paths. It unifies game agents lacking dynamics modeling with world models lacking task policies. A meaningful step for unified generative game agents.

entry.title: Same Model, Different Harness: Different Coding-Agent Results

author.name: Sydney Lewis

entry.summary: Holds the model and tasks fixed while varying only the coding-agent harness, comparing full in-order conversation history against a harness that mechanically shortens older tool results and responds to stalled work. The treatment raises fail-to-pass fractions and complete solutions across SWE-bench variants under tight context. Demonstrates that harness design, not just model quality, drives coding agent results.

entry.title: FaithSieve: Fine-Grained Evaluation of Math Proofs with Faithful Formal Evidence

author.name: Ziyu Wang, Qiming Dai, Yishan Wu, Zaiwen Wen

entry.summary: FaithSieve is a Lean-assisted framework for fine-grained evaluation of natural-language math proofs, using formal evidence to localize early logical errors while guarding against overly broad formal targets and auto-formalization drift. Addresses gaps in model-judged proof evaluation. Contributes to rigorous verification of LLM mathematical reasoning.

entry.title: AgentJudgeBench: A Multi-Difficulty Benchmark for Evaluating LLM Judges on Agentic Tool-Calling

author.name: Abhigya Verma, Amit Kumar Saha, Seganrasan Subramanian, Sai Harshitha Aluru

entry.summary: AgentJudgeBench systematically studies LLM-as-a-judge reliability for agentic tool-calling over workflow DAGs, with 3,808 instances, six topologies, three difficulty tiers, five generators including GPT-5.4, and six judges. Judge alignment degrades monotonically with difficulty and 1.5x faster without ground truth. Fills an important evaluation gap as judges are increasingly used to score agents.

entry.title: Categorizer Automata for Discounted-Sum Payoffs

author.name: Nathalie Bertrand, Pranav Ghorpade, Senthil Rajasekaran, Sasha Rubin, Moshe Vardi

entry.summary: Introduces categorizer automata that read infinite reward sequences and identify which bin contains their discounted sum, generalizing comparator automata with a state space linear rather than exponential in bin count. Applied to synthesize MDP policies managing discounted-sum payoffs. Solid theory from strong authors including Vardi and Rubin.

entry.title: ASIL: Replacing Screenshot-and-Click with Structured State and Semantic Actions

author.name: Rui Xie, Lu Chen

entry.summary: ASIL argues screenshot-and-click is a poor interface for software-operating agents and proposes an agent-native layer exposing structured JSON observations and code-executable semantic actions across 15 applications, with a benchmark of 300 single- and 80 multi-application tasks. Challenges the GUI-agent paradigm on efficiency and semantic grounds. Interesting interface-level contribution.

entry.title: Omni-Interactive Universal Embedder

author.name: Wei-Yao Wang, Kazuya Tateishi, Shuyang Cui, Christian Simon, Takashi Shibuya, Shusuke Takahashi, Yuki Mitsufuji

entry.summary: OmniUE is proposed as the first omni-interactive universal embedder learning a unified embedding space across text, video, and audio via intermediate-layer learnable tokens, supporting queries composed of text, visual regions, and other modalities. Extends LLM-based embedders beyond the dominant text-image pairing. From a strong Sony industrial research group.

entry.title: LiveVVT: High-Fidelity Video Virtual Try-On in Real Time

author.name: Yushe Cao, Shikun Feng, Ruxiang Duan, Liyong Wang, Dianxi Shi, Chun Yu, Junliang Xing

entry.summary: LiveVVT introduces a rolling streaming diffusion framework for real-time video virtual try-on that preserves bounded bidirectional spatio-temporal modeling within causal recurrent generation. It addresses the prohibitive latency of full-clip diffusion methods while retaining synthesis quality, making try-on viable for continuous deployment.

entry.title: Making Clinical Language Models Auditable: Concept-Guided Fine-Tuning for Robust Prediction

author.name: Jin Mu, Guanhua Chen

entry.summary: CAST uses sparse autoencoders to expose human-auditable features in clinical language models, LLM-assisted labeling with ICD-10 constraints to identify artifact latents, and residual subtraction during fine-tuning to suppress note-specific artifacts. It improves robustness under deployment shift on MIMIC-IV while providing per-concept attributions.

entry.title: From Static to Dynamic: Benchmarking Real-World Code Review with MCR-Bench

author.name: Dewu Zheng, Yanlin Wang, Xiwen Wang, Kefeng Duan, Hongyu Zhang, Xilin Liu, Yuchi Ma, Zibin Zheng

entry.summary: MCR-Bench is the first defect state-aware benchmark for realistic multi-round LLM code review, with 2,269 real-world multi-round review scenarios across five languages, capturing iterative interaction rather than single-round static decisions.

entry.title: SWE-Prime: Fewer Trajectories, Better Performance

author.name: Dewu Zheng, Ruizhe Ye, Yanlin Wang, Yang Ye, Hongyu Zhang, Ensheng Shi, Xilin Liu, Yuchi Ma, Jianxing Yu, Zibin Zheng

entry.summary: SWE-Prime proposes multi-granularity, two-stage SFT data selection that filters agent trajectories at trajectory and segment levels, showing that successful trajectories contain noisy, risky steps and that fewer, better trajectories improve SWE-bench-style performance.

entry.title: Shared Actors Need Not Share Critics: Effects of Value Mismatch in Parallel Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zhenya Liu, Yang Meng, Zhuokai Zhao, Xuefeng Liu, Yuxin Chen

entry.summary: The paper analyzes a subtle but consequential flaw in parallel RL: a shared critic across heterogeneous environments must reconcile conflicting value targets, systematically redistributing advantage updates and reinforcing unhelpful actions. Using bandit models, it characterizes when value mismatch helps or harms.

entry.title: Chart2SVG: Editable SVG Generation from Raster Chart Images

author.name: Jinning Cui, Lu Chen, Haoyan Shi, Yue He, Chenglong Wang, Mengyu Zhou, Weidong Huang, Yunhai Wang

entry.summary: Chart2SVG is a multimodal LLM converting raster charts into structurally organized, semantically enriched editable SVGs, with a 33K-sample dataset (Beagle+), rendering-aware post-training, and a Chart Structure Graph for higher-level manipulation.

entry.title: SimCast-S2S: An Efficient Generative Model for Subseasonal Precipitation Forecasting via Transfer Learning from Climate Simulations

author.name: Hiep V. Dang, Antonios Mamalakis

entry.summary: SimCast-S2S is the first diffusion-based generative framework for probabilistic subseasonal-to-seasonal precipitation forecasting, using transfer learning from climate simulations to address weak signals and operational cost constraints with uncertainty quantification.

entry.title: Robust Neural Stimulation Response Modeling Through Meta-Learning and Pretraining

author.name: Matthew J Bryan, Daniel C Muir, Felix Schwock, Azadeh Yazdan-Shahmorad, Rajesh P N Rao

entry.summary: From Rajesh Rao's group, the paper demonstrates for the first time that meta-learning and pretraining improve neural stimulation response modeling, reducing catastrophic per-session forecast failures and calibration burden for closed-loop therapeutic stimulation.

entry.title: When Privacy Hurts Mergeability: Geometry-Aware Model Merging under Differential Privacy

author.name: Jin Liu, Junkang Liu, Ning Xi, Yinbin Miao, Dawei Wei, Ke Cheng, Jianfeng Ma

entry.summary: The paper identifies two geometric obstacles, local sharpness and reference drift, that make differentially private task models difficult to merge, and proposes geometry-aware fixes for DP model merging where released task models leak private fine-tuning data.

entry.title: Unifying Detection and Adaptation in Task-Free Continual Learning

author.name: Dezheng Han, Anbang Zhang, Zhihao Zhu, Shuaishuai Guo

entry.summary: FiUni unifies task detection and parameter-efficient continual adaptation for LLMs using orthogonality of principal subspaces in a K-FAC Fisher approximation, enabling batch-level task-free continual learning without explicit task boundaries. Addresses catastrophic forgetting in realistic task-free settings.

entry.title: Cross-Platform Generalisation Failure in Mental Health Natural Language Processing: A Five-Axis Fairness Audit of Transformer Models on Social Media

author.name: Rajveer Singh Pall, Sameer Yadav

entry.summary: Audits cross-platform generalization of transformer mental-health classifiers using a five-axis fairness framework (performance, calibration, significance, equity, attribution stability), finding 30-40% AUC degradation when models trained on one platform are tested on Reddit/Twitter. Highlights deployment risks for sensitive NLP.

entry.title: Planting a Latent Variable in Natural-Looking Text: a More Realistic Test of Belief States in LLMs and Their Link to Concept Geometry

author.name: Alexandru-Iulius Jerpelea

entry.summary: This paper plants a controllable latent variable in natural-looking text by steering a teacher LLM along sparse autoencoder directions following a ring Markov chain, then tests whether small trained models track belief states and connects this to concept geometry in LLM features. It bridges theoretical belief-state results and empirical interpretability.

entry.title: Ancient-Bench: A Comprehensive Multi-millennial, Multi-medium, and Multi-script Benchmark for Ancient Chinese Artifact Text Recognition

author.name: Hiuyi Cheng, Nuo Xu, Yuyi Zhang, Xuhan Zheng, Wei Pan, Jing Zhang, Dezhi Peng, Minghui Liao, Yihua Teng, Jihao Wu, Haoyu Ren, Lianwen Jin

entry.summary: Ancient-Bench introduces a 2,700-image benchmark for ancient Chinese artifact text recognition spanning 3,000 years of character evolution, nine artifact media, and seven historical scripts, with standardized evaluation protocols across heterogeneous media. It addresses fragmentation in existing heritage-digitization benchmarks.

entry.title: MeshPriorDiT: Hierarchical Modeling for Action-Conditioned Cloth Dynamics

author.name: Zihang Wang, Jianming Hu, Shang Su, Hao Huang, Mengkai Shi, Jun Gao, Shuo Feng

entry.summary: MeshPriorDiT is a hierarchical transformer dynamics model for action-conditioned cloth prediction that decomposes future motion into a structured mesh prior handling local material responses plus learned long-range coordination, combining the strengths of mesh GNNs and global-attention models.

entry.title: Benchmarking_Fast_Domain_Adaptation_for_Unsupervised_Speech_Units

author.name: Robin San Roman, Manel Khentout, Tu Anh Nguyen, Paul Michel, Yossi Adi, Emmanuel Dupoux

entry.summary: Introduces ABX-Accent, a benchmark on 10 English accents with small unlabelled adaptation sets, to study how self-supervised speech representations adapt few-shot to out-of-domain and accented speech. Addresses the long tail of accents for unsupervised speech modeling.

entry.title: Towards a universal meta-optics solver via large language models

author.name: Huanshu Zhang, Lei Kang, Yuyan Chen, Luxiang Wang, Zhaolong Cao, Douglas H. Werner

entry.summary: Presents a unified LLM workflow for multi-family metasurface modeling and inverse design by converting geometries and optical responses into instruction-following text and fine-tuning Gemma-2-9B (an existing model) across 8 metasurface families, outperforming family-specific surrogates.

entry.title: Neuro-symbolic PRM: Enhancing Scientific Reasoning via Structured Traces and Symbolic Verification

author.name: Yuxin Zi, Cong Xu, Suparna Bhattacharya, Martin Foltin, Amit Sheth

entry.summary: The neuro-symbolic PRM framework decouples STEM reasoning verification into symbolic validity, guaranteed by a deterministic verifier, and semantic groundedness, handled by a reward model. This targets reasoning steps that are executable and unit-consistent yet contextually ungrounded.

entry.title: Surgical Alignment in Knowledge Graph Training for Clinical Diagnosis with Large Language Models

author.name: Saksham Khatwani, He Cheng, Majid Afshar, Dmitriy Dligach, Yanjun Gao

entry.summary: A systematic study of five KG task formulations, three training paradigms, two biomedical knowledge graphs, and three base LLMs for clinical diagnosis, introducing GID and GD metrics for gradient-level intervention analysis. It reveals that comparable in-domain accuracy can hide very different knowledge transfer behavior depending on training paradigm.

entry.title: Reconstructing Humans and Objects in Interaction using Large Reconstruction Models

author.name: Agniv Chatterjee, Georgios Pavlakos

entry.summary: MILO leverages Large Reconstruction Models as geometric scaffolds to reconstruct 3D human-object interactions from a single image, moving beyond parametric fitting with reprojection and contact constraints. It targets applications in AR/VR, robotics, and embodied AI.

entry.title: CIFQA: A Deterministic Tool-Grounded Multi-Agent LLM Framework for Financial Query Answering

author.name: Kunjesh Parekh, Anil Kumar Tiwari, Divya Saxena

entry.summary: CIFQA decomposes calculation-intensive financial question answering across specialized agents for interpretation, routing, parameter extraction, and computation planning, delegating math to deterministic tools. It addresses the known failure mode of LLMs producing plausible but numerically wrong financial answers. The architecture is a sensible pattern rather than a fundamental advance.

entry.title: Knowledge Cards: Structured Knowledge for AI Systems

author.name: Liliana Ferreira

entry.summary: Proposes Knowledge Cards: expert-reviewed, structured, inspectable representations of the concepts, relations, and reasoning patterns an AI system should use, filling the gap between model, data, and system cards. Positioned as a documentation and governance artifact for consequential AI decisions. Conceptually valuable for grounding and auditability, though it is a position-style contribution.

entry.title: Predicting Consequences and Reinforcing Navigation Policies with Latent World Models

author.name: Zengmao Wang, Wei Gao, Shuhan Shen

entry.summary: Proposes a Latent World Model for robot navigation that predicts action-conditioned latent feature compatibility instead of reconstructing future observations, exploiting the correlation between spatial proximity and latent similarity. Counterfactual training leverages action sequences across trajectories. A targeted efficiency improvement for world-model-based control.

entry.title: Agent Mesh: Reliability Primitives for Non-Idempotent Agent Delegation - Identity Adequacy and Evidence Adequacy

author.name: Mazhar Shaikh, Anurag Rajkumar Bombarde, Harshal Pathak

entry.summary: A failure study of a production agentic software-delivery platform across 147 incidents, showing that service-mesh primitives like retries, timeouts, and circuit breakers violate their core assumptions when applied to non-idempotent agent delegation. Quantifies failure consequences such as undetected 54-call loops and guaranteed false circuit trips. Valuable production-grade evidence for agent reliability engineering.

entry.title: SKILL.state: Scalable Long-Horizon Agent Skills

author.name: Sanket Badhe, Priyanka Tiwari, Jonghyun Chung

entry.summary: SKILL.state replaces append-only conversational history in agent runtimes with an explicit, mutable execution state, feeding the model only the skill specification, current structured state, and latest observation while discarding intermediate reasoning. This prevents latency degradation and context poisoning over long horizons. A promising runtime architecture for long-running procedural skills.

entry.title: PILOT in the Loop: Live Self-Improvement for Long-Horizon Agents

author.name: Yang Xiao, Yusong Sun, Haoyi Wu, Wenyang Hui, Wen Da, Zhaokai Luo, Mu Chuan, Yao Hu, Wenjie Li, Chengyue Jiang

entry.summary: PILOT is a supervisor-worker harness enabling live self-improvement during long-horizon agent runs, using emerging experience to redirect the active run and update the persistent harness rather than only post-hoc. Contrasts with single-agent self-correction and subagent delegation that cannot redirect active work. Addresses a real architectural gap in agent self-improvement.

entry.title: Graph-Guided Selective Unlearning for Language Models: Controlling Support Routes Beyond Forget Seeds

author.name: Waqas Khan, Tabinda Sarwar, Jingyue Cong, Xun Yi, Estrid He

entry.summary: GRAPHSU expands machine unlearning scope beyond explicitly identified forget examples by constructing a weighted support-route graph that propagates deletion pressure through paraphrases, aliases, and neighboring examples with graded forgetting strengths. Targets enterprise compliance obligations on fine-tuned models. A concrete advance on the recoverability weakness of selective unlearning.

entry.title: DEEPCHART: How Far are LLMs from Faithful Data-Science Chart Generation?

author.name: Jiahui tang, Kuicai Dong, Dexun Li, Hongchao Gu, Haocheng Yu, Wei Han, Chen Zhang, Yong Liu, Hao Wang, Enhong Chen

entry.summary: DEEPCHART is an expert-annotated benchmark of 1,482 chart-generation instances from scientific papers, financial filings, and ecosystem reports, formulating chart generation as an Extract-Reason-Visualize pipeline evaluated stage by stage. Exposes data-level hallucinations that visually plausible LLM charts hide. Valuable diagnostic benchmark for multimodal data-science workflows.

entry.title: Evaluating human and LLM screening workflows in a conceptually complex scoping review: Recall--workload trade-offs and run-to-run consistency

author.name: Nikol Figalov\'a, Lynn Huestegge, Anne B\"ockler-Raettig

entry.summary: A preregistered comparison of human and LLM title-and-abstract screening in a conceptually complex scoping review, evaluating seven LLM runs against one lead and four assistants on 1,131 records with 316 verified eligible studies. Quantifies recall-workload trade-offs and run-to-run consistency. Rigorous evidence for LLM-assisted evidence synthesis.

entry.title: Counterfactual Bias Testing for Application Tracking System

author.name: Sai Yashwant, Shruti Bansal, Anurag Dubey, Samaroha Chatterjee, Satyam Kumar, Shreyash Gupta, Gantala Thulsiram

entry.summary: Presents a reusable methodology for counterfactual demographic bias testing of application tracking systems, using LLM agents to synthesize identity-neutral resumes with controlled treatments across five protected-characteristic axes, aligned with EU AI Act auditing requirements. Scales correspondence audits beyond hand-crafted studies. Practical compliance tooling for high-risk AI.

entry.title: Learning Transverse Momentum Distributions from Raw Scattering Events via Conditional Diffusion

author.name: Jitao Xu, Christopher Cocuzza, Kevin Braga, Daniel Lersch, Nobuo Sato, Yaohang Li

entry.summary: A conditional diffusion model learns to map raw SIDIS scattering event kinematics directly to transverse momentum dependent parton distribution functions, bypassing parameterized functional forms used in traditional nuclear physics extractions. Evaluated at CLAS12 kinematics, it recovers TMDs with informative, steadily narrowing uncertainties.

entry.title: PACE: A Unified Condense-and-Extract Paradigm for Fast VLM Inference

author.name: Junjie Liu, Shengyuan Ye, Xu Chen

entry.summary: PACE is a training-free inference framework that accelerates both the vision encoder and the LLM in VLMs via a unified condense-and-extract paradigm, addressing the unoptimized encoding latency and context/detail trade-offs of post-encoder token pruning.

entry.title: Compositional Online Learning for Semantic Data Processing Systems

author.name: Pawe\l{} Liskowski, Fuheng Zhao, Benjamin Han, Anupam Datta, Dimitris Tsirogiannis

entry.summary: The paper develops compositional online learning at the LLM call boundary in semantic data processing systems, observing that LLM latency and cost invert classical constraints on lightweight adaptive query processing. It provides a framework for combining online-learning components whose updates fit inside the LLM round-trip.

entry.title: How Language Models Organize and Structure Moral Knowledge

author.name: Orion Reblitz-Richardson

entry.summary: The paper trains linear probes for Moral Foundations Theory categories on open-weight LLMs and analyzes their geometric relationships in representation space, finding moral foundations span near-maximal independent dimensions while sharing a common positive component.

entry.title: Activation Outliers Matter: Robust Recovery for Quantized Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Tanzila Rahman, Mehran Taghian Jazi, Yunke Peng, Zhuang Ma, Anandharaju Durai Raju, Yao Wang, Xing Huang, Hei Yi Mak, Shadan Golestan, Hoang Le, Yonghan Dong, Wei Guo, Yaoyuan Wang

entry.summary: A systematic study of MXFP8-to-HiF4 quantization in multimodal LLMs for video generation and reasoning, showing MXFP8 is near-lossless while 4-bit formats degrade significantly, with activation quantization and activation outliers identified as the primary loss source and a robust recovery approach proposed.

entry.title: GRAS: Guided Reduced-Variance Proposals and Adaptive Selection for Training-Free Reward Alignment in Discrete Diffusion

author.name: Kwanyoung Kim

entry.summary: GRAS improves training-free reward steering of discrete diffusion models in the combined guidance-plus-search regime via Rao-Blackwellized variance-reduced gradient proposals and reward-adaptive selection temperatures, adding no denoiser cost.

entry.title: A Layer Importance Metric for Quantization Accounting for the Speed-Quality Trade-off in Autoregressive Models

author.name: Artem Safronov

entry.summary: Proposes a composite layer-importance metric combining information retention (SQNR-based) with throughput gains (roofline latency analysis) to guide selective quantization of small autoregressive LLMs. Profiling Gemma 3 1B (an existing model) finds FFN blocks and embeddings the best acceleration targets. Practical efficiency work for on-device models.

entry.title: Profit based evaluation of machine learning for nitrogen recommendations in winter wheat

author.name: Xulong Wang, Po Yang

entry.summary: Builds a profit-based test bench for ML nitrogen recommendations in winter wheat using 892 yield response curves from UK experiments, finding ML models fail as profitable recommenders despite being judged on prediction accuracy, and standard fixed advice is robust. A cautionary evaluation-paradigm result for decision-focused ML.

entry.title: Making Latent Evolution Explicit: Operator-Structured Transitions for World Action Models

author.name: Xiaoxiao Lu, Yunlong Dong, Jiahao Shi, Ye Yuan

entry.summary: Introduces LEON, an operator-structured transition network for world action models, modeling latent evolution via context-modulated operator networks rather than token-interaction transformers, making latent dynamics explicit. Targets robot policies augmented with scene-evolution prediction.

entry.title: TRACE: Retrospective Streaming Generation of Physical Fields under Sparse Structured Sensing

author.name: Xinyu Zhang, Lihao Chen, Panqi Chen, Lei Cheng, Ting Zhang, Jianlong Li, Shikai Fang

entry.summary: TRACE performs retrospective streaming generative reconstruction of physical fields from sparse, structured sensor streams, addressing the fixed-batch conditioning assumption of prior methods when probes scan, fields move, or frames drop. Aims at monitoring, inverse modeling, and digital twins.

entry.title: Hyperspectral Diffusion Equivariant Imaging (HyDiff-EI): A Self-supervised Framework for Hyperspectral Image Inpainting

author.name: Shuo Li, Mike Davies, Mehrdad Yaghoobi

entry.summary: HyDiff-EI is a self-supervised, test-time diffusion framework for hyperspectral image inpainting that embeds equivariant consistency constraints in the diffusion process, learning from a single corrupted acquisition without large-scale pretraining, suiting varied sensor configurations in remote sensing.

entry.title: Data-driven Koopman mode approximation: A neural power iteration algorithm

author.name: Guillaume O. Berger, Rapha\"el M. Jungers

entry.summary: The authors propose a neural power-iteration algorithm to approximate dominant Koopman modes of nonlinear dynamical systems, avoiding explicit construction of the operator projection. This mitigates curse-of-dimensionality issues and enables linear analysis and control of nonlinear dynamics.

entry.title: Scaling Graph Neural Networks for Friend Recommendation: Multi-Hash User Embeddings and Temporal Neighbor Sampling

author.name: Maksim Utushkin, Andrei Ovsiannikov, Alexander D'yakonov

entry.summary: The authors describe a production-scale GNN ranking system for friend recommendation on a social graph with hundreds of millions of users, combining multi-hash ID embeddings and temporal neighbor sampling to avoid massive embedding tables. It reports practical systems lessons for deploying message-passing GNNs at industrial scale.

entry.title: Evaluating Language Models in Realistic Conversational Contexts

author.name: Ilija Subasic, Andrew Rabinovich, Zhao Chen

entry.summary: UPHELD is a benchmark of hundreds of complete human-to-human professional dialogues (from Upwork) for evaluating LLM conversational quality beyond factual correctness, addressing the reliance of existing metrics on synthetic sources. It targets human-scale multi-turn dialogue evaluation with full references.

entry.title: Survival-Guided Length Control for Efficient Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Ivan Kobyzev, Abbas Ghaddar, Yufei Cui

entry.summary: Survival-guided length control recasts sequence-length selection in diffusion language models as a discrete-time survival problem over the EOS token, providing a training-free plug-in length predictor. It achieves up to 7x inference speedup across reasoning and code benchmarks while preserving accuracy.

entry.title: Benchmarking Clinical Decision Pathway Adherence in Large Language Models

author.name: Nuo Chen, Xinyang Jiang, Zilong Wang, Zhifei Zhang, Xiaoye Qu, Jiajun Deng, Yulan Guo, Cairong Zhao

entry.summary: MEGA-CDP is a benchmark built from 2,274 English and Chinese clinical guidelines yielding 42,353 cases with reference clinical decision pathways, evaluating whether medical LLMs generate guideline-adherent pathways in single- and multi-turn settings. It moves beyond final-answer accuracy toward process adherence.

entry.title: JudgeStealer: Extracting LLM Judging Capabilities across Evaluation Protocols

author.name: Chen Chen, Yaolin Chen, Xuehan Sun, Juan Lin, Xueluan Gong, Yuhang Zheng, Qian Wang, Kwok-Yan Lam

entry.summary: JudgeStealer is the first query-efficient extraction framework targeting LLM judging capabilities, replicating pointwise, pairwise, and listwise evaluation protocols by exploiting cross-protocol agreement under query budgets. It exposes a security risk as LLM judges become valuable intellectual property.

entry.title: UniFLM: United Segmentation and Measurement on Fetal Limb Ultrasonic Image

author.name: Zeen Zhou, Qiuhua Chen, Xiaojun Cao, Changmao Chen, Chao Sun, Bo Du

entry.summary: UniFLM introduces a unified framework for automatic cross-plane segmentation and biometric measurement of fetal limb bones in ultrasound, accompanied by a new annotated dataset covering humerus, femur, tibia-fibula, and radius-ulna. It aims to improve prenatal detection of lethal skeletal dysplasias.

entry.title: Contact-Aided Factor-Graph Localization for Underwater Sampling

author.name: Michele Grimaldi, Yosaku Maeda, Hitoshi Kakami, Ignacio Carlucho, Yvan R. Petillot, Tomoya Inoue

entry.summary: A Contact-Aided Factor-Graph Localization framework fuses suction-manipulator contact events with adaptive visual odometry, learned detections, and onboard sensors for AUV close-range seafloor sampling, treating physical interaction as an informative geometric constraint to overcome scale ambiguity over featureless seabeds.

entry.title: Notes on "Patterns and problems in emerging multiagent systems"

author.name: Shunk

entry.summary: These notes summarize Anthropic's research on emerging patterns and problems in multiagent systems, covering how agents spin up subagents, fail to treat other agents as peers with their own goals, and where highly parallelizable tasks work versus where coordination breaks down in a 45-agent forum setup.

entry.title: Dependency-Aware Revocable Decoding for Efficient Diffusion Large Language Model Inference

author.name: Wooje Park, Insu Lee, Minyoung Noh, Jaeyun Jang, Sungmin Lee, Kyuhong Shim, Byonghyo Shim

entry.summary: DARD identifies that unreliable early tokens in diffusion LLM decoding can corrupt the verification context itself, and proposes a training-free revocable decoding scheme separating masked, candidate, and unmasked states with selective verification contexts. This improves quality under parallel decoding.

entry.title: Tensegrity Continuum Robots Enable Task-Adaptive Morphologies for Cooperative Behaviors

author.name: Mahmud Hasan Saikot, Sydney Spiegel, Sudheera Akalanka Kariyawasam, Andrew Stefka, Josh Chrisler, Jianguo Zhao

entry.summary: This paper introduces a modular reconfigurable robot combining tensegrity-based compliant bodies with claw-based connection mechanisms, unifying continuum-robot compliance with self-reconfiguration into task-adaptive multi-robot morphologies, with units able to manipulate and locomote independently.

entry.title: GROUND: Reducing Hallucinations in LLM-Based Enterprise Analytics Through Governed Semantic Definitions

author.name: Aravind Sasidharan Pillai

entry.summary: GROUND constrains LLM-generated enterprise analytics to a governed semantic layer of approved metrics, dimensions, join paths, and row-level security, validating SQL before execution to reduce hallucinated metrics and unsafe access. It targets the gap between schema-grounded text-to-SQL and real enterprise reporting requirements. Practically valuable for production deployments.

entry.title: Structured Evidence Routing for Incident Risk Prediction from Multimodal Longitudinal EHRs

author.name: Animesh Agarwal, Meysam Ghaffari, Nina Fatehi, Carlos Morato

entry.summary: Introduces structured evidence routing for incident risk prediction from longitudinal multimodal EHRs, using a router-predictor-reviewer workflow that separates full-record access from disease-specific assessment. It matches or reaches competitive AUROC against EHRSHOT-supervised baselines across five incident diagnosis tasks. Combines agentic decomposition with clinical prediction effectively.

entry.title: LLM Agents for Time-Series: A Survey

author.name: Yilong Chen, Xiao Qin, Chenghao Liu, Liang Wu, Noelle I. Samia, Kaize Ding

entry.summary: A problem-driven survey organizing LLM agents for time-series into forecasting and reasoning, augmentation and synthesis, anomaly detection and diagnosis, and decision support, examining how task requirements shape architecture, tool use, and memory. Compares datasets, environments, and reported performance. Timely consolidation of a fast-moving area.

entry.title: Knowing When Not to Reuse: Conditional Experience Transfer in Autonomous LLM Post-Training

author.name: Tingyun Li, Wenfeng Feng, Weiqing Li, Abudukelimu Wuerkaixi, Guohua Liu, Yuewei Zhang

entry.summary: Formulates conditional experience transfer for autonomous LLM post-training: deciding which past update evidence remains actionable after the parent model has changed, since treating past success as context-free permission wastes compute or derails subsequent training. Proposes criteria for knowing when not to reuse experience. A useful formalization for self-improving post-training loops.

entry.title: GraphMemix: Query-Aware Evidence Forests for Long-Term Multimodal Agent Memory

author.name: Geng Li, Yuhao Wang, Dong Li, Jianye Hao, Yuxin Peng

entry.summary: GraphMemix frames long-term multimodal agent memory as query-aware evidence-forest construction via combinatorial optimization, expanding multi-view seed memories through schema and semantic relations while decoupling direct support from anchor-conditioned relation values. Avoids expensive question-agnostic summaries and naive similarity matching. A technical advance in agent memory.

entry.title: Evaluating Confidence-Gated Retrieval with Matched Trajectory Replay

author.name: Prateek Chhikara

entry.summary: The paper proposes matched trajectory replay, a controlled protocol for evaluating confidence-gated retrieval decisions in interactive LLM agents, holding answers, evidence, budgets, and costs fixed. It finds calibrated confidence changes action-level outcomes versus raw verbalized confidence in multi-hop QA across Mistral, GPT, and Qwen models.

entry.title: Active Diffusion-Based Inference for Ill-Posed Inverse Problems under Incomplete Priors

author.name: Jitao Xu, Nobuo Sato, Yaohang Li

entry.summary: The authors propose an active diffusion-based solver for ill-posed inverse problems that iteratively detects and corrects model misspecification via posterior uncertainty, learning the correct parameter region even when initial training bounds exclude true parameters. It gives a Bayesian justification for adaptive domain augmentation.

entry.title: Successive Capacity Growth: Task-Complexity-Driven Width and Depth Expansion for Vision Transformer Encoders in JEPA World Models

author.name: Frederik Berenz

entry.summary: Successive Capacity Growth grows JEPA world-model ViT encoders incrementally in width or depth from a minimal 283K-parameter start, using function-preserving expansion with test-and-verify rollbacks driven by prediction loss. It avoids over- and under-provisioning for varying task complexity.

entry.title: Beyond F1: Evaluating Coverage and Failure Recovery in AI Model Security Scanners

author.name: Qianlong Lan, Vinothini Pandurangan, Anuj Kaul, Indranil Sanyal

entry.summary: The paper evaluates ML model security scanners (ModelScan, ModelAudit, Fickling) on a controlled pickle and PyTorch artifact benchmark, going beyond F1 to measure coverage, analysis completion, and failure recovery. It finds substantial gaps in definitive security decisions across tools.

entry.title: SAGE: Variate-Wise Semantic Augmentation for Vision-Language Time Series Forecasting

author.name: Haizhao Fan, Xinyi Le

entry.summary: SAGE is a CLIP-based framework for time-series forecasting that injects per-variate semantic knowledge via text and visual encodings rather than uniform dataset-level prompts or costly inference-time LLM calls. Jointly models temporal, cross-variable, textual, and visual information end-to-end. Falls in the emerging semantic time-series modeling space.

entry.title: Graph-Based Pseudo-multimodal Contrastive Learning for 12-Lead ECG Representations

author.name: Mengyu Wang, Kozo Okada, Takafumi Goto, Natsuko Jinba, Hiroki Yamaya, Kiyoshi Hibi, Tomoki Hamagami

entry.summary: Graph-CMMC is a graph-based pseudo-multimodal contrastive learning framework for 12-lead ECG representation learning that captures inter-lead dependencies, which CNN/RNN single-lead approaches miss. Targets coronary artery disease diagnosis using a standard clinical modality.

entry.title: Decentralized Multitask Learning over Learned Task Graphs

author.name: Zirui Wan, Stefan Vlaski

entry.summary: Proposes decentralized multitask learning over learned task graphs: a two-phase method that estimates a graph Laplacian from noisy non-cooperative gradient iterates, then uses it for cooperative diffusion learning, with analysis under a Gaussian Markov random field prior. Removes the known-structure assumption in graph-regularized multitask learning.

entry.title: TRACE-CRC: Trajectory-Adaptive Conformal Risk Control for Multi-Step Channel State Information Prediction

author.name: Kiarash Rezaei, Mehdi Sattari, Javad Aliakbari, Tommy Svensson, Paolo Monti, Carlos Natalino

entry.summary: TRACE-CRC applies trajectory-adaptive conformal risk control to multi-step CSI prediction in wireless systems, providing calibrated uncertainty over full channel trajectories so downstream beamforming and scheduling decisions remain safe. Combines conformal prediction with wireless prediction pipelines.

entry.title: Ultra Low-Power, Lightweight, Probabilistic RSS-Based Path Reconstruction: A System for Landscape-Scale Bee Tracking

author.name: Christopher J. Noroozi, Joseph L. Woodgate, Michael Mangan, Michael T. Smith

entry.summary: A probabilistic RSS-based path-reconstruction system enabling landscape-scale tracking of ultra-lightweight, power-constrained receivers such as bees, using few RSS measurements to avoid the power demands of angle-of-arrival inference. Combines signal processing and ML for movement ecology.

entry.title: When Interference Graphs Evolve: Doubly Robust Estimation of Dynamic Peer Effects

author.name: Xiaojing Du

entry.summary: Introduces a causal contrast framework and the DynaNet-DR doubly robust estimator for peer effects when interaction graphs evolve, separating own-treatment, peer-exposure, and network-evolution effects with a temporally factorized propensity model. Careful causal methodology for dynamic interference.

entry.title: Interpretable, Fairly Evaluated Automated L2 Speaking Assessment that Beats the Single-Human Ceiling and Why Pause Encoding Does Not Change LLM Fluency Scores

author.name: Eichi Uehara

entry.summary: Builds an interpretable feature-plus-LLM hybrid for automated L2 English speaking assessment, evaluated without fitting to human labels against the ICNALE archive of ~80 raters; a deterministic speech-timing composite reaches rho=0.764 and a blend exceeds the single-human ceiling, with analysis of pause encoding effects on fluency scores.

entry.title: Linear Independence of Polynomial Compositions and Identifiability of Deep Neural Networks

author.name: Kathl\'en Kohn, Giovanni Luca Marchetti, Alex Massarenti, Massimiliano Mella

entry.summary: This theory paper conjectures and partially proves linear independence results for polynomial compositions, generalizing Newman-Slater's theorem, and uses them to characterize parameter identifiability of deep fully connected networks with polynomial activations. It connects algebraic geometry to understanding of neural network parameter symmetries.

entry.title: Data-efficient crack quantification in lithium-ion cathodes using foundation model transfer

author.name: Thorsten Tegetmeyer-Kleine, Thomas Schmitt, Phillip Aquino, Christiane Rahe, Dirk Uwe Sauer, Weihan Li

entry.summary: A frozen self-supervised vision transformer with a lightweight decoder and model-assisted annotation enables data-efficient quantification of particle cracking in lithium-ion cathodes from huge electron-microscopy images. The approach converts sparse labeling budgets into population-scale degradation measurements relevant to battery aging.

entry.title: TreeGraft: Adaptive Multi-Drafter Grafting for Tree-Based Speculative Decoding

author.name: Jiaming Fan, Daming Cao, Canchen Huang, Jiale Fu, Jin Zhang, Junjie Gao, Kai Yang, Xiangzhong Luo, Xu Yang

entry.summary: TreeGraft introduces a multi-drafter speculative decoding framework where drafters of different costs jointly build a shared draft tree, with the stronger drafter rescoring the weaker drafter's candidates. This resolves the speed-versus-quality dilemma of single-drafter tree methods for LLM inference.

entry.title: Agents Don't Paginate: First-Chunk Selection for LLM Tool Responses

author.name: Tatiana Petrova, Andrei Mazniak, Radu State

entry.summary: Analyzing session logs from MCP middleware, the authors find coding agents never request a second page of tool responses, making first-chunk selection critical. They formalize first-chunk selection as a 0/1 knapsack over SWE-bench Verified tasks and compare six value functions for maximizing precision-at-1.

entry.title: AfriSwitch: A Benchmark for In-the-Wild African Code-Switched Speech Recognition

author.name: Gabrial Zencha Ashungafac, Busayo Awobade, Tobi Olatunji

entry.summary: AfriSwitch is a 61-hour human-transcribed benchmark of in-the-wild code-switched speech across 16 African languages, with switch-level tags and code-mixing indices. Zero-shot evaluation of five multilingual ASR systems reveals large performance gaps on real code-switched speech.

entry.title: Reasoning about In-Context Samples for Machine-Translation

author.name: Maxime Bouthors, Josep Crego, Fran\c{c}ois Yvon

entry.summary: This work introduces fragment-based reasoning for LLM machine translation with in-context exemplars: the model extracts parallel source-target fragments from retrieved examples as intermediate reasoning traces before producing the translation, trained by distilling silver fragments from a teacher. Experiments with the Qwen3 family across six languages show significant gains.

entry.title: DocTalkBN: A Novel Dataset of Expert Telemedicine Conversations in Bengali

author.name: Anik Saha, Fahmida Sultana Naznin, Sadatul Islam Sadi, Ananya Shahrin Promi, Wahid Al Azad Navid, Rifat Shahriyar

entry.summary: DocTalkBN is a 557-hour multimodal dataset of real Bengali telemedicine conversations with board-certified physicians, spanning 26 specialties with 1.5k multi-turn patient calls and 1.7M tokens. It preserves authentic spoken interaction for medical conversational AI in a low-resource language.

entry.title: SSMB: Self-Supervised Local Feature Detection under Motion Blur

author.name: Zhenjun Zhao, Fabio Bellavia, Wenting Wang, Fan Zhu, Jiajun Wu, Suryansh Kumar, Mingqiang Wei, Haoang Li, Javier Civera

entry.summary: SSMB is a deblur-free, self-supervised keypoint detector robust to motion blur, introducing a Local Discriminability Enhancement module that avoids handcrafted detectors and external pseudo-labels. It targets the repeatability degradation that blur causes in feature localization for SLAM and tracking.

entry.title: Beyond Edge Cuts: Activity-Weighted Multicast Hypergraph Mapping for Spiking Neural Networks on Mesh NoCs

author.name: Amirreza Khorasanian

entry.summary: M-HySMap reformulates mapping spiking neural networks onto mesh neuromorphic many-cores as route-aware, activity-weighted multicast hypergraph mapping rather than pairwise graph partitioning, optimizing destination fanout, shared mesh routes, and congestion. It better matches the physical one-to-many spike communication event.

entry.title: Beyond Shallow-Water Photorealism: Physically and Sensor-Grounded Simulation for Deep-Sea Robotics

author.name: Michele Grimaldi, Enrico Di Maria, Ignacio Carlucho, Yvan R. Petillot

entry.summary: This work extends the Stonefish underwater simulator with deep-sea physical and sensor realism, including stochastic IMU and DVL drift, magnetometer disturbances, higher-order hydrodynamics, terramechanics, pressure-driven variability, and physically based underwater optics, to better support AUV/ROV development beyond shallow-water photorealism.

entry.title: Barrier Function Conformal Safety Clearance Certification with CVaR for Driving Trajectory Selection

author.name: Pei Yu Chang, Qadeer Ahmed

entry.summary: This paper certifies driving-trajectory safety clearance by combining a differentiable separating-axis barrier margin that lower-bounds oriented-bounding-box clearance with CVaR-based tail evaluation and post-selection conformal calibration of the plan-time versus realized safety margin gap.

entry.title: On efficiency gains via augmenting a tiny sample with a massive auxiliary sample

author.name: Yen-Chi Chen

entry.summary: This statistical theory paper analyzes augmenting a tiny target sample with a massive auxiliary sample via Tukey factorization, showing IPW suffers the limited target sample problem while full-likelihood methods can achieve full efficiency gain (parametric rates set by the auxiliary sample) for exponential families and mixtures.

entry.title: Common Geodesics Do Not Guarantee Fisher Consistency of the Structured SVM: Minimal Counterexamples and a Tree-Metric Classification

author.name: Jintao Fei, Jiangying Luo

entry.summary: Shows the common-geodesic metric condition for structured SVM Fisher consistency is not sufficient for the coordinate-wise argmax decoder, with a minimal four-output counterexample and a complete classification of tree metrics where argmax consistency holds (paths only). A sharp theoretical correction to a known result.

entry.title: Multi-Dataset Inverse Problem Solving with Distributed Generative AI

author.name: Daniel Lersch, Steven Goldenberg, Johann Rudi, Markus Diefenthaler, Kevin Brager, Xingfu Wu, Yaohang Li, Nobuo Sato

entry.summary: Generalizes a scalable asynchronous generative AI inverse-problem framework to jointly analyze multiple heterogeneous datasets with different measurement settings, jointly rather than naively merged, targeting shared unmeasurable quantities. Computational-science systems contribution.

entry.title: Hadamard Flattening and Gaussian Pooling Sketch for Least Squares with Coordinate-wise Guarantee

author.name: Zhao Song, Lichen Zhang

entry.summary: Improves coordinate-wise guarantees for randomized least-squares sketching using Hadamard flattening and Gaussian pooling, achieving l_infinity-accuracy solutions at improved row counts over prior SRHT results. Randomized numerical linear algebra theory.

entry.title: ElementCheck: Complexity-Aware Long-Form Text Factuality Evaluation via Sentence Elements

author.name: Xinming Wang, Haoran Du, Yi Chen, Jian Xu, Hongming Yang, Han Hu, Yulong Chen, Cheng-Lin Liu, Xu-Yao Zhang

entry.summary: ElementCheck is a complexity-aware framework for long-form factuality evaluation that extracts entity pairs linked by verifiable connections into an element graph, using graph topology to decide when direct verification suffices versus when targeted decomposition is needed. It addresses noise and fixed granularity in the standard decompose-retrieve-verify pipeline.

entry.title: CARE: Causally-Aligned Reasoning Exploration for Medical Large Language Models

author.name: Yucheng Zhou, Peng Luo, Qianning Wang, Chengzhong Xu, Jianbing Shen

entry.summary: CARE is a framework for medical LLM reasoning that curates intrinsic training experiences using causal conditions to avoid the right-answer-wrong-reason trap of outcome-based RL, addressing credit assignment failure and gradient variance. It targets safer clinical reasoning under scarce expert annotations.

entry.title: Meta-Learning Where to Allocate Experts: Task-Conditioned Layer-Wise Compression for MoEs

author.name: Rongfeng Wang, Shichao Weng, Zhiqiang Wang, Xinyu Liu, Yang Yi, Peilong Zhou, Hongwei Tang

entry.summary: MetaNet is a support-set controller that predicts per-layer expert-retention thresholds and routing biases for frozen mixture-of-experts models, task-conditioning the compression without touching backbone or router. It addresses the fixed active-expert allocation limitation of deployed MoEs.

entry.title: Cross-Platform Benchmark of Neural 3D Reconstruction for Autonomous Laboratory Robots

author.name: Yongho Kim, Mengjiao Han, Victor Mateevitsi, Silvio Rizzi, Michael E. Papka, Nicola Ferrier

entry.summary: A systematic cross-platform benchmark of neural 3D reconstruction (NeRF, 3D Gaussian Splatting, SAM3D single-image) for autonomous laboratory robots, spanning devices from single-board computers to servers and measuring training and rendering latency against control-loop budgets. It clarifies real-time viability on the hardware robots actually run.

entry.title: Graph-Based Modeling of Financial Volatility Dynamics

author.name: Chuanzhen Wang, Alice Zhang, Wei Chen, Michael Brown

entry.summary: FA-GSTN reframes realized volatility forecasting as spatio-temporal graph modeling of the implied volatility surface, with nodes as grid points and finance-aware adaptive spatial and temporal edges. Domain-informed architecture for risk management and derivatives pricing.

entry.title: Constraint-Aware Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Static Shape Estimation of Co-Manipulative Continuum Robots

author.name: Rana Danesh, Pari Qarehdaghi, Farrokh Janabi-Sharifi

entry.summary: A constraint-aware PINN for static shape estimation of co-manipulative continuum robots enforcing static equilibrium and loop-closure residuals of the closed chain, outperforming a purely data-driven ANN under limited noisy data. Robotics-focused physics-informed learning.

entry.title: A Unified Descriptive-Complexity Framework for Model Selection under Correlated Designs

author.name: Yanhang Zhang, Wei Liu, Yuhong Yang

entry.summary: Proposes a Descriptive-Complexity Information Criterion for model selection under correlated designs and exponentially many model classes, with selection consistency under sub-Weibull noise without RIP-type conditions and oracle risk bounds under misspecification. Coding-theoretic model selection theory.

entry.title: Natural-Language Policies to Executable Decisions: An Interpretable Large Language Model Framework

author.name: Ziqiang Zhang, Jing Ma, Zilong Wang, Jiayuan Chen, Yi Qiao, Yu He, Wei Zhang, Dai Cheng, Xiaoyu Shen

entry.summary: A production-grade LLM pricing system for large-scale tourism where LLMs handle structured extraction and bounded policy selection while all numeric pricing is executed deterministically, with policies compiled into interpretable condition trees. This offers a template for reliable, auditable LLM deployment in financial decision-making.

entry.title: Cross-lingual Representation Learning via Centroid Intervention Fusion

author.name: Wei Sun, Marie-Francine Moens

entry.summary: Centroid Intervention Fusion consolidates multiple per-language cross-lingual intervention projections into a single language-shared operator applied at inference time without parameter updates. This improves scalability and knowledge sharing for low-resource language transfer in LLMs.

entry.title: SPEAR: Distilling Domain-Adaptive Reasoning Skeletons via Sequential Symbolic Alignment in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zhuochun Li, Yuelyu Ji, Yiming Zeng, Daqing He

entry.summary: SPEAR is a training-free, plug-and-play process reward method for sequence-level on-policy distillation that projects reasoning traces into domain-adaptive symbolic milestones scored via longest common subsequence. It avoids the dilemma between sparse outcome rewards and expensive neural PRMs.

entry.title: Instruction Quality Matters: Refining Instructions for Effective Preference Learning

author.name: Seohyeong Lee, Hwaran Lee, Buru Chang

entry.summary: This paper identifies instruction quality as a hidden bottleneck in preference learning, showing via Best/Worst-of-N analyses that weak instructions constrain both ceiling and floor of response quality. An instruction-refinement pipeline using reward signals and rubric-guided feedback improves preference data.

entry.title: Task-space model-based control of pneumatic soft actuators

author.name: Nithin S. Kumar, Joshua Gaston, D. Caleb Rucker, Eric J. Barth

entry.summary: This paper presents real-time task-space feedback control and estimation for pneumatic soft actuators based on a non-minimal coordinate discrete elastic rod model with holonomic constraints, combining a quasi-static feedforward inverse model, task-space PI control, and a dynamic observer, supporting up to 10 discretized rods in real time.

entry.title: EduRiskX: A Neuro-Symbolic Framework with F-Logic Reasoning for Early Academic Risk Prediction

author.name: Yu Fu, Yongqi Kang, Yong Zhao, Rongfang Bie

entry.summary: EduRiskX combines a temporal Transformer predictor with an F-Logic symbolic rule base to predict student academic risk early in online education while producing interpretable outputs. It targets the black-box trust problem that limits adoption of predictive models by educators. The neuro-symbolic integration is sensible but the domain contribution is application-level rather than architectural.

entry.title: EEG-to-Report: An Annotation and Feature-Text Framework for Training Language Models on Clinical EEG

author.name: Xuan-The Tran, Le Trung Kien Nguyen

entry.summary: This paper identifies an Accuracy-Efficiency Paradox: highly accurate on-device energy forecasting can produce a net energy deficit once inference energy and battery aging are counted. It proposes a Total Cost of Ownership framework that treats battery degradation as physical energy loss. The framing is a useful corrective for edge AI deployment decisions.

entry.title: TutorTrace: A Dataset and Taxonomy for Classifying Learner Behavioral States during AI-Assisted Programming Education

author.name: David Barron, Xiaohang Tang, Rezky Dwisantika, Minsun Kim, David H. Smith IV, Jiaming Cui, Yan Chen

entry.summary: TutorTrace converts low-level IDE telemetry into real-time learner behavioral context for AI programming tutors, releasing a dataset of roughly 180K events, 13,633 behavioral segments, and a taxonomy of learner states across 480 students. Enables tutors to adapt to what learners did, not just what they say. A solid dataset and taxonomy contribution for AI-assisted education.

entry.title: Don't Overthink, Don't Underthink: Toward Adaptive Reasoning in Agentic AI

author.name: Md Jueal Mia, M. Hadi Amini

entry.summary: Argues that fixed or pre-allocated reasoning controls do not fit agentic AI, where reasoning needs evolve dynamically through planning, tool use, memory, and agent interactions, leading to overthinking or underthinking. Proposes toward adaptive reasoning allocation in agentic workflows. A direction-setting contribution rather than a validated method.

entry.title: SIGMA: Structured Noise-Effect-Aware Grouped Multi-Agent Aggregation

author.name: Li Mingqian

entry.summary: SIGMA characterizes structured noise effects in cooperative multi-agent RL, where independently introduced observation disturbances produce locally correlated decision effects through cooperation structures, and proposes grouped multi-agent aggregation to exploit this structure. Addresses robustness gaps in existing MARL methods. Technically coherent but incrementally scoped.

entry.title: Relational Over-Regularization: Graph-Based AI-Generated Text Detection via Sentence Transition Deviation

author.name: Hyeonchu Park, Bugeun Kim

entry.summary: Identifies a sentence-pair-level structural signal for AI-generated text detection: LLMs exhibit inflated inter-sentence transition variance via recurring similarity bursts and templated transitions, formalized as Relational Over-Regularization and validated across four benchmarks. The contribution is the relational problem formulation rather than a new architecture. Offers generator-robust detection signals.

entry.title: AI Control Scientist: LLM-driven Agentic System for Automated Control Design

author.name: Haiteng Wang, Weihao Li, Jing Zhang, Lei Ren

entry.summary: AI Control Scientist is an LLM-driven agent that generates optimized controllers from natural-language design requirements via task modeling, controller design, and closed-loop parameter tuning agents. Targets the expert-heavy, manual tuning bottleneck in industrial control. Promising domain application of agentic LLMs to engineering design.

entry.title: LiveSim: Simulating Environment-Shaped Users in Multi-Agent Live-Stream Ecosystems

author.name: Jiaqi Xu, Yiran Qiao, Jing Chen, Qiwei Zhong, Xiang Ao, Xueqi Cheng

entry.summary: LiveSim simulates live-stream ecosystems with LLM users represented as editable behavioral hypotheses refined through trajectory-grounded interactions, extracting environment-shaped effects as transferable signals. Moves beyond static user profiles for socially intensive multi-agent simulation. Interesting for ecosystem modeling and policy testing.

entry.title: C-Unseen: Weak Signal Detection in Dynamic Temporal Knowledge Graphs via LLM Reasoning

author.name: Yassir Lairgi, Ludovic Moncla, Khalid Benabdeslem, R\'emy Cazabet, Pierre Cl\'eau

entry.summary: Builds an MCP server reproducing a proprietary hardware design tool and benchmarks locally deployed LLM agents on expert-defined, dependency-ordered design workflows, motivated by confidentiality constraints. Quantifies whether local models can reliably execute multi-step tool-calling in industry-realistic settings. Useful for the on-premise agent deployment question.

entry.title: A Contract-Centered Architecture for Scalable and Manageable Agentic Runtimes

author.name: Yaxiao Liu, Pengbo Liu, Yiwen Liu, Yihua Guan, Zhenghe Hou, Jiaxing Song

entry.summary: Proposes an enterprise architecture for agentic AI built on four responsibility objects (Skill, Harness, Scaffold, and an externally governed data substrate) treated as organizational contracts across business, engineering, and governance teams. It targets the coordination problem of owning and evolving agent capabilities at scale rather than single-task benchmark performance.

entry.title: FaultLens: Learning Compact Behavioral Test Suites for Generated Operational Programs

author.name: Zeming Liu, Hang Lyu, Jingtao Zhang

entry.summary: FaultLens learns compact behavioral test suites for generated operational programs using a sparse fault-probe outcome cache and greedy-plus-diversity probe selection. It aims to balance cost of exhaustive regression suites against sparse boundary fault detection.

entry.title: From Reasoning to Pixels: Grounded Medical Multimodal LLMs for VQA and Segmentation

author.name: Haowen Gu, Gensheng Pei, Junzhu Mao, Qiong Wang, Mingwu Ren, Yazhou Yao

entry.summary: MedREAL unifies medical VQA reasoning with pixel-level segmentation grounding, introducing Seg Anchored Reasoning Pooling to align linguistic reasoning with spatial localization. It aims to improve clinical trustworthiness of medical multimodal LLMs beyond global image features.

entry.title: When Memory Takes Gradients: Collaborative Vector Memory for Agentic Recommender Systems

author.name: Hanchong Chen, Xing Tang, Lingjie Li, Xiongfeng Shan, Xiuqiang He

entry.summary: CoVeMem replaces text-based agent memory in agentic recommender systems with a collaborative vector memory built from frozen LightGCN user and item states, retrieved by candidate sets at each decision. It enables training the memory end-to-end and preserves graded collaborative evidence lost in textual narratives.

entry.title: Per-View Gaussian Predictions Enable Training-Free Distractor Filtering in Feed-Forward 3DGS

author.name: Kangmin Seo, Jae-Pil Heo

entry.summary: The paper introduces a training-free filtering procedure for feed-forward 3D Gaussian Splatting that removes transient distractor objects by exploiting per-view Gaussian predictions, re-rendering with each view's Gaussians excluded. It reduces blur, duplication, and floating artifacts in casual-capture reconstructions.

entry.title: Multi-Person Human Motion Forecasting in Complex Scenes

author.name: Serdar Ozsoy, Lars Doorenbos, Juergen Gall

entry.summary: OCSD is a conditional diffusion model for multi-person human motion forecasting in complex scenes, integrating object cues via per-timestep conditioning and modeling social interactions with a dedicated encoder. It handles variable numbers of people and human-object reasoning in a unified framework.

entry.title: Emotional Preferences as Goal-Priority Regulation

author.name: Shiqi Liu, Yihua Tan, Hu Fu, Guanyu Qi

entry.summary: Inspired by the goal-directed theory of emotion, this paper computationally realizes emotional preferences as state-dependent regulation of competing lower-level goal priorities via reinforcement learning. It proposes a conception of emergent emotional preference induced by high-level goals.

entry.title: When Text Misleads: Inconsistent-Aware Reasoning for Audio-Grounded Dialogue

author.name: Yen-Ju Lu, Yuzhe Wang, Yaohan Guan, Xiluo He, Jiarui Hai, Mingrui Liang, Kaavya Chaparala, Thomas Thebaud, Laureano Moro-Velazquez, Najim Dehak, Jesus Villalba

entry.summary: The paper formalizes cross-modal disagreement in spoken dialogue, where transcripts suggest plausible but wrong interpretations while acoustic cues support different answers. It builds a scalable framework converting disagreement regions into conflict QA examples to test genuine speech grounding.

entry.title: KnockGS:interaction-Grounded Calibrationof Physical Gaussian Representations

author.name: Chenchen Ge, Hanwen Shen, Bowen Jing, Jiyuan Cai, Xiaofeng Wang, Hongsen Lei, Weitao Zhou, Dandan Zhang, Haibao Yu

entry.summary: KnockGS estimates elasticity and density parameters of physics-integrated 3D Gaussian object representations from observed dynamics under a known applied force, turning force-induced response into a calibration signal. It removes the need for manually specified material parameters.

entry.title: Persona-Execution Separation: An Architecture Pattern for Evolving LLM Agents under Execution Audit

author.name: Yisen Xi

entry.summary: Persona-Execution Separation is an architecture pattern placing LLM agent persona and execution in different trust domains connected by a governed contract bridge with approval matrices, DLP, and audit controls. It targets organizations needing free persona evolution alongside traceable audited execution.

entry.title: Distributed Training using an Intelligent Network

author.name: Nihar Shah, Ben Blier

entry.summary: The paper proposes making the WAN an active participant in distributed training, using multicast and in-line FPGA aggregation to ease egress and ingress bottlenecks, plus an optimization framework producing rotating-clique synchronization schedules around the network topology.

entry.title: Active Curriculum Refinement for Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Zhenya Liu, Yuxin Chen

entry.summary: PATH performs active learning over a curriculum DAG in RL, sampling diverse curriculum paths and reallocating training to unmastered regions, exploiting explicit prerequisite structure among environments.

entry.title: When Is the Sharp Covariance Envelope Tight? Feature-Only Geometry for Volume-Sampled Least Squares

author.name: Kihun Rhee

entry.summary: Establishes a Loewner envelope for the coefficient covariance of volume-sampled least squares, sharpening prior Derezinski-Warmuth results across all budgets and characterizing when the envelope is attainable via a feature-only margin. A mathematical contribution to volume sampling theory for least squares.

entry.title: Tabular Deep Learning for Algorithmic Trading: Cross-Regime Bayesian Optimisation for Equity Signal Generation

author.name: Joshua Le Grice

entry.summary: Trains five model classes on ~300 US large-cap equities with Bayesian hyperparameter optimization targeting trading performance across distinct market regimes, showing regime-robust selection improves out-of-sample signal precision and portfolio stability. Applied finance ML with regime-aware evaluation.

entry.title: Importance Scoring of Transformer Attention Heads in Learning Tabular Data

author.name: Ahmad Jad Allah, Kazi F. Akhter, Md. Kamrozzaman Bhuiyan, Manar D. Samad

entry.summary: Proposes an importance-scoring metric for transformer attention heads when learning from tabular data, demonstrating across 40 datasets that removing lowest-importance heads most often preserves performance, aiding interpretability and pruning of tabular transformers. One of the first head-level interpretability studies for tabular transformers.

entry.title: Sharp Minimax Regret for Infinite-Memory Logistic Prediction

author.name: Vaneet Aggarwal

entry.summary: Derives sharp minimax regret bounds for online logistic prediction with infinite input memory, giving a lag-resolved spectrum and matching lower bounds for exponential and polynomial envelopes via localized Bayesian mixtures and Toeplitz designs. Refined sequential prediction theory.

entry.title: SecureDrive-FL: Joint Differential Privacy and Gradient-Aware Selective Homomorphic Encryption for Federated Driver Monitoring

author.name: Baran Can G\"ul, Hanuma Siddhartha Tunuguntla, Anjana Arvind Naik, Abhishek Vijay Potekar, Nasser Jazdi, Michael Weyrich

entry.summary: SecureDrive-FL combines differential privacy with a selective homomorphic encryption scheme (GASHE) that encrypts only gradient components exceeding a DP-calibrated sensitivity threshold, for federated driver monitoring. It reportedly forms the first closed-loop DP+HE pipeline addressing both interception and poisoning threats.

entry.title: Over-The-Air Extreme Learning Machines with Nonlinear Stacked Intelligent Metasurfaces

author.name: Kyriakos Stylianopoulos, Mattia Fabiani, Giulia Torcolacci, Davide Dardari, George C. Alexandropoulos

entry.summary: The paper demonstrates an extremely large MIMO receiver operating as an over-the-air extreme learning machine, using cascaded metasurfaces with nonlinear response as activation functions and tunable layers as physical weights. This performs binary classification directly on wirelessly transferred signals with a single RF chain.
