entry.summary: Tests whether decodable empathy directions in instruction-tuned LLMs act as causal levers, finding that while both EPITOME-derived facets remain decodable and steering rewrites text, automated empathy metric shifts are at most partial, disentangling decodability, metric control, and human-perceived change. A cautionary result for steering-based interventions. Relevant to interpretability claims about linear directions.

entry.title: HCC+: Hyperbolic Guarding for Certified Attention Retrieval

author.name: Liangchen Ge

entry.summary: Introduces HCC+, a theoretical framework giving deterministic guarantees on attention retrieval in hyperbolic spaces by exploiting properties of the Poincare ball, bounding per-layer attention deviation and total variation decay under finite-precision representations. Addresses Lipschitz stability of hyperbolic attention. Theory-forward contribution to geometric deep learning.

entry.title: Behind the [MASK]: Disentangling Representation and Faithfulness in DAPF-Based Dementia Detection

author.name: Pardis Ranjbar-Noiey, Natalie Parde

entry.summary: Analyzes the interpretability of prompt-based domain-adaptive fine-tuning (DAPF) for dementia detection from spoken language, finding the best-performing model had the most recoverable diagnosis representation yet token-level attributions reflected language features rather than clinically meaningful evidence. A representational-versus-faithfulness dissociation in a clinical model. Cautionary for clinical deployment.

entry.title: WAVE: Reversing the Guidance Hierarchy for Coarse-to-Fine Guided Depth Super-Resolution

author.name: Tayyab Nasir, Daochang Liu, Ajmal Mian

entry.summary: Introduces WAVE for guided depth super-resolution, reversing the conventional fine-to-coarse guidance hierarchy via multi-level discrete wavelet transforms so low-level spatial cues are consumed late, with an interpretable feature-control mechanism to preserve depth boundaries. A focused computer vision architecture contribution. Solid but within a specialized task.

entry.title: CRAMER: Control via Request-Aware Masking for Editing Recommenders

author.name: Zhiyuan Julian Su, Naihe Feng, Zhen Luther Qin, Ga Wu

entry.summary: Presents CRAMER, a framework letting natural-language user requests immediately modify sequential recommendation model behavior via request-aware masking, inspired by model editing and avoiding backbone retraining or LLM inference overhead. Improves responsiveness of large-scale recommenders to timely user intent. Practical recommendation control contribution.

entry.title: AERIS: Offline Policy Improvement for Multi-UAV Integrated Sensing and Communication

author.name: Ziyuan Wang (Steven), Yifan Sui (Steven), Wei Wei (Steven), Wenjie Xin (Steven), Zekai Zhang (Steven), Xiangwang Hou (Steven), Xiao-Ping (Steven), Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes AERIS, an offline policy improvement framework for multi-UAV integrated sensing and communication in 6G, learning from fixed flight logs under centralized training and decentralized execution to balance communication quality, sensing reliability, and flight safety without risky online trial-and-error. Addresses a practical constraint of real UAV deployment. Competent domain RL contribution.

entry.title: A Multi-View Coupled Tensor Decomposition for Lightweight Online Adaptive Traffic Prediction

author.name: Quan Yu, Jie Ni, Yu-Hong Dai, Xiongjun Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes MVCTD, a coupled tensor decomposition model for online traffic prediction that jointly models shared spatial structure and view-specific temporal dynamics across speed, flow, and occupancy views, with group sparse regularization to handle missing data and anomalies. Targets practical intelligent transportation settings with imperfect sensing.

entry.title: Unsupervised Anatomical Feature Learning via Diffusion Models: Enhanced Medical Image Segmentation with Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models

author.name: Akshat G, Divyansh Gupta, Shaleen Bhatnagar, Shilpa Ankalaki, Tusar Kanti Mishra

entry.summary: Uses a DDPM trained on 21 unlabeled abdominal CT scans to learn anatomical representations, transferring the encoder to BTCV multi-organ segmentation and improving liver Dice from 0.75 to 0.93. Demonstrates unsupervised diffusion pretraining as an alternative to scarce pixel-level medical annotations.

entry.title: SAMpLE: A SystemC-AMS Machine LEarning-based Framework for Virtual Prototyping

author.name: Andrei Mihai Albu, Sara Vinco

entry.summary: SAMpLE is an open-source SystemC-AMS framework integrating ML models as first-class Timed Dataflow components via a standardized plug-and-play interface, with native C++ online-training and offline execution backends. Brings reuse, comparability, and reproducibility to ML in embedded virtual prototyping.

entry.title: VietAIDetector: An Open-Source Zero-Shot Detector for Vietnamese AI-Generated Text

author.name: Trieu Hai Nguyen, Van-Dung Hoang

entry.summary: VietAIDetector is an open-source zero-shot tool for detecting Vietnamese AI-generated text, built on Binoculars-style methods with a Gradio interface handling raw text, scanned documents, and long inputs beyond LLM context. Requires no domain-specific training data.

entry.title: A Dual-Transformer for Multi-Camera View Recommendation

author.name: Josep Cabacas-Maso, Carles Ventura, Ismael Benito-Altamirano

entry.summary: A Dual-Transformer with cross-attention decouples temporal encoding of past frames from candidate camera-view querying for multicamera editing, claiming large SOTA gains on the TVMCE dataset. The design lets each candidate camera independently interrogate a memory of recent history. Relevant to automated media production workflows.

entry.title: EgoNav: Bridging Learned Waypoints and Geometry-Aware Local Control for Robust Indoor Navigation

author.name: Jing Wang, Shiqi Zhao, Hairong Qu, Peng Yin

entry.summary: EgoNav is a hierarchical indoor navigation system that combines learned image-goal waypoint prediction with a geometry-aware local controller that enforces collision avoidance. It bridges the common gap where waypoint predictors produce geometrically infeasible targets in topological-map navigation.

entry.title: PRISM: Projection-Integrated Sampling-Based MPC with Bayesian Cost Tuning for Bimanual Manipulation

author.name: Alinjar Dan, Iryna Hurova, Karl Kruusam\"ae, Arun Kumar Singh

entry.summary: PRISM is a GPU-accelerated sampling-based MPC framework for bimanual manipulation that uses a physics simulator as an online world model. Its key contribution is a QP-guided control sampling strategy that projects sampled trajectories onto kinematically feasible sets, decoupling exploration from feasibility.

entry.title: Trust-Aware Sequential Decision Making and Rollout Planning for Resilient Multi-Robot Systems

author.name: Roee M. Francos, Daniel Garces, Orhan Eren Akg\"un, Nathaniel D. Bastian, Stephanie Gil

entry.summary: Studies multi-robot routing under localization spoofing, introducing a distance-constrained spoofing model for monitor-aware adversaries and a trust-aware monitor combining probabilistic localization trust calibrated with real GPS spoofing data plus behavioral evidence. Provides resilient sequential decision-making and rollout planning.

entry.title: A General Framework for Metropolis-Adjusted Dikin Walks: Dimension-Square Mixing on Polytopes and Log-Det Walks on Spectrahedra

author.name: Zhao Song, Lichen Zhang

entry.summary: Analyzes Metropolis-adjusted Dikin walks, proving warm-start mixing bounds for the regularized Lee-Sidford walk on polytopes and a log-det walk on spectrahedra, with a shared acceptance-to-mixing reduction. Provides dimension-square mixing guarantees for exact-metric Markov chain Monte Carlo on constrained domains.

entry.title: How researchers adapted Dolma for better Thai language models

author.name: Unknown

entry.summary: Thai researchers adapted Ai2's open Dolma data toolkit to build Mangosteen, a 47-billion-token Thai corpus that filters low-quality web data while maintaining or improving model performance and strengthening Thai cultural knowledge. Demonstrates effective open-source data curation for a lower-resource language.

entry.title: Skeleton-based Zero-Shot Spatio-Temporal Action Localization via Weakly-Supervised Pretraining

author.name: Koshiro Nagano, Fumiaki Sato, Ryo Hachiuma, Kazuki Tsutsukawa, Taiki Sekii

entry.summary: This paper proposes weakly-supervised vision-language pretraining for skeleton-based zero-shot spatio-temporal action localization, switching pooling kernels from video-level alignment during pretraining to instance-level features at inference without target-action training. It includes a scene-mixed data strategy to reduce annotation cost. Niche but well-motivated zero-shot extension of action localization.

entry.title: Ethical LLM-Assisted Research: A Framework for Responsible Delegation, Verification, and Epistemic Value

author.name: Kalin Stoyanov

entry.summary: This paper develops a normative framework for responsible delegation of scientific reasoning to LLMs, treating science as a distributed process where contribution origin may be human or machine while responsibility for acceptance into the record remains human. It specifies conditions under which delegated reasoning preserves epistemic legitimacy and accountable authorship.

entry.title: Maia 200: A Software Defined Dataflow System for Large-scale AI Acceleration

author.name: Sherry Xu, Marco Heddes, Jackson Peng, Tom Savell, Monica Tang, Prashant Ranjan, Jesse Benson, Ofer Dekel, Saurabh Dighe, Anupama Kurpad, Artour Levin, Matthew Mattina, George Petre, Cheng Tang, Yuan Yu, Li Zhang, Torsten Hoefler

entry.summary: We covered the Maia 200 paper in Research yesterday, Maia 200 is a Microsoft AI accelerator delivering 10,145 Tflop/s FP4 and 5,072 Tflop/s FP8 in a 750W envelope with 7 TB/s HBM bandwidth, exemplifying Software Defined Locally Accessed Dataflow architecture that programs dataflow engines around specialized memories and a Flynn-inspired data management taxonomy.

entry.title: LAION-BVD: A 10-Million-Hour Open Video Dataset for Multimodal Pre-training

author.name: Andreas Hochlehnert, Marianna Nezhurina, Mehdi Cherti, Andrej Radonjic, Thadd\"aus Wiedemer, Christoph Schuhmann, Romain Beaumont, Wieland Brendel, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf, A. Sophia Koepke, Jenia Jitsev, Matthias Bethge

entry.summary: We covered the LAION-BVD dataset release in Research yesterday, Releases LAION-BVD, a large open video dataset of 80M videos totaling 10 million hours, built for multimodal pre-training across video, audio, and image modalities with synthetic captions and content-aware scene detection. Models trained on it achieve competitive video-text and audio-text benchmark performance with consistent scaling gains.

entry.title: Incorporating Cognitive Load and Knowledge Transfer for Multi-Domain Knowledge Tracing

author.name: Haotian Zhang, Shucun Wang, Jinze Wu, Liang Ding, Shuochen Liu, Zhenya Huang, Jing Sha, Shijin Wang, Qi Liu

entry.summary: This paper proposes a multi-domain knowledge tracing method incorporating cognitive load from managing learning across domains and knowledge transfer between related states, improving student knowledge-state assessment over single-domain methods. It targets realistic learning scenarios where students study multiple subjects simultaneously.

entry.title: Eating for a Sustainable Planet: Personalized Sustainable Diet Recommendation via Constraint-Aware Decision-Making Modeling

author.name: Ying Jin, Weiqing Min, Mingyu Huang, Shuqiang Jiang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a constraint-aware decision-making model for personalized sustainable diet recommendation, incorporating nutrition, affordability, cultural acceptability, and environmental impact as learnable constraints rather than user preferences, to handle inter-individual heterogeneity. It targets individual-level adoption of population-level sustainability goals.

entry.title: Implicit Q-learning-bootstrapped ant colony optimization for maritime moving-target observation scheduling with agile satellites

author.name: He Wang, Junyu Wu, Yeye Liu, Yifan Zhou, Jie Zhang, Hui Li, Yanjie Song, Liang Li

entry.summary: IQACO combines implicit Q-learning with ant colony optimization for maritime moving-target observation scheduling with agile satellites, where moving sea targets make feasible windows vary dynamically. Rather than learning a task-selection policy directly, it bootstraps the ACO with learned value estimates. It handles time-window, attitude, onboard-resource, and cloud-availability constraints jointly.

entry.title: LDAC-Net: A Learnable Multi-Lag Differencing Attention-Convolution Network for Drift-Robust Recognition with Low-Cost MOX Gas Sensors

author.name: Xin Zhang, Liangxiu Han, Yue Shi, Tam Sobeih

entry.summary: LDAC-Net is an end-to-end learnable multi-lag differencing attention-convolution network for drift-robust gas and odour recognition with low-cost MOX sensors, replacing fixed first-order temporal differencing with learnable feature enhancement.

entry.title: Same-Player Verification for Account Consistency in Counter-Strike 2

author.name: Xuchen Zhang

entry.summary: Formulates same-player verification in Counter-Strike 2 as behavioral fingerprint matching: encoding a player's trajectory in a match replay and judging whether two observations come from the same real player, to support account-integrity review for boosting and smurfing. Novel application formulation for competitive gaming integrity. Focused niche contribution.

entry.title: Multi-View Trust Evaluation for Collaborator Selection via Evidential Deep Learning

author.name: Botao Zhu, Xianbin Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a multi-view evidential learning method for trust evaluation in collaborator selection, modeling heterogeneous, multi-source trust data per task and device view with evidential uncertainty. Addresses accurate trustworthiness inference in distributed systems. Companion work to a related trust paper in this batch.

entry.title: Choose Your Game Wisely: Measuring Game-Theoretic Structures in Real-World Vehicle Interactions

author.name: Yueyuan Li, Rongcheng Nie, Weijie Xi, Mingyang Jiang, Songan Zhang, Hanyang Zhuang, Ming Yang

entry.summary: Develops a trajectory-based framework to measure whether real-world vehicle interactions follow simultaneous, sequential, or asymmetric game-theoretic structures, quantifying behavioral change onset, response dynamics, and ordering stability across six trajectory datasets including INTERACTION, highD, inD, and rounD. Provides empirical grounding for interaction modeling assumptions.

entry.title: Schr\"odinger Bridges over Kinetic Swarming Models

author.name: Asmaa Eldesoukey, Md Zulfiqur Haider, Italo Napolitano, Yongxin Chen, Abhishek Halder

entry.summary: Formulates finite-horizon minimum-energy collective steering of stochastic inertial swarms as Schrodinger bridge problems over mean-field Cucker-Smale and Morse interaction models, connecting bridge methods to bio-inspired swarm control for applications like targeted therapy and evacuation.

entry.title: Characterizing Full Nonequilibrium Dynamics of Simple Exclusion Processes

author.name: Zhimao Liu, Jing Liu, Pan Zhang, Ying Tang

entry.summary: Uses variational autoregressive networks to characterize full nonequilibrium dynamics of simple exclusion processes (SSEP, ASEP, TASEP) in one to three dimensions, reproducing known finite-time results and extending to previously intractable cases including 3D finite-time analysis. Demonstrates neural variational methods on a classic statistical physics challenge.

entry.title: Auditing the Synthetic Memoir: Measuring Scene-Level Confabulation in LLM-Generated Autobiography Against the Documented Record of the Life It Describes

author.name: Heather Renze

entry.summary: A scene-level case-study audit quantifies how much of an LLM-generated autobiography is confabulated, checking 366 first-person entries against a ground-truth corpus of the subject's own life using a fixed rubric. It is presented as the first quantified audit of LLM-generated memoir against documented records.

entry.title: Evolutionary Recurrent Decision Model in Developing Adaptive and Maladaptive Behaviors

author.name: Andrew Hu

entry.summary: ERDM is a reinforcement learning framework simulating agents in evolutionarily recurrent environments to examine how evolutionary mismatch, bounded rationality, and satisficing produce adaptive and maladaptive behaviors like learned helplessness and aggression. A validity study under varying adverse childhood experience conditions shows such strategies emerge without hardwiring.

entry.title: A Behavior-Guided Online Probabilistic Forecasting Method for Electric vehicle Charging Loads

author.name: Chenghan Li, Qingxiang Liu, Yinliang Xu, Yuxuan Liang

entry.summary: This paper proposes a behavior-guided online probabilistic forecasting framework for EV charging loads, using a dual-timescale behavior representation to separate persistent station-specific charging patterns from recent behavioral changes. The behavioral signals then modulate online forecasting under evolving operating conditions. It targets a concrete smart-grid forecasting need.

entry.title: Revelation Control

author.name: Qinyou Wang

entry.summary: Introduces Revelation Control, a decision-theoretic framework for choosing priced interventions that reveal hidden state only when the revealed distinctions can change a downstream decision. It defines decision-sufficient revelation and revelation depth and derives a cost-adjusted factorization criterion for learning systems.

entry.title: QML for Quantum Sensing under Measurement-Induced Information Loss

author.name: Sounak Bhowmik, Himanshu Thapliyal

entry.summary: Frames magnetic-field estimation in NV-center diamond magnetometry as supervised regression and compares quantum machine learning models under NISQ-era noise, finite shots, and measurement-induced information loss. It evaluates which QML approaches improve parameter estimation from limited sensing data.

entry.title: Markerless Pose Estimation for Resistance Training Technique Assessment

author.name: Joseph Turner, Jeff Clark, Nawid Keshtmand

entry.summary: Applies markerless pose estimation with BlazePose to resistance training technique assessment, converting joint-angle trajectories from squat, bench press, and deadlift videos into quantitative error measures against reference repetitions.

entry.title: Multimodal Injury Risk Prediction in Tennis

author.name: Francisco Erramuspe Alvarez, Shobharani Polasa, Weihao Qu, Jay Wang, Ling Zheng

entry.summary: PART is a multimodal framework for tennis player performance and injury risk prediction, integrating wearable and alternative data sources where prior tennis-specific work is sparse.

entry.title: Quantum-Inspired Modeling of Driving Behavior

author.name: Mohammad Elayan, Omid Armantalab, Wissam Kontar

entry.summary: Introduces a quantum-inspired representation of driver behavior in which each driver is encoded as an evolving density matrix capturing behavioral uncertainty, temporal evolution, and learned interactions among behavioral variables. Aims to reconcile flexibility with interpretability in heterogeneous driving behavior modeling. Novel framing for transportation modeling.

entry.title: PA-CoT: Profile-Adaptive Chain-of-Thought for Personalized Nutritional Consulting

author.name: Evgenii Garmashov, Nikita Kulin, Artur Khairullin, Viktor Zhuravlev, Daniil Sukhorukov, Mikhail Mozikov, Ilya Makarov, Sergey Muravyov

entry.summary: Proposes PA-CoT, a multi-stage prompting method treating user-profile interpretation as an explicit standalone reasoning step for personalized nutritional consulting, plus the QPA benchmark of 200 samples scored on four criteria, compared against 11 prompting baselines. Addresses the structural gap of unstructured profile passing in health prompting. Modest but well-structured contribution.

entry.title: BanglaMamba: Exploring State Space Models for Bangla Fake News Detection

author.name: M. K. Khalidi Siam

entry.summary: Explores Mamba-based state space models for Bangla fake news detection, comparing BanglaMamba against pretrained BanglaBERT and a from-scratch BERT, with BanglaBERT achieving the highest Macro-F1 (0.9260). A low-resource-language efficiency study where the SSM alternative does not beat the transformer. Honest negative-leaning result.

entry.title: TrustFormer: Cross-Temporal and Cross- Dimensional Transformer for Task-Specific Multi-Dimensional Trust Evaluation

author.name: Botao Zhu, Xianbin Wang

entry.summary: Proposes TrustFormer, a task-specific transformer for multi-dimensional trust evaluation handling asynchronous trust data across dimensions and their intra- and inter-dimensional dependencies. Moves beyond scalar trust representations in dynamic collaborative systems. Same authors as the evidential trust paper, indicating a focused research program.

entry.title: Energy Yield and Lifetime Climate Classification via Machine Learning for Optimizing Photovoltaic Module Design and Materials

author.name: Youri Blom, Sofia Dutto, Alexandru Costache, Rowan Richie, Ruben Pelsser, Wesley Berger, Jing Sun, Rudi Santbergen, Olindo Isabella, Malte Ruben Vogt

entry.summary: Develops a PV-specific climate classification framework using ML that incorporates energy yield and, for the first time, module lifetime with climate-dependent degradation, using an interpolated dataset of twelve input features and two targets. Supports geographically tailored photovoltaic module design and materials selection. Solid applied sustainability contribution.

entry.title: Opportunities of Self Supervised Learning for GNSS: Evaluation of a Deep Learning-Enhanced PVT Algorithm

author.name: Thomas Barbero, Bertrand Ekambi

entry.summary: Applies deep learning to GNSS positioning by jointly predicting range corrections and uncertainty, with a JEPA-based self-supervised pretraining stage on unlabeled GNSS data. Evaluated on driving scenarios, it improves positioning accuracy in harsh urban multipath conditions.

entry.title: DESCENT: Directed Edge Scene Encoding for Airport Surface Movement Prediction

author.name: Alexander Prutsch, David Schinagl, Horst Possegger

entry.summary: DESCENT is a transformer-based architecture for airport surface movement prediction, featuring Potential Reachable Set context sampling and a detection-transformer decoder to handle heterogeneous dynamics and strict topological constraints. It extends motion forecasting, well studied in autonomous driving, to an underexplored aviation domain.

entry.title: PARAssist: A Framework for Personalized and Adaptive Robotic Assistance from Ambiguous User Requests

author.name: Pourya Aliasghari, Goldie Nejat

entry.summary: PARAssist is a service-robot architecture that disambiguates ambiguous user requests in a personalized way, using vision-language models to assess task demands and passively learning user preferences by contrasting tasks users perform independently versus request help with. Generates task candidates from user history for context-aware assistance.

entry.title: PhaseShift: Topology-Aware Data Harmonization and Model Consolidation Across Signalized Intersections

author.name: Yash Ranjan, Artur Kumik, Rahul Sengupta, Anand Rangarajan, Sanjay Ranka

entry.summary: PhaseShift harmonizes heterogeneous roadside trajectories across signalized intersections into a shared actor-centric representation to train one reusable traffic-behavior backbone, supporting pooled operation, zero-shot transfer to held-out intersections, and low-data adaptation. Evaluated on five intersections in two Florida regions.

entry.title: Learning the Kohn-Sham map with neural operators for quasi-linear scaling density functional theory

author.name: Danish Khan, Maurice D. Hanisch, Nikolai Argatoff, Evan Xie, Sandeep Sharma, Anima Anandkumar

entry.summary: We covered the full Kohn-Sham neural operators paper in Research yesterday, Identifies the Kohn-Sham map, from potential to density, as the right learning target for orbital-free DFT, using neural operators to achieve quasi-linear scaling electronic structure calculations. This avoids ill-conditioned kinetic-energy functional learning and poor extrapolation of direct ground-state prediction.

entry.title: Constrained Hyperparameter Optimization for Streaming Data

author.name: Bruno Veloso, Jo\~ao Gama

entry.summary: Addresses hyperparameter optimization for streaming data with boundary constraint-handling techniques so that self-adjusting online optimization operators do not propose invalid solutions in bounded search spaces.

entry.title: Lowering the Barrier to AI-Driven Inspection: A No-Code Workflow for Automated Structural Defect Detection

author.name: Michael Holm, Tanner McElroy, Xinghang Zhang, Guang Lin

entry.summary: Presents a no-code workflow enabling non-experts to build automated structural defect detection pipelines for structural health monitoring, lowering adoption barriers that limit CV use in SHM. Engineering-deployment contribution rather than a new method. Practical for condition-based maintenance.

entry.title: Simulating Cognitive Smart Freight Corridors with Agent-Based Models and Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Madelaine Martinez-Ferguson, Chun Wang, Mustafa Can Camur, Xueping Li

entry.summary: Presents an agent-based modeling framework for smart freight corridors coupling physical infrastructure, V2X connectivity, and a decision layer with RL and MARL for platoon formation and charging coordination, evaluated across three scenarios on throughput, congestion, energy, emissions, and robustness. Preliminary results favor the cognitive scenario. Simulation-stage transportation research.

entry.title: Low-Resolution Perception for Robotic Packing

author.name: Giuseppe Fabio Preziosa, Federico Vignoni, Chiara Castellano, Marco Faroni, Andrea Maria Zanchettin, Paolo Rocco

entry.summary: This work shows that low-cost, low-resolution depth sensing is a practical option for robotic packing by jointly selecting next-best views and deciding when to grasp via reconstruction cues and grasp-evidence stability estimates. Validated through ablations and end-to-end experiments.

entry.title: When Obstacles Bend: Modeling Vegetation Deformation in the context of Field Robotics

author.name: Muhammad Hsaeeb Zaar Khizar, Tom Montagnon, Roland Lenain, Romuald Aufr\`ere, Johann Laconte

entry.summary: Proposes characterizing vegetation deformation properties directly rather than from a robot-centric traversability perspective, so assessments transfer across platforms in field robotics. Models how obstacles bend when contacted by robots in natural environments.

entry.title: A Mathematical Theory of Interpretation: Rational Entropy, Spectral Readout, and Confusability as a Resource

author.name: Blake Reynolds

entry.summary: Presents an abridged mathematical theory treating interpretation as observer-relative spectral measurement under an access structure, introducing Rational Entropy and results on confusability and unique utility maxima. It frames interpretation as a method-design problem determined by access, query, utility, and medium.

entry.title: Geometry-Constrained Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks: Learning Edge Geometry via Banach Duality

author.name: K S Sesh Kumar

entry.summary: Applies a Random Forest classifier and computer-vision-based waste sorting to quantify the relationship between household waste disposal practices and illness patterns in Kumasi, Ghana, extending a 2022 descriptive field study. Provides quantitative validation of a public-health association in a low-resource setting. Applied, community-focused work.

entry.title: Forecasting Weather-Driven Price Dynamics Across Sri Lankan Tea Market Catalogues

author.name: Hesandi Mallawarachchi, Senilka Madurapperumage, Nadil Kulathunge, Thilokya Angeesa, Nethsith Gunaweera, Sandeepa Weerasekara, Patalee Narasinghe, Nisansa de Silva, Sandareka Wickramanayake

entry.summary: Builds a structured dataset from 105 weekly Colombo Tea Auction broker reports (late 2023 to 2026) plus region-specific weather data and applies Granger causality and tree-based models to forecast weather-driven price dynamics across four tea catalogues. A solid domain-specific data contribution for agricultural economics. Applied forecasting study.

entry.title: A Primer on Computational Semantics for Artificial Intelligence Systems

author.name: Casey Kennington

entry.summary: A primer on computational semantics for AI systems covering formal, grounded, and distributional semantics and comparing transformer LMs with human language learning. Aimed at building informed understanding of meaning representation in modern models.

entry.title: AGRO-Nav: Autonomous Graph-based Orchard Navigation

author.name: Ho Young Yun, Jaemin Yu, Duksu Kim

entry.summary: AGRO-Nav builds a sparse topological graph from SLAM trunk clusters for autonomous orchard navigation, using Dijkstra plus Theta* and B-spline smoothing without manual waypoints. Real-orchard trials show accurate row-center following in semi-structured agricultural environments.

entry.title: Announcing the MATS Residency: A New Path for Experienced Researchers Working on AI Safety, or Moving Into it

author.name: Raj Thimmiah

entry.summary: Announces the MATS Residency, a 6-24 month program for experienced researchers pursuing sustained AI safety research agendas, citing 630+ accelerated researchers, 215+ papers, and organizations founded including Apollo Research. Program announcement with application dates for the 2027 winter intake.

entry.title: Gating Before Commitment: Anticipating Intent Divergence to Prevent Post-Interaction Decision Failures in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Cong Xu, Ravi Sankar

entry.summary: Presents a language-guided intent module that computes an intent-geometry divergence score to gate planned driving maneuvers before commitment, preventing post-interaction planning failures. Evaluated on a handful of replayed clips with disclosed implementation and calibration analysis.

entry.title: [Macroagents] 1. The Macroagent Ontology

author.name: Towards_Keeperhood

entry.summary: Introduces a macroagent ontology abstracting over teams, companies, AI scaffolds, countries, and markets as optimization processes with agentic subsystems, intended as groundwork for design lenses to improve alignment and epistemics of human systems and AI societies. First post in a conceptual mini-sequence.

entry.title: AI safety through the lens of uncertainty quantification (UQ).

author.name: arradiat

entry.summary: A PhD student in Bayesian deep learning observes that mainstream AI safety literature largely ignores uncertainty quantification and proposes UQ as a lens on AI safety. Reflective commentary connecting two research communities.

entry.title: Do LLMs Understand Limit Order Book Dynamics?

author.name: Junxiao Chen, Paul Glasserman

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.23706v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: A large language model (LLM) trained on synthetic limit order book (LOB) data achieves near perfect scores in generating valid sequences of LOB events....

entry.title: A Formal Methodological Framework for Auditing Robustness and Fidelity in Explainable AI: From Application to Trust Certification

author.name: Rosa Elysabeth Ralinirina, Jean Christian Ralaivao, Niaiko Micha\"el Ralaivao, Alain Josu\'e Ratovondrahona, Thomas Mahatody

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.23817v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: SHAP and LIME are now standard tools for interpreting black-box predictions, yet their outputs can vary substantially when the input is perturbed by sm...

entry.title: Reinforcement Learning-Guided Evolutionary Policy Optimization for Preference-Adjustable Heterogeneous Agile Earth Observation Satellite Scheduling

author.name: He Wang, Junyu Wu, Hui Li, Yanjie Song, Witold Pedrycz, Liang Li

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.24470v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Heterogeneous agile Earth observation satellite (AEOS) scheduling requires task selection, satellite assignment, and observation sequencing under satel...

entry.title: Pivot-and-Station Multi-Agent Path Finding: Solvability, Complexity, and Algorithms

author.name: Andrea Di Nezza, Mihir Patel, Fabio Fagnani, Sara Bernardini

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.24585v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Automated high-density storage systems (warehouses, robotic parking, plant logistics, etc.) require fleets of agents to move through scarce task-critic...

entry.title: A Dual-Dimensional LLM Framework for Automated Item Incidental Content Similarity Analysis in Large-Scale Assessments

author.name: Jing Huang, Jihong Zhang, Hua-Hua Chang

entry.summary: arXiv:2608.24825v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The rapid expansion of large-scale assessments and the growing adoption of automatic item generation have intensified concerns about incidental content...

entry.title: Feedback That Backfires: Why Small Language Model Agents Repeat the Call They Just Watched Fail

entry.title: Developing frames

author.name: Richard_Ngo

entry.summary: Richard Ngo publishes a previously unreleased 2023 essay from his meta-rationality sequence exploring how frames are structured and how that affects learning and improvement, connecting to the frame problem in AI and philosophy. Conceptual epistemology writing with a note that his current thinking has moved on.

entry.title: Against Modesty’s Bailey

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: Zvi argues against modesty arguments that defer wholesale to expert consensus, contending that a smart informed person sincerely asserting X can cease to be evidence for X once social pressures and information cascades are considered. Epistemics essay engaging with Yudkowsky-adjacent discussion.

entry.title: LLMs are Adaptation-Executers, not Understanding-Maximizers

author.name: olehif

entry.summary: Argues LLMs resemble biological adaptation-executers more than understanding-maximizers, using a cellular analogy where emergent behavior arises from many small learned conditionals rather than built structure. Speculative conceptual framing of LLM cognition.

entry.title: The central fallacy: the second-worst argument in the world

author.name: Connor Williams

entry.summary: A philosophy essay proposing a second-worst argument in the world — the central fallacy — as a complement to Scott Alexander's category-based worst argument, analyzing how discourse misuses central versus noncentral category members. Intellectual commentary rather than empirical research.

entry.title: My MATS 11.0 Application Experience

author.name: Evan Conway

entry.summary: A first-person account of applying to the MATS AI safety fellowship and being accepted into the OpenAI safety team stream, with advice for future applicants. Community advice post rather than research.

entry.title: "So You Don't Trust Me?"

author.name: Zack_M_Davis

entry.summary: An essay analyzing the logic of the phrase so you don't trust me, arguing that trustworthiness must be communicated via statements a dishonest person could not equally make, illustrated through a Rand passage. Philosophical commentary.
